records.script: Robots are dumb. However, with great teachers and programmers, we can train them to be exceptional. The winners rammed knowledge into their robot to create a sophisticated autonomous system.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team sped through a three-week build. Consisting of all rookie students, they found a way to catapult themselves forward.

This team’s process-oriented approach starts with prioritization and strategy, including a structured and creative approach to fundraising. Their business plan is solid and supports their team’s technical goals. They also help other FIRST teams by providing a striking fundraising guide. It’s storming in Warren.

This team has a thorough process for identifying specific issues and designing solutions that translate to better performance. Among these successes are much improved shooting accuracy, quicker ball input, better swerve speed without wheelies, and improved bearing design. Everyone raves about this team!

When it comes to humility and working together, this team rose above the rest. Establishing a funding mechanism that seeded a fresh start for a neighboring FIRST family, this team of kind but creepy crawlers will never say ‘bug off’ to a group that asks for help. Countless teams acknowledged the help they offered throughout the competition, and it’s clear back home their program is open and welcoming to all.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Consistency was key for this team, who infused the feeling of their home into every detail of their image. From safety signage with a western flair to a machine subtly modeled after an oil derrick, when you step into this handcrafted ranch-style pit, you might think you’ve been transported to Oklahoma.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team considered all design elements to the core. Their rock-solid designs and choice of materials lead to victory on the field. The design process and result are truly industrial class.
Whether swerving, climbing or shooting, this team can control it all. They fused manual and autonomous actions to meet all the game’s challenges. You can even github their code online.

This team demonstrated significant accomplishments across all six award categories. They describe themselves as “family”, acted and dressed professionally, and presented plenty of visuals and folders documenting their significant accomplishments. School year 2021-22 highlights included 62 outreach events, almost 3,000 volunteer hours, and over 200 STEM kits sold or donated to keep individuals and teams engaged in robotics during the COVID pandemic.
This team understands what it takes to soar. With their component choices, continuous improvements, and clearly laid out electronics, the sky is the limit.

The most commendable FIRST teams change not only themselves, but the world around them. This team’s demonstration of sustainability is clear with the pipeline that they have created and their adherence to a documented initiative assessment and implementation process. They have disrupted the educational norms in and around their community and are helping to grow these initiatives internationally. In the year of COVID alone, they started 14 teams from, FLL JR all the way through FRC. Moreover, they took proactive efforts to improve inclusivity in these teams, and within their community. To change their community, and their world, they execute on superhero initiatives in education, the environment, and healthcare. The results from their transformational engineering are felt and realized by real, everyday people. We believe that everyone should join the ROAR.
The time has come to recognize this team for their engineering prowess. Their kind hearts and hard work put the gears in motion to provide neuro diversity tools to keep their community ticking.

This team’s members were passionate and eager to share what they love about FIRST and their teammates. Embodying FIRST ideals, they were quick to give specific shout-outs to other teams who have provided help to them this week. Based on what they learned in their first regionals, they have definite ideas now on upgrades they'd like to make for next year and continue on with their fund-raising successes. They started up an amazing 8 teams in their first year to ensure a pipeline of students funneling into the high school program. Their retro art design creatively combines their school theme with robotics and could grow into an outstanding theme in future years.
This rookie team has come crashing into FIRST with stubborn tenacity. They may not have the biggest team, but we bet you a buck they climb their way to the leader’s board in no time.

The level of passion, enthusiasm, and sense of inclusion exhibited by this team was central to their every interaction. From teaching a fellow team the Boot Scoot Boogie, to bubbling over with excitement when talking about their team, to leveraging the power of social media to strengthening partnerships across the larger FIRST community. The Wolf Pack howls above the rest.

records.eventName: Arkansas Regional presented by Harding University and Searcy A & P
records.script: Their alliance consistently blows up the score before the other teams even get off the ground. Are they a bomber or a drone, we don’t really know. Whatever you call them, everyone known their early scoring is automatic.

records.eventName: Arkansas Regional presented by Harding University and Searcy A & P
records.script: In a game based on sniping, this team is able to bomb from deep. They are also sharp-shooters from close range and consistently traverse to the peak when climbing. They bust the competition and are afraid of no other bots.

records.eventName: Arkansas Regional presented by Harding University and Searcy A & P
records.script: Exemplifying the principles of the FIRST core values through their support of the FIRST community, this team provides support for many. There are teams this weekend that would not be able to compete without their assistance. Upcycling is all the rage these days, and this team has been doing it for years.

records.eventName: Arkansas Regional presented by Harding University and Searcy A & P
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Lights, cameras, robots! The integration of these features provides drivers the clarity needed to see the proximity to their goals. Their elegant, yet simple, design allowed this team to climb the summit of FIRST.

records.eventName: Arkansas Regional presented by Harding University and Searcy A & P
records.script: This team clearly has experience with CNC machining and fine tuning their robot. They have woven quality into every part of their machine, making their robot robust and reliable. Their parts are capable of withstanding all the stresses trying to break them away. Their climbing feature consistently springs them to the top of the event and pushes them ahead of the competition.

records.eventName: Arkansas Regional presented by Harding University and Searcy A & P
records.script: Whether tinkering with storms, driving on the STEM pathway, or wheeling toward outreach, this team exemplifies FIRST values in local and international arenas. This team is geared to grow, expanding FIRST participation by helping over 160 teams and helping to bring accreditation to STEM education in their state. Accomplishments include collaborating with the National Guard to design and manufacture face shields in response to the pandemic, hosting a six-week Lego camp every summer, and increasing the number of college-bound students from their community pursuing STEM degrees.

records.eventName: Arkansas Regional presented by Harding University and Searcy A & P
records.script: This team isn’t afraid to work to inspire others in STEM and share the mission of FIRST 365 days a year. Putting Arkansas on the map, this winner is not in denial. This team shines the STEM light and connects people from all across the world.

records.eventName: Arkansas Regional presented by Harding University and Searcy A & P
records.script: This team danced their way into the judges hearts, and lended the emcees a strong helping hand in pumping up the crowd. There’s no BOSSing this team around.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: Can you count to three, or twelve, actually, in 15 seconds? This robot sure can! The team lays out a path to the wayward cargo and the robot takes care of the rest. Keep your hands off when this robot is climbing. This robot delivers the points with a side of fries. Congratulations Team 2122, Team Tators.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This creative team has a guiding light on their robot leading their robot to score. The shooter flies around with automation to control the shooter speed and angle just before they strike. This team latches onto the rungs to climb and soar like an eagle. Congratulations Team 114, Eaglestrike!

These guys have a tight grip on their business. They were monsters, never "slacken" as they managed risks and requirements. They're "dispatchen" some serious entrepreneurial skills. Congratulations Team 1410, The Kraken.

When designing the robot from conception to production, they spread knowledge throughout the team. Every member helped evolve their ideas, using cutting-edge tools. This robot may be short and stout, but it can survive the Rapture. Congratulations Team 3200, Raptacon!

When not at a FIRST competition, you might expect to find this team hunting for dragons to slay. They graciously shared their safety bags and emailed plans for other teams to use. Whether you are a squire, a wizard or a sage, you have a place with these Knights. Congratulations Team 996, Mecha Knights!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When it comes to their robot, this team is all heart. From the team's name to their robot's, their theme carried through like a steady pulse. Their imagery is not on a "pacemaker", but definitely uses CPR. Congratulations to Team 8087, Cougar Pride Robotics.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Books could be written about this robot's appearance and function. The design and innovation of this machine flowed like magical across the field. This team is really serious about their design and made the judges purple with pride. Congratulations Team 2403, Plasma Robotics.

This team has an insatiable appetite for data. They have such good control that with one push of a button, they can send their robot out to feed itself. Watching from the stands, you can see a green blitz bolt across the field. Congratulations, Team 2083, Team Blitz.

We were very impressed by this community-based team. They run and organize camps for upper elementary students and don't "lego" of anyone who can't attend by providing scholarships. This ain't no bull. Congratulations Team 1891, Bullbots.
The blue sleek design keeps all components safe and secure. Their process is as agile as their robot. This team's quality is not built on impulse. Congratulations, Team 4418, Team IMPULSE.

In a field of all-stars, this team shown with gracious professionalism, positively impacting a large number of other FIRST teams. Through advocacy, social awareness, and strong community partnerships, they hit a home run for robotics with their achievements. Organizing multiple events that are open and free to all, and spreading the message of FIRST, this team slithered to home plate, winning the Chairman's Award. Congratulations Team 498, Cobra Commanders.

All team in FIRST change lives. This engineering inspiration team documented, in a measurable way, the impact and change they have had on their school, city, and national communities. You don't have to be "Nuts" to know that this team is a role model for others. Congratulations to the CocoNuts, Team 2486!

Even though they're a pup in this competition, they're not the runt of the litter. This fully-commited team successfully designed and implemented each element of the competition. These energetic students proved to be no underdogs. Congratulations All-Star Rookies, Team 8745, RoBeagles!

This team opens their campus to other schools. They are polite, well-spoken and have contagious joy and enthusiasm. It was a a very dicey decision, but they rolled to the top. Congratulations Team 7426, Pair of Dice!

Their design was consistent, reliable and just plain worked. Through the use of control loops, sensor fusion and good old fashioned algebra, they were able to score all the time. They are not changing the world, but they are certainly creating people and robots who will.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team sparks with creativity. Their custom 3D printed designs were a gem to look at. One thing we know for sure; if we are ever in a bind, this team will surely be our knight in shining armor.

This team truly understands what it means to create a brand while honoring their sponsors. Their inspiration makes the FIRST community glow. What did the sorting hat choose for you? The entrepreneurship award!

This excellence in engineering award team designed their robot with the big picture in mind. They knew the importance of gaining points on the traverse and started the process as soon as 20 seconds early to make sure they made it to the top. Calling themselves a “jack of all trades”, they even gained team buy-in with a signed design contract.

Gracious Professionalism is at the heart of this team, and this team’s heart is filled with a fire like no others. They consistently impressed other teams and the judges with their humility and engagement.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: You will never feel blue when you look at this team. They shine like stars! Let's Launch FIRST forward with them!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team developed several prototypes so they could continuously improve their design and reliability. This robot has a consistent targeting system, a backspin eliminators to stick their shots, and a dependable traverse climb. With their signature triangular-patterned bot, this team really tears it up on the field!
This team had their robot spit out opposing cargo automatically. Using a custom dashboard, the robot also gave their driver advanced feedback in an EPIC way.
This team reaches their claws in and out of the FIRST community. They inspire younger generations to fall in love with STEM. Let’s roar in excitement with them!

These guys showcased beautiful CAD designs in their robot documentation. Although at first glance the robot appears a bit wiggly, it can shake off the rigors of game play. This bot traveled across an ocean to showcase their reliable high shot from the base of the hub.

In a field filled with intense competition, one team takes to the sky spreading the FIRST mission. From using their engineering and robotics knowledge to mentor teams and engage with children to their analytical approach towards measuring their impact, the community flocks to this team. The judges recognize that this team has been working hard to “make it loud” while they soar to great heights.

This team is always happy to assist others. Their strategy to diversify their outreach and change minds is a force to be reckoned with. From exoskeletons to adaptive transportation, this team certainly soars when it comes to inspiring others.

The winner of this award will have their championship registration paid for by SOAR (Simoncic Opportunities for Arts and Robotics) in the event that they advance from the priority waitlist. If they don't advance from the priority waitlist SOAR will pay their registration fee for 2023 season. This blue team got their game on. They applied FIRST values and found that all that glitters was gold with their double-smash mouth style of play.

Your enthusiasm reminds us why we got into this sport in the first place. Your clear explanations about every aspect of your design showed the judges you knew how to unleash your potential. You might not like the barking parts of your meetings, but you know your stuff! We’re howling for you!

This team ventured into the center of AZ. Their spirit spreads from their school to their neighbors and even the local mercados. Spreading extraordinary enthusiasm to all, focusing on inclusion, this team is truly about the good stuff.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation

records.script: This team soared through the competition with independence and bird-like vision. They employed an iterative circle flight pattern to hunt their “prey” with consistent, pinpoint accuracy. The potential for this team’s autonomous capabilities clearly goes towards the galaxy… and beyond!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team built the most unusual climbing mechanism we saw. The judges couldn't figure out how their robot's multiple flailing arms were supposed to work until we saw it in the hangar. They were driven by enough chain to armor a medieval knight.
This team has a plan to foster STEM for students of all ages. They use technology to manage the team resources. This out-of-this-world aquatic team swam to the top at today’s event.

This gymnastic robot showed unmatched balance on the uneven bars of the hangar. The judges were impressed by their description of the stress analysis and trigonometry that went into their design. They truly engineered one climber to rule them all.

Teams usually have their hands full just driving their own robots. This team managed to drive their own, and jumped in to help out another team who did not have enough members to drive it. This dragon swooped in from its nearly cave to save a team that found themselves out in the cold.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team brightened up the pits, the stands, and other teams’ robots. Their new theme is a creative connection between park animals and water structures. They kept all their ducks in a row.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: From first sight, this team has had us turning our heads. Their modular implementation and meticulous manufacturing really made a splash. It was clear that the functional design of this robot hit the “high tide” of the season!

This award goes to a team that looked at the game from a different angle. Their blinged-out robot can find its own cargo, deliver it to the hub, and reach the top of the hangar, all at the push of a button. I pity the fool who goes up against them.

Every team had to deal with trying to develop their robots remotely this last year. This team, however, had to take it to the next level. Even though they did not even meet in person for the most part till competition, a few team members developed their robot at a public makerspace. The rest of the team members contributed via the the information highway from Chicago to LA, plus a branch in Italy. For proving that an online high school can have a robotics team, the judges award this special award to Team 4014.

To no one’s udder amazement, this machine was nearly perfect in every way. The symmetry of their machine made it possible for them to swap parts quickly without missing a beat. This was the epitome of quality on the hoof.

Colorful does not even begin to describe this Chairman’s team. From the commitment to FIRST and the community they serve, their effects reach far beyond their team’s boundaries. Whether it be creating curriculum to providing online support, this group soars above the rest.

All FIRST teams want others to jump into building robots just like they did. This team’s own robot was solid and exemplified good engineering practices. Since they know FIRST is more than robots, next they focused on upending stereotypes about who should be building a robot and drew a big fraction of their school into the team. They met younger students where they were, coming up with pint-sized robot friends.The geared-up robots in their petting zoo even survived being around gators!

If you are looking for high energy in the pits of in the stands, this is your team. If you need a battery or a translator, this is your team. If you are looking for an unstable connection, this is not your team.
This team lets the software do the hard work. Their robot is in its element as it lines itself up to take the shot. The autonomous award goes to team 5419 – Berkelium

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team embodies being “scrappy”, Highway signs and drawer slides make this robot happy. Their climber was designed to be partially passive and never tire, We are happy to congratulate these penguins from the empire.

Their business plan revolves around their mission statement, That emphasizes the gravity of student empowerment, And builds partnerships for community engagement, To ensure sustainability of their organization, They orbit in pairs to build their relations, And budget contingency for future rations. The entrepreneurship award goes to Team 4904 – Bot Provoking.

From conception to execution, this team demonstrated Excellent Engineering practices. With a strong, functional design, they forged their way to victory. The team worthy to wield the Excellence in Engineering Award is the RoboVikes.
This team’s GP can be seen throughout the pits, When emotions run high, out come the oven mitts. They are always around to help find a fix, Congratulations to team 766.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Several teams at this competition have successfully brought together multiple communities into a cohesive team. But this team had an eye to take integration to a higher power, by developing and implementing a name and logo that is the cat’s meow. Orange you glad this team won?

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team has a keen eye for design and a fastidious focus on their process. Their practical modular design stresses the importance of integration. And with their autonomous shooting algorithm we hope to see them AIM for the stars.

This team can track the Innovation in Control Award from anywhere on the field, keeping their eye on the goal at all times, the autonomous turret controller kept them on target. Award goes to team 973 Greybots.

The judges are calling this award “Apple of Our Eye”. Though small, this team’s impact was large, lending a helpful hand all across the field and pit. These “magnificent 7” exhibit the FIRST spirit that “chains” us all together.
This team focused on simple design and optimized speed and defense, without lacking in slick aesthetics. This robot zoomed around the field and could take some battering to “boot”!

They expand their reach by building alliances with other teams, and enable students across their community to have robotic dreams. Their services enable every team to be best in show, allowing these “avocados” to continue to grow. This teams eloquence really blew the judges away, they empower other to excel each and every day! Their statistics show their impact is first-rate, please join me to congratulate team sixteen seventy eight!

To recruit more girls they found you just have to ask, Reaching higher they discovered they were up to the task. Mentoring, volunteering, and working with their school board helped this team rise above the rest, These newly-minted veterans really impressed.
When this team spreads their wings, you know they’re in the building. Their presence brings a surge of energy to the stands. Not even coyotes can hold them back.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: This team’s robot consistently maneuvers to gather and shoot up to 5 balls in autonomous mode. This team of polymaths spent some personal time with their robot using over 4000 pictures of cargo, so that it could give real-time tips to its human driver during each match. Leonardo himself would be proud to give this award to The Vitruvian Bots!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s robot doesn’t weigh much, but it’s no lightweight in competition. Having a lot of freshman engineers might be a weakness for some teams, but it is no Achilles’ heel for this one. Their ball shooter resembles a dog’s ball launcher – too big for dogs but just the right size for Panthers.

Their business plan took a byte out of the competition. Even though you may think this selection is fishy, the birds appreciate their Ferris wheel, and we think for the entrepreneurship award they are the real deal!

This team's impressive engineering helped them rise to the top in the hangar AND rankings. Their robot was a white blur as it zipped around the field. Their elegant design ensured that they would never break a circuit.
This team is bodacious in how gracias they are. We all had a lot of gratitude for their positive attitude. It’s not too far to go to congratulate the team from Mexico!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team works hard to inspire others, and they do it all with style! They suited up and did MORE to create an impressive aesthetic that’s cohesive between their pit, members, and robot.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Industrial design is a key component of FIRST robots. This robot’s design mimics creatures normally seen flying through trees. This team harnessed the ability to 3D print and waterjet components to create the mighty Bandar.

This award goes to a team whose coding impressed us on and off the field. They built a system to make the process of programming autonomous as easy as point-and-click. Because it's all open source, we expect all of the other robots to include a little orange code next year.

This team built their robot and ran several impressive outreach initiatives-- all from a school hallway. With no defined build space, they had to go mobile and pack out their gear. This is definitely a high-wattage team worthy of recognition.

This team demonstrated astute decision-making and great team organization. This facilitated them in creating a robust and high-performing robot that is a pleasure to see on the field. The team optimized their design for high scoring and met this challenge with a capable autonomous system.

This year's Chairman's recipient demonstrated profound impacts to the FIRST community - locally and globally. They've started and are actively mentoring many FIRST teams, including many local FLL teams and an FRC team in India. Their thousands of volunteer hours are helping underserved people including homeless and orphans, and also initiated a website service to help local businesses stay open through the pandemic. They are inspiring the future by continuing in STEM professions and giving all team members a chance to be a team lead in their scrum rotational program. They are helping other FRC teams through sharing their Autobuilder and other public documentation. Their many contributions embody the FIRST mission.Congratulations Team Optix 3749 !!

The judges want to recognize an organized team run like a professional enterprise, which has made a focused and deep impact on their community including by creating FLL teams that feed directly to their FRC team. Their outreach goes far beyond their community though, as they have made successful efforts to train future STEM leaders around the globe. We were impressed by their dedication in deploying their large team to well-directed efforts that reach underrepresented groups in STEM, including Native American and special education students. Perhaps next will be outreach to a galaxy far, far away…

The judges want to recognize this team for their resourcefulness and perseverance. They worked on a tighter timeline and with a smaller group than most other teams while simultaneously making the transition into FIRST, but nonetheless they built a robot that they’re proud of. We look forward to seeing what these young women bring to the competition next year!
This team exhibits great enthusiasm and presence to project an integrated team. Their exceptional partnering across an entire country embodies the principles of FIRST.
How do you manage autonomous control? Well, you better KNOW how to knead your DOUGH! Their 5-ball auto always LED. The autonomous control award goes to team BREAD.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Speedy swerve drive? Smart shooter? Reliable autonomous? Consistent climb? The COLLECTIVE effort of this team developed MANY innovative solutions. Beep … Beep… Beep… that SOUND lets you know that RESISTANCE IS FUTILE.

Entrepreneurial spirt is recognizing a weakness and turning it into a STRENGTH. With a focus on INFORMATION TRANSFER, This team created detailed documentation of all team processes … Branded too! This team was on FIRE cross-training and nurturing an FTC pipeline to build strength in their BUSINESS PLAN and operations!

This team came into the competition like a WAVE OF FIRE. Their professionalism and consistency never BROKE. Their design was ADVENTUROUS, even with their backs against the wall, they NEVER seemed to reach their BREAKING point

When a last-minute call for help went out to assemble the Regional’s field, this team was one that STEPPED UP with volunteers. ALWAYS WILLING to lend a hand, when a struggling team needed help with wiring, software. and soldering, this team continued its DEEP ongoing partnership to bring that team’s robot to life.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Everything this team produces - from posters to promotional materials, documents, shirts, buttons, and their robot – builds upon the ICONIC BRAND of the organization from which it grew. Combining robots and cookies, their attractive designs AND visuals for modern times leads to ….

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This UNCOMMONLY ambidextrous bot moves smoothly through itself to make that ball DANCE! This bot’s IRON-like CONSTRUCTION may not extend to their FLEXIBLE omnidirectional multi-tool of a manipulator. BUT they sure can CLAW that cargo!
It’s really hard to plan your PATH Sensor fusion needs Kalman MATH! They use their cameras in STE-RE-O The Award goes to Team T -K -O!

This year the judges were inspired by this team with their PERSEVERANCE and ACCEPTANCE of assistance from the “Depths of Space” to produce a functional and working robot. The Judges would like to celebrate this RISING TEAM, its PROGRESS, and DETERMINATION to compete.

This team’s SEAMLESS execution starts at their pit walls and carries through their lightweight intake into the SMOOTH EDGES of their chassis. NO RIVET WAS LEFT UNCOATED in their MAD pursuit of consistency. This is the BOT to take OUT on the TOWN!

The winning team displayed excellence in all the core areas of the Chairman’s award, from middle school outreach events; to fun and creative freshman training initiatives. This team was able to “FLOCK” together multiple levels of the FIRST programs to students both domestically and internationally. Their professional presentation AND eloquent essay made the difference and will be “taxi-ing” them all the way to Championship.

This team focuses on every aspect of FIRST and have made themselves a FORCE FOR CHANGE. Engaging their ENTIRE community to support STEM, through multiple events, resulting in CONGRESSIONAL RECOGNITION. This team shows their PATRIOTISM for FIRST.....truly an inspiration!

This energetic team of cheerleaders is always learning and applying their talents. They used their knowledge of pneumatics, blowing air into a HAUNTED house helping it come alive, entertaining and motivating LOTS of youngsters – starting and mentoring several new FLL and FTC teams. Their enthusiasm inspired the judges!

Autonomy incorporates inclusivity on a robot's mechanism and code. This team elaborately incorporated a reliable, well-engineered, and excellently executed design. The robot was embedded with a custom code to map the field and interpolate its position to shoot a goal anywhere on the field. This excellent robot is one sweet orange.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The judges saw a tremendous display of creativity in the robots this season. However, these "titans" of creativity stuck out. By repurposing everyday objects to work seamlessly into their design, they were able to construct a functional, practical machine without the need for expensive equipment.

With a solid foundation in FIRST Robotics this team has stood the test of time. They are a team with strong student leadership and a comprehensive understanding of strengths, weaknesses and opportunities to foster continuous improvement. This team is an example of how cross-town rivals can join forces and demonstrate the Spirit of Entrepreneurship.

Straight out of Middle Earth, this "precious" team arrives "precisely when they mean to". This team has shown impressive engineering knowledge and analysis well beyond their years. Incorporating complex trigonometry and Finite Element Analysis, this team meticulously carried their design from cradle to grave with seamless execution. While "deeds will not be less valiant because they are unpraised", we wanted to offer praise for the Excellence in Engineering award to the one rung to rule them all: "the Lord of the Rungs!"

This team exemplified a contagious aloha spirit of professionalism. From community fundraising, organizing STEM campaigns for 4th through 8th graders, and consistently exhibiting a positive attitude on and off the field, we are proud to present the gracious professionalism award to the team with the spirit of Ohana.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When it comes to an original, visually-stunning, and attention-grabbing team, this group was a cri-CUT above the rest. The legwarmers, yoga mats, neon lights, and contagious 80s electric energy was palpable from every corner of the floor, and exemplifies is the core value of fun.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team has shown exceptional knowledge in their design approach. They are a confident team relying on basic principles and research which created a simple but robust design. The judges would like to commend this team for learning from their past experiences. Designing subsystems for modularity has allowed for easy maintenance and an industrially sound robot.

Because of their turret and vision tracking system, this team rarely misses shots into the upper hub. It is not a gamble to say that their autonomous routine is very reliable. Clearly what happened in Vegas didn't stay there.

We all count in these competitions: rich, poor, tall, short, boy or girl. This team supports each other and the community and therefore deserves the judges award. From their robotic courses to breast cancer awareness always with great excitement they represent. Please help us with a big ovation.

This quick robot had some great rapid prototyped parts. Our hares stood on end as we watched this team's machine hop from bar to bar. Their robot's vision works so well, they must be feeding it carrots.

For this team... It's about TECHNOLOGY. From mentoring FLL and FRC teams and hosting tournaments, to running annual summer camps, they do it all. It's about TEAMWORK and working with their corporate sponsors to host career and inclusion panels. It's about RESPECT and advocating for diversity groups such as Black Voices, Asian Americans, and women in STEM. For this team, it's more than robots. It's The Vitruvian Bots.

With their grit, representation and awareness, this team not only helps each other but have also designed a system so other teams can reach out. Their knowledge is transferred through generations and they have even written books for little ones. With a little sweetness they support their community, their love for robotics and STEM. Their motto describes them perfectly: "Bake a difference, one cookie at a time!"

While this Rookie team welcomed assistance from more veteran teams, they are already starting to exhibit "Chairman's-like" qualities by helping other clubs. This team recruits Young Cubs from middle schools and ensures their freshman own the mechanical elements of the robot. This rookie team "roared" to a 300% increase in participation in Year 2.

These rookies are a small yet very enthusiastic team who showed us that they are excited to be here! Aiming high to grow the ranks, this team has inspired us with their positive can-do attitude. Their robot incorporated fun design elements, rad 1980's retro materials and a strong structure that's ready to fly into the wild blue yonder. Wait! What's that I hear? It must be this pride of lions roaring down the runway for their Rookie Inspiration Award.

Members of this team regularly-and genuinely wished other teams good luck this weekend. The team captain so energized the team that they promoted her to "coach". The team's enthusiasm and outreach extend not just to middle schoolers but also to other high schoolers in the community.

This team built one of the speediest robots on the field. Its sensors and software transported it from the tarmac to the traversal rung at a breakneck pace, with record-breaking scores along the way. The judges found their gyroscopic climbing routine particularly a-peel-ing.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team didn't have expensive machine tools or computer vision like some other teams. Still, they were committed, and brought their intake and shooter together in a garage. In a sea of lower-resource teams, they stood out as kings.

This team doesn’t fear risks when it comes to facing challenges. They have fired up their business and community plan to drive their team to success. As budding entrepreneurs you can say they are lit. Congratulations team Firebots!
This team complements their approach to the design process. Their 3 ball autonomous pounds out the cargo, and this team’s ability is “poi”-tentially the best on the mainland and the North Shore!

From the dawn of time, FIRST has celebrated the values of Gracious Professionalism. More recently, this team has roared and stomped their way through children’s hospitals, farmers markets, senior centers, and feeder elementary schools to spread the core values of FIRST. Even an asteroid strike would not stop these singularly magnanimous reptiles on a roll.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Fun colors and a visible story welcomed visitors to their pit. This team embraced the focus on transportation, integrating team and game for a strong visual aesthetic. Take the train, cross the bridge, all routes taking us to our imagery award winner.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s approach to design is smart, creative, and persistent. Their documentation is as telling as a robotic oracle. Their bot with an epic turntable can do it all, just like Phineas.

This award goes to a team that we couldn't miss seeing as they floated by. However, the feedback that their robot serves-up impressed us even more than their costumes. The robot's user interface help both their driver and their programmers get right to the point.

FIRST celebrates bringing people together from near & far. They have now taken this to the “nth” degree. They broke new ground by coaching another team to run their robot when the robot could travel but they couldn’t, even updating their software from half a world away, persevering under terrible odds.
This team's robot was as immaculate as their pit. Their beautifully integrated design didn't cut any corners. They set a high water mark for other teams to aspire to.

This team doesn’t play around when it comes to STEM. Their voice is heard over the radio waves in addition through their hands to include everyone and all abilities in FIRST and STEM. This team is marching through their habitat like a cougar hunting for STEM prey.

When this team encounters obstacles, they jump at the opportunity. Having lights out in the bunk house meant it was time to saddle up and learn new skills. Whether integrating FIRST LEGO League statewide or mentoring FTC teams, they said “giddy up” to the challenge of spreading FIRST near and far.

All rookie teams have to run around and gather materials where they can. This team did an amazing job of gathering crumbs and assembling them into a very respectable robot. Congrats on making it to the top of the rookie hill, Mechanic Ants.
All rookie teams work hard to overcome many obstacles. This team showed they know to work with dinosaurs and with school districts. Clearly this team will be a titan of FIRST going forward.
A competitive team who helps other teams, their spirit is felt through both their energy and service. Sporting red, yellow, and blue, their spirit cannot be contained.

San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team is brilliant in more than one way. They closed the loop on their vision control which allowed them to outpace the competition. They robustly executed and scored with precision. The award goes to the TorBots.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: No mission was impossible for this team. They creatively designed their climber to reach the top hanger rung in a very controlled and consistent manner, comparable to that of Tom Cruise. It goes without saying that the robot's achievements are nothing less than a Top Gun Maverick.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: By harnessing the power of the sun, this team continues to propel their extensive endeavors. They utilize 3D printing, laser cutters, and CNC to create unique treasures. These treasures flow like magma in their online store, where happy customers support their STEM outreach.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team focused their creative efforts on solving multiple engineering challenges with one simple, elegant mechanism. With a single, rotating hook-bearing cage, their robot can intake cargo, shoot to the high hub, and climb. This clean, powerful design demonstrates why these roboticists are giants on the field.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Their efforts are all about giving back and helping others. This team took supporting other teams to a new depth. They made a work assignment schedule and made time to float between schools and many other teams. The award goes to the Aluminum Narwhals.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team stands out with its vibrant and colorful outlook on everything from their team’s logo to their illustrations. Incorporating everyone’s artistic contribution, their red and yellow colors formed an inclusive and cohesive brand image. The Griffin stands tall and proud in all of their marketing material.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This fine looking machine started with a logical and complete design and delivered a solid all around performance. The result was clearly several sigma above the mean! Especially when in motion!

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team spent weeks solving differential equations to automate their shooter. They then took on the troublesome vision control systems and developed a data processor to analyze which feedback was actionable. They were able to operate without hesitation and charged ahead in the competition.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This year, the Judges’ Award is for Expanding FIRST without Boundaries. Like a collection of dots assembling into a complete picture, this unique team truly came together in time and space to compete this weekend. Their virtual solutions provided tangible team benefits, for a wide ranging audience.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: High quality is a label that is applied to an entire design, yet lives in the details. This team invested the time to develop its methodology and set high standards. They created a robot that not only performs well, but also looks the part.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team continues to make a huge impact on our community, from the San Diego region to far beyond. Their outreach activities are not just voluminous but also FIRST rate. They have increased their team diversity, volunteered in multiple countries, started and mentored many, many teams, and are a big presence on social media. Lastly, their published curriculum has been used by multiple teams and STEM camps to emulate their successful plans. For their successful 8-legged approach,

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: We were blinded by their impressive body of volunteering efforts that extends beyond our shores. Their advocacy for gender diversity in STEM fields is bearing fruit. They have started and mentored numerous FLL teams, developing a curriculum and virtual workshops for robotics students, including special education classes. It’s clear to us that their inspiration is no optical illusion.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: This team started from the ground up with nothing holding them back. There was no hill they couldn’t climb, and they made their mark in the pits. An ant on the move does more than a dozing ox and that is exactly what they proved.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: Working late into the night on their robot and resting by day high above in Eucalyptus trees, this rookie team promotes diversity and inclusion in the FIRST community as part of the team’s foundation.

records.eventName: San Diego Regional presented by Qualcomm
records.script: When a group of people feel really invested in a goal they will vocally support each other. This was witnessed passionately in the stands, and also the playing field and pits. They were loud. They were cohesive. They strike like lightning, impacting all teams at the event.

This robot has a mind of its own. From a super functional autonomous period routine, to intelligent decisions calculated within milliseconds from sensor input, this team is set for success. They're turning heads, and we're doing backFLIPs for this Spartan Robot.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's creativity springs ahead while keeping their systems simple. Their passive climber was thoughtfully designed for maximum consistency and effectiveness. These teams aren't just building robots, they're building an empire.

This business-savvy team maintains community sponsorship as part of their strategy. Realizing that local businesses suffered financial hardships during the pandemic, this team "mixed it up" by adding their own fundraising to manage their season. “TEA-ing up" team sustainability and marketing excellence with sweet treats and fine drink, the entrepreneurship award goes to….TEAM 253

This team clearly explained how they took multiple designs through rigorous engineering analysis. A perfectly balanced intake quickly deploys, grabs, and retracts for safety, feeding their energy-optimized shooter. Their funky robot swings all the way to the top of this year‘s challenge.

On this team, safety training is a must, and everyone's an owner. Anyone can touch a wire, and a rookie is a top fundraiser. From their actions to their signed pledge poster, this team truly exemplifies Gracious Professionalism.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This winning team embraced this year's transportation theme and looked for ways to soar and connect the world. From a pit that draws you in, to a color-coordinated cheering squad in the stands, to well-bundled wiring on their robot, they show us a consistent image and their brand. Their heads may be in the clouds among the airplanes, but on the ground they still strike gold.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team worked hard to blend both form and function – taking the shape of a whale, while striving to keep their robot light enough to travel. Despite being a featherweight, this robot is no pushover, regularly making shots after a game-time redesign. We’re thrilled to see this team striving for the summit: give it up for Team 3880 the Tiki Techs!

When the robot is rocking and rolling, you don't want it to reach out at the wrong time. This team had a full suite of driver aids, from shooting to safety. The judges were especially impressed by this team's swerve drive controls, which gave them lightning "QUICK" reflexes on the field.

FIRST is about inspiring and being inspired – this award recognizes a team that did both. When trouble strikes and both the robot and your season are not going as planned, FIRST provides a place where you know help is ready. We are recognizing a team that came especially ready to learn. With a little Aztec and Spartan help and a positive attitude, this team got into the game and is ready to return the favor.

This team has a STEADfast dedication to quality with an intake that is designed to withstand defense. Their climber stays tuned with a serviceable tensioning system and stays locked in place until it’s ready for flight. Back at HOME, their health check software ensures all robot systems are ready for the next match.

In a building well-stocked with champions, it's a challenge to select the very finest. The winning team expanded the FIRST mission by taking a leadership role in a TV training documentary, and by creating and hosting summer workshops and qualifier competitions. Furthermore, they demonstrated leadership of the FIRST community during the COVID shutdowns by increasing their mentoring role for FLL and FTC teams, and by remotely training scouts seeking their Robotics and Programming merit badges. They make long-lasting waves by providing mobility devices to physically-challenged children, and by their successful advocacy for an increase in funding for STEM at the Congressional level. The biggest fish in this ocean of champions is Team 649 - MSET Fish!

This team did an outstanding job working with other teams to inspire the youth across their region. They work with disadvantaged students introducing them to FIRST at a very young age. They have also translated FLL, FTC, and FRC materials into multiple languages, inspiring teams in many countries. You can hear them trumpeting FIRST Core Values around the world. The Engineering Inspiration Award goes to Team 8159, Golden Horn!

Starting a team during the pandemic is ambitious, so we give kudos to all 4 rookies this season. What stood out to the judges was this team's willingness to learn - from finding off-season build space to soaking up ideas at the event like scout badges. Their planned school-wide morning announcement will celebrate this San Francisco team's bright future.

This team has dedicated themselves to spreading the word and recruiting new students from diverse populations by showcasing their program within their school and community, and promoting the FIRST mission and values. They're just getting started, but they've already proven they are a pumpkin that their community can be inspired by and proud of.

Entering the pits, the judges and undoubtedly everyone else were inevitably distracted by the singing and clapping from this team. When you venture closer and find the source, you can't help but find yourself smiling and maybe even singing along. Their enthusiasm makes it easy to join them in "Gearing Up for STEM".

Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: (In engineering, we are frequently asked to cutback, but his team refuses to do so, surging forward. Like in a Tesla, their driver could have taken a nap. A “High” mark has been set in autonomy!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Sometimes people see being creative as just spinning your wheels. Success is often littered with tough breaks. Their creative climber is by far a high bar to equal.

This team’s business plan crept into the lead with its vision, capturing our attention with its intricate details of a self-sustaining program. They were able to spin an elaborate web by combining threads of entrepreneurial spirit with enthusiasm. Even Dr. Octopus would agree that these arachnids should snare this award!

As efficient in design as the warriors of Greek mythology were in combat, their sub-teams created several modular designs to prototype and test. Daedalus’ engineering excels on the battlefield once again as a valiant member of this team.

Their veteran team graciously helps others by making parts, volunteering to take over the wheel and the sting out of their neighbor’s season. Sacrificing their build time, they changed their direction to one degree north. In the end, this king picked up the pieces to complete the circuit of life.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This well-packaged team showed MORE than the rest. They integrated their pit, robot, and their team to stand out MORE. They TORQUED the competition.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Take a magical ride on a mechanical dragon. This dragon climbs smoothly with great balance, with a little friction to help transition up. Festus smoothly glided into Ventura County Regionals with an all-girl-powered team.

These old-timers have been working on innovative control systems for over 25 years. With their custom gearbox and drive system, this team was able to maintain a robust centralized design. From “Norse” all-powerful strength, this team was able to regroup and drive in for the win.

On the field and in their community, this team has demonstrated perseverance and strength. Thirteen is their lucky number with a mantra of innovate, improve and adapt. They’re geared up to head out of the container and into the future.

It’s obvious from the outside this bot is built like a brick. Its design quality is only equaled by its execution, this bot is a thing of beauty. All other bots should be red with envy and spitting fire!!

This group of kids fly far beyond their own shores in the name of FIRST. They share robotics and STEM within their small sphere and also around the world. When the “Bug” changed all societies on Earth, they rose .to the challenge and were determined to plow forward by creating intensive safety standards that were adopted statewide. These kids are farming FIRST with a great Aloha Spirit!

This team really has heart. Operating on a community and global scale to inspire STEM for everyone through FLL mentoring, conferences, camps, and certification programs. Resistance is futile with these warriors on and off the field!

In their first FRC competition, this team exemplifies small but determined! Their ability to balance both FRC and FTC has inspired us all. These Robos may live on The Rancho, but they are destined for the stars!
This is the way, the force is strong with this team’s spirit. They cheered for blue and red alliances and there is no mystery with where this team stands. Let’s give a roar ……..

records.script: They can shoot and score from anywhere. Limelight aims and fires, and their Path Weaver makes them consistent and reliable. Their solution is more than brute force, it’s elegant.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When it comes to climbing, this team was already a natural. Their chainsaw cut through the competition. With claws like no other, they scaled to new heights.

Small but mighty, this young team took ownership of their learning. After evaluating their strengths, weaknesses opportunities and threats, they Titan-ed up their strategy. Building on their strengths they will become Titans in industry!

This team’s engineering process is both excellent and comprehensive. They developed a “STREAM” of features in drive train, shooting, and climbing. Their efforts have paddled them to the top of the engineering ranks.
The team improves themselves while sharing their field. They work hard, but are known to “SLACK” while improving communication. They make sure their CAVE is a home for all.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is clearly in good shape. Their cricket can’t chirp but it sure can print. Get ready for some exercise and clap your hands for Team 1339 AngelBotics.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team took 3D printing to a completely new level. Their turret was always trying to “SEEK” success. As they say, once a Sabercat, always a Sabercat.
Even though their bot refused to listen at FIRST; This team never lost sight of the goal while evading defenders. In a nutshell, this team’s innovation allows their bot to Go Nuts on the tarmac.
The student’s drive this incredible Team that embodies diversity and inclusion. Mental health is at the core of their success. Their comprehensive fall training program is no SMAaaaaall feet!
This team’s well thought out design sped them to the top. They proved that a robust design can be both flexible and fast. That had a climber so reliable it could scale Mt. Rushmore.

The Colorado Regional Chairman’s Team took the drought of the past few years as an opportunity to redefine their roots and grow themselves and their community. They stepped up their team outreach by providing essential products to the community; proving that FIRST really is about more than robots. The team then spread the FIRST spirit by establishing FLL Explore as part of the 3rd grade curriculum in every school in their district.

One team rose above the rest with their community outreach diversity and core values. This clan showed their true colors through their training and readiness. They inspire leadership and teamwork, while wearing their kilts with pride.
In everything they do they are enthusiastic and diverse; they are loud, they are proud. These cats can be heard all the way from the Springs. They have Gone completely Wired for FIRST.
Masters of their domain, the frequency of their 4 ball auto was very high. Slithering along auto paths, their code made it easy. They regulargly soar to the traversal bar.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team never intended to climb low. They chose to latch onto a higher bar, and pivot even higher. Other teams are green with envy watching this team climb end over end.

Your teams impact has nothing to do with your team size. One of the smaller teams here demonstrated the most impact on FIRST. This team has social media impact metrics far greater than any other team that presented. This teams volunteer impact is measured in community outreach through summer camps and Cub Scouts. This teams environmental impact is measured in how much money they make in recycling your stuff. This teams FIRST impact is measured in hosting events at all levels of FIRST They are mentoring 12 FIRST teams this season, 11 of them started this year. Where’s this team?

This team showed confidence, poise, and passion for all aspects of FIRST. Their outreach extends to all levels of competition and all rookie teams have felt their generosity. With one thousand percent of the school's support, they are deeply hard wired into the curriculum.

This team has a solid business plan that is forging its way into the future. It is developing a future full of innovators, iterators, and illustrators. This Owl-some 4H team and their makerspace are a driving force for the future.

This team's ever watchful eye created a robot that would be at home in the most advanced robotic work cell. From the initial design concept, to 3d models in VR, to a build process that resulted in exceptional robot performance; this team exhibited the best in the code of chivalry. We would scan their QR code anytime.

This team inspires young people to be science and technology leaders. They love helping their local teams and have a shared shop with a few teams, this team supports FLL events where they are involved as volunteers, judges, and even as hosts for the events. Their unofficial motto is “minority being the majority.”

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: With bright colors and a unified aesthetic, this team highlights the principles of FIRST both on and off the field. This veteran team’s theming is so consistent, they are recognizable across New England. With smiles on their faces and on their robot, there is certainly a lot of buzz around this team.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team exhibited impact protecting features and weight management from the start of their build. The risk management in their design process allowed them to sizzle on the field with a hopper that couldn't be stopper'd.

Sensors and nodes galore give this robot situational awareness. With a real sense of cargo locations, their robot knows exactly where it is. Their goals are so lofty, they don't have time to stop, square, and shoot.

This team straddled many categories from robot design to gracious professionalism. Their enthusiasm leads them to share their code freely and help teams remain functional throughout the weekend. Their programming SLAYS allowing the driver to let the robot take control.

Color coded pneumatics allow this team to know exactly what tubes and pressures they're dealing with. Their intake can shrug off a blow with nary a grunt. Armor plated racks keep their climbing system bulletproof.

This team believes it’s the bond they have together that is the most important. They impressed the judges with their obvious enthusiasm in supporting the members of their team, community, and other teams. They brought their mojo back to their school system during covid, when they made buttons for all teachers with the teachers’ faces on them.

Sitting back and reeling in point after point with their well-designed autonomous system, this team is truly a catch. Using a customer designed shot alignment system and a color sensing intake, they made quite a splash.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Heating UP the competition, this team used their creativity and ingenuity to conquer all of the challenges they’re facing. With no access to a machine shop, this team had to design parts that were easily adjustable and multi-functional. Their perseverance and gusto lit up the playing field.

When the world turned upside down, This team looked adversity in the eye and said, What can we do to help? Their incredible dedication to community service, became about switching gears in a crisis, while paying extra attention to their team’s mental health. Their generosity, spirit and inspiration are felt by Lego Leaguers and Scouts, by students in an amazing number of STEM classes and clubs, by local first responders, and by girls in Africa, India and South America. Do they cat nap to keep their energy up? It’s time to Girl Up!

This team is nearing the PINNACLE of STEM outreach. They bring local guidance and mentorship, while also donating foreign assistance and teaching. They are a BEACON of light for all interested in learning to ride the WAVES of engineering.

This team practices engineering and excellence in competition and business. Their budget, team structure and SMART goals are clear and detailed, making them out of this world. Analyzing their strengths and weaknesses, they’ve planned to ensure future PEACE.

It’s never easy to create a final design. Prototyping is better than guessing, and this team brainstormed an elegant robot and stuck to their schedule. With an ACE up their sleeves their robot aims HIGH!

When talking with this team, it was clear that they understand and practice gracious professionalism. They have a long working relationship with another FRC team, providing robot demonstrations annually to the larger community. This team stood out for their partnerships with the two newer FRC teams, lending their shop space, equipment, and expertise during the build season and at competition.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s growth, impact, advocacy, and outreach are top bar! The EYES have it. GREG is not your average snail.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot’s sleek, slightly menacing profile is the result of an elegant design concept. This robot was looking good as it was put through its paces, succeeding in autonomous, scoring in the upper hub and climbing the bars. In a performance that would make its former mentor proud, this team worked their MAGIC on the field.
With a philosophy to make it easy and address problems that arose, this team fixed it with gyros, sensors and controls. With a GALE of wind, these HAWKS soared above the rest.

This team wowed the judges with a well thought out approach for building the team as well as making an impact in the community. All the members have learned and leveraged technology for building a solid robot in spite of multiple challenged and donate money raised from their outreach to Parkinson’s research. They were the APPLE of our eyes.

This team exhibited consistent performance throughout the match. A clean design with solid construction techniques, well managed wiring and an efficient electronics board helped this team score the lower hub time after time. Attention to detail and quality work has helped this team FALL into this award.
This team built themselves to success in less than 5 weeks. Continuously learning on the fly, their robot just keeps getting better and better. Their PROJECT Was big, but their ambitions were bigger.

The number of teammates excited to speak with the judges and their enthusiasm helped this team stand out. This cohesive team tries to foster excitement about FIRST by volunteering for FLL Challenge at events, mentoring a team, and submitting a proposal for a new FLL team at another middle school. During COVID, the team reached out to their local elementary school to create photo buttons for teachers to wear on their masks to help the young students connect with their teachers.

records.script: Their ability to soak up the limelight and keep themselves oriented, even when hit, kept their scores high and their rapid iterations on their software assured their autonomous was certainly not canned. Team 180- SPAM.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This unique design swings through the air. This team uses a chip bowl to defeat its opponents. You don't normally see a periscope on a BAT. Team Combat.

While still young, this team has demonstrated an aptitude for business and their membership has soared. This team has successfully created a team nest egg. Making Ms. Erin proud, this Entrepreneurship Award goes to team 7431 - Wingspan.

Melvin Conway's law is that the architecture of a system will always resemble the organization that created it. This team created an exceptionally modular beautiful robot, software and pit. The design allowed for a Noble autonomous mode in which they secured the LION share of the points. A true masterpiece, team 4481-The Rembrandts
This team might help you by surprise. After a little political guidance you might be throwing stars. When you are in trouble - call a ninja.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: In a swamp far far away emerged an unlikely hero. Their theme is better kept out than in and Dragon was able to emerge from her tower. Lets celebrate with some waffles and congratulate tea 7072 - OGRE.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The preparation and design for this robust robot was of of this world. The best robots only have two parts and this one only needs two tools to put it together. The force is strong with this blue and white robot, good it looks

The ability to rotate and control your robot is key to success. This team can traverse and over the challenges of the game. With the innovate use of gyros and locks, this is no resistance in their path to reaching the top.

This team bubbled to the top of many judges list. Their team's operation, membership, outreach, and machine process are better than a trip to the beach. The judges want to float the Servant Leadership Award to team 4118, Roaring Riptide.
This team of kids continuously improves. A team of youthful machine workers from the muck. Gator-managed risk, task, milestones and progress out of the Swamp.

This team reaches out to students of all ages, from hosting workshops, outreach events and mentoring dozens of other FIRST teams. They also hosted the first off season competition in their region, one of the oldest in the country. On inclusion, they are on the right track, publishing a book on female STEM role models. COVID did not derail their efforts from hosting webinars, their strong alumni network, to translating FIRST documents into multiple languages. Fasten your seatbelts. This team has everything UNDER CONTROL.

This team pipeline advances respect for engineering throughout their school, community, and state... Through measurable impact including FIRST LEGO Leagues, off-season events, and advocacy. As this team pushes FIRST into the future, it Breaks Away from the competition .

This young team has created a strong bot with powerful performance! While not racing to finish their robot, this team made waves in their community through outreach events and charitable donations. They caught numerous donors and plan to fish for new recruits in the coming years. It was easier to find your award-earning talents than it was finding Ralph.
They might be new, but they are all geared up! Don't see through the importance of effective branding. Don't worry these ghosts are friendly.

There is an electricity in the air when you are near this team in the stands and pits. Everyone's battery is recharged through this inexhaustible energy source. It won't be shocking to know the Team Spirit award goes to Team Voltage.

This team’s robot swerves away from the swarm. As they buzz around the field, they gather their cargo so they can sting their competition. Their autonomous mode achieves their goal with pointed precision.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The multiple wheels pulled the balls like cat paws. Like all predators, they wanted to make sure they were lean and mean. Their LED’s helped their cat like eyes to hone in on their prey.

This team clearly has the tools it needs to change the world. Their detailed budget, documentation, and planning put them in the top tier when it comes to fundraising. This diverse team’s business plan soars above the others.

One of the most successful components of this robot began as a pizza box. This team bounced into the competition and catapulted themselves to the top. The autonomous climbing system features automatic fail-safe lockouts, gyro sensor, and pneumatic lockout after climbing is done for operator and technician safety.

The ties that bind this team to the FRC community are abundant in quality and strength. When others were struggling, they volted into help like a hero to help others get them on the field. You’ve heard of robot in 3 days, but how about a robot in under 3.86 hours

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: You cannot miss this team when you walk by their pit. From their nice colors of amethyst and gold, to the hissing pest etched into their robot. This team crawled all over the judges.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This elegant machine was designed with modularity, and functionality, and survivability from the forefront. Their swerve drive glides them across the field and their whole machine acts as a turret. There are many bands that keep this team together. From booty bands to construction bands.

This team looked internal to solve this year’s traversal challenge. Their innovative use of sensors allowed them to reliably climb above their competitors. While some teams would simply spin their wheels, this team uses them to control chaos.

This team went above and beyond to engage all members of their divers community. They climbed above various obstacles and created lasting partnerships with their school district and local Historically Black Colleges and Universities through stem kits and engagements. This team didn't have to use any magic to convince the judges to recognize them.
For most teams, falling off the hanger would have knocked them out. But this quality teams’ resiliency proves that being red is clearly better than seeing red.

From outreach through 20 demos to mentoring multiple FIRST teams, providing STEM camps to advocacy for STEM funding; this team STEALS the flame. This Team provides a lifeboat for all, wherever they go!

This teams well defined brand can be easily identified in their large community. Their passion for engineering can be seen and heard through their actions both at home and in the stands. Their global program is the SPARK that makes engineering Explode!

This team uses constant forces to spring into action on the field as well as to navigate the waters of FRC. They decided to incorporate work ethic into their mission statement. Look out for this fin as they cut through the waters, because their main goal is to give every kid a place to be themselves.
The judges were rocked by this small unified team. From their FIRST partnerships with the mouse to their heavy metal enthusiasm.
Throwing a ball is old hat for many machines. Climbing multiple uneven bars without human intervention takes it to a new level. Metal birds rule!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s robot starts each match ready for battle, and likely nourished by a healthy salad. Through the use of creative and unorthodox parts, this team’s competitive advantage is their ability to catapult cargo over the competition.

Just like their mascot, this team represents a unique species due to: A business plan, including a 5-year strategic plan addressing overcoming risks, cross-training team members and raising sufficient funding to guarantee sustainability. They will never become endangered, like their mascot, due to this plan and their community outreach efforts to help others achieve a better future through STEM.

Among our esteemed competitors, one team stood out for the beauty and quality of their build, allowing them to Rapidly React without getting bogged down as they mastered shooting and climbing challenges.
This team dusted themselves off with a clean start. Their positive attitude and respect for all is a great foundation for The Future and puts them at the front of the parade.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team is out of this world and full of opportunity and perseverance. Based on their cohesive theme from their robot to their pit to the entire team, plus all of the ALIEN sightings.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Silently stalking the competition, this team makes their presence known on the field with elegance and industrial flair. We got some robots over here giving it all... You might even think 108%

This is a team that floats like a butterfly, and stings like a bee. Expertly navigating the field - and conquering the competition. There's no surprise: Coming from this state that they brought BIG things to the competition.

One of the teams, considered for a number of awards really stood out because of how they succeeded in rebuilding their team this year. This team, like many others, faced an uphill TREK, in overcoming multiple challenges with team continuity and funding. Through focused efforts, they cut through their obstacles with a machete, and were able grew the team by an amazing 700%.. On top of that, they have become OSHA certified.

This team's stealthy robot has they sway under control and withstands the rigors of competition. With a zen-like calm, this dual intake robot was designed to reduce cycle time and improve redundancy during competition.

This Team is worthy of attention because they are a known force in our community. When it’s raining cats and dogs, this team rises to the occasion with a flood of initiatives – STEM days, Robo Competition days, thousands of face guards to their health heroes, and advocating for state funding for FIRST and STEM. Despite all the challenges of the last couple of this year, they have weathered everything thrown at them and represents the model to emulate because they are the “Eye of the Storm.”

This Team has framed a pipeline for success – FLL, FTC, FRC, and on to the Engineering workplace. They have painted a pathway for others to follow to grow FIRST and the field of Engineering. This team is open and built on the value of sharing, like family - sharing designs, offering engineering advice, setting up a 24-hour call center. There is no secret of who is deserving of this award because “There are no secrets left behind!”
The design of a competitive robot would Vex most beginning teams. This team enjoys shooting for FIRST, pursuing the gold, and it appears they have found their treasure.

In just a few short months, this team has shown they are Masters at advancing STEM in the community. Their success in providing Tech Learning to hundreds of kids in multiple countries is inspirational.
Their enthusiasm, attitude and energy are evident to all. Everywhere this team goes is like a Regal Procession.
