records.script: This team rose from the ashes. They swerved into action using a turret that enables them to score 6 balls during autonomous. Do not let the short T-Rex arms fool you their long reach shots will win every time.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: For reaching great heights and swinging through the competition. Reaching, grasping, and rotating from one level to the next.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award

records.script: This team emphasizes FIRST core values in working with other teams. With their assistance, other teams are able to maintain and even thrive. We bet their efforts build a hunger, a hunger that can only be satisfied by a Big Mac!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: A lot goes into making an identifiable image for a team and these birds have spread its wings with a new colorful and creative mascot. Like a phoenix rising, this team is on fire and leading the pack by storm.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team kept it simple from strategy, to design, through implementation. With their clean lines, minimalistic design, and motors tucked away at right angles they may march past you without even noticing. Don’t worry, we won’t let this team fly under the radar.

This team sets the standard for innovative control through the automation of almost every system on their robot. Floating from one end of the tarmac to the other they launch their cargo on the fly without a care in the world. You won’t need a telescope to see this team’s robot in action, even from space!

Stand in Atlanta, Look to the west, There you will see, quality at its best, Google their name, NASA is part of their fame, Belong! Is their cry, Have fun! As they try, Learn! Is their intention. The Big Cat is here, double hooks for ascension, you have found your dimension.

records.teamName: Career Blazer Robotics - The Fighting Mongooses

records.script: This rookie team’s focus on STEM is a key aspect of their success on and off the field. Their enthusiasm and passion is inspiring. Without a doubt, this team will create a better future for everyone they engage. If you need to be inspired, just look for their shiny hats of gold!

This team’s enthusiasm and spirit in the pits and in the stands makes you want to get up and dance. Their robot’s name embodies their mission to continuously improve. You will remember these caped crusaders chant long after you leave here today. We are the Titans the mighty mighty Titans.

Our autonomous award winner consistently impressed us with their ability to snip the high hoop, especially in autonomous mode. They have definitely found the secret sauce in the code. Don’t let the name fool ya, this team earned much better grades than 4C’s.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This robot was twice baked in the fires of creation and competition. This team took the term recycled wheels to the extreme. With their head, heart, hands, and health they have brought creativity to the event.

This team has been a solid performer that always strives to help others even as they try to excel! An important part of a growing group of teams dedicated to helping each other with knowledge, time, and even resources. This team has catapulted students into the STEM world and has been an integral part of advocating legislators to grow STEM programs for underserved students around Georgia.

This team’s engineering was truly inspirational. Their commitment to science and technology education across multiple schools in their community is unsurpassed. They have established a true “turret” approach to building strong bonds with local industries and true outreach to the next generation.

For the newer teams who have done so, their entrepreneurial spirit has shined through during the event. One team in particular presented a comprehensive plan for success in 2022 and beyond. If this team successfully executes their plan, they should continue to climb the mountain of success.

This team described the whole engineering process precisely. Their robot is truly an engineering marvel; it is both functional and practical. It is an excellent marriage of engineering ideas and creativity. The team certainly deserves a CARROT for their excellent integration of a multitude of parts in a well-functioning machine.

This team is populated with young talent and truly exemplifies collaboration. They ensure tasks are divided fairly and equitable throughout the team. They exude a Gracious all-inclusive Professionalism that is as strong as a “steel talon”.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s aesthetic integration was obvious every time the robot competed in Rapid React. The robot reflects their school spirit during the event by flying those school colors proudly. It’s unique violet color scheme allows it to stand out from the competition.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team is able to describe the practicality and efficiency of their machine. The entire robot is worthy of recognition for its industrial design. Being among the top qualified teams, their robot is unique in terms of both its aesthetic and functional design. They certainly deserve to be FLYING high.

The team identified and described their control system design in a precise manner. Their control system integrated many different sensors for feedback purposes. The control innovation is unique and practical. This is truly a robot that ROARS like a LION.

This team leads with determination, as if they were seeing red. Through cooperation and collaboration, they have built a reputation for leading the herd. By building a coalition of teams that work together and support each other, they have found their way to the final round up. The Bull By The Horns Award

When it comes to a quality plan, this team stood out. Their robot demonstrated robustness throughout the competition. It demonstrated overall quality in terms of workmanship, welds and attachment systems. This team set the bar in climbing. Not only are they a star, but also a Super NOVA.

This team understands what FIRST is really all about; technical careers can be both rewarding and fun. They are creative problem solvers that know the difference between success and failure is sometimes measured in microns. What we’re TALONing you is its no rookie mistake that the Rookie All Star award goes to team 8865; the Dacula Falcon Robots

This team was created to reinvigorate a FIRST journey that began decades earlier. This team has a commitment to science and technology education amongst their team members. Their goals include the establishment of a county wide protocol. A storm of inspiration is brewing……

This team exudes a contagious enthusiasm that bubbles over from every member. Their positive attitude, excited demeanor and inclusive team ethos obviously emit from a genuine and sincere team character. When you combine these traits with tutus and antennae, you get an excellent example of Team Spirit.

Leave transportation to the humans and there is bound to be some lost luggage. What the world needs is a robot with a mind of its own. While some teams set still, these Bulldogs AI saved the day. The Autonomous Award goes to TEAM 1771, North Gwinnett Robotics.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When two development teams overlap on the same system, it often costs time and money. This team from Marietta, Georgia designed a clever way for two people to work on the same system at the same time. Their driver station really shines, thanks to their clever “fake robot”. Congratulations to TEAM 1311, Kell Robotics, for winning the Creativity Award.

This team should bottle their passion for FIRST! With a HAWKEYE focus on expanding FTC Teams, they have grown to be one of the largest FIRST programs in Georgia. Creating scholars at home and abroad. They are clearly a SUPERHERO FIRST program. Congratulations to TEAM 7451, Avenger Robotics for winning the Chairman’s Award.

records.teamName: Career Blazer Robotics - The Fighting Mongooses
records.script: This team’s engagement with FIRST, their community, and sponsors continue to inspire. Like their mascot, they fearlessly pushed on post-covid with innovation when they launched a new program focused on feeder schools, doubling their team and increasing female participation over 30% . The Engineering Inspiration Award goes to Team 5900: The Fighting Mongooses!

Building robots can be expensive, but this team has a great business plan to support their technical know-how. They creatively use websites and apps to keep members and sponsors involved every step of the way. The winners of this award are titans of entrepreneurship. The Entrepreneurship Award goes to team 1683 - Techno-Titans.
This team climbed their way to the top of the competition. Once mistaken for MERMAIDS, this team truly demonstrated excellence in engineering. Congratulations to TEAM 6340, the Marist Manatees!

This team is always first to jump to help other FRC competitors, to recruit new members and to expose their community to FIRST. Their Mascot has traveled all 7 continents, even space, spreading the FIRST word and promoting STEM. It should be no surprise that the Gracious Professionalism winner is Walton Robotics.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Integrated imagery is an important part of life. Integrated imagery which also refers to a favorite breakfast food should be an important part of everyone’s day. Let’s all TOAST to Toaster Tech - TEAM 5332 for achieving just that!!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: From building industrial-sized robots in 2017, to their wildly unique design in 2022, this team of cool cats snagged the INDUSTRIAL DESIGN AWARD! Congratulations, great job, TEAM 6705, Wildcat 5e.
With three different autonomous shooting methods, this team lit up the competition by turning over control to their robot. The innovation in control winner is TEAM 6829, Ignite Robotics.

Sometimes inspiration comes from one place. Sometimes it comes from many parts of the state. A positive attitude and a happy demeanor is inspiration to us all. Congratulations, The judges award for perseverance goes to TEAM 8577, Georgia Cyber Academy Champion
This teams focus on simplicity proves their long-lasting quality. Returning strong after a top 5 finish last year. The QUALITY AWARD goes to Team 8083, ALX Robotics!

This Rookie team already has their sights set on the Chairman’s Award. Not only are they a brand-new school, with over 100 students, the leadership and orchestration exhibited during their inaugural season is a solid indicator of their drive and innovation. They also created STEM Saturdays to promote First Robotics to the local elementary and middle schools. Our Rookie All Stars are Team 8866 - Innovation Robotics

This team from Marietta Georgia worked as a system of parts working together as a machine. This first-year team worked as a machine representing the best and brightest of FIRST in working to promote STEM principles. Congratulations to team 8736, “The Mechanisms” for winning the Rookie Inspiration Award.

This is not a group you will find in a trash can hanging out w/the junk. This team is Loud, Proud and full of FIRST Spirit! You will find them cheering, helping others, and forever active in their community spreading the word of FIRST. This team is no grouch... they are our Team Spirit Award winners. Come on down Oscar.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Right, left, back, forth…this robot can do it all. With their innovative dual intake system and beam-break shooting technology, this team truly demonstrated why Hawaiian parents are always so proud. Ranked #1 in the competition, these keiki really produced a great result.

With an engineering designed climbing system, an accurate shooting system and a little help with some great driving, this team steadily “charged” up the ranks to #3 overall. We were wowed by their detailed documentation of the design process. They earned their position on the highest bar of excellence in engineering.

The idea of FIRST has taken root in Japan and will grow through their efforts. This team translated the game manual from English to Japanese for all Japan teams to use. Cherry blossoms bloom for this team.

This team’s robot impressed everyone as a full-court threat. Using a well-designed array of sensors and automated controls, this team quickly established a reputation of being highly “koalified” to throw another shrimp-on-the-barbie… Their finished product “bearly” needs a driver.

This team spreads the FIRST core values within their school by advancing world-class education with the establishment of a four-year STEM academy. Always striving for the summit, this team develops personal connections and empowers their community to create a foundation for innovation.

This team let no pandemic constraint limit their mission. They were “Rapid to React” to spread STEM learning opportunities worldwide. They accelerated access to technology with open-sourced global curriculum and personally lobbied industry and government to obtain funding to match education needs. With a passion to inspire innovation and transcend diversity boundaries, this team raised the bar, fully supporting twenty plus schools and seven FRC teams. Let’s celebrate and IGNITE their onboard success. Holomua ‘Iobotics!

This team exemplifies in fostering the magic of STEM to younger students through the innovation of fun crafts. This team continues the legacies forged in fire from previous members and alumni. The principles of “kaizen” – continuous movement – is deeply engrained within this team and its members.

We were thoroughly impressed by this team's self-drive and passion to independently problem solve to produce a well-designed robot. We were wowed by the amount of sponsors gained through crowdfunding to travel from the snowy caps and have their colors shine as the rookie team.

records.script: While other teams are just backing up, this team gives their robot the liberty to aim high and move all over their field. Watch out, they're not at the helm, putting 20 points on the board.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This red team pulls out all the stops to score. Their metal mammal did a wheelie to climb They were creative when they built "Leodore"

With a strong foundation it would be easy to boast, but the team working hard was unable to coast! Building on the past while strategically planning for their future, not only for themselves but also other teams needing nurture.
Before touching tools, they sat for three days, which was really cool. By shooting their shot, they're a jack of all trades All of this makes them cool as ICE.
When teams called for help a team from the north answered the call Extensively helping teams to show they are kings of Gracious Professionalism. They royally light up to support other teams.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Their brand is strong, no matter where you see them. For a long time, they have brought the dream to fields in Iowa. Not to be corny, but this team is a-maize-ing!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This is a team that thrives on form, function and aesthetics while climbing rapidly for the sky. It follows its strategy instead of the herd. It applies high level industrial design to build a metal-clad team and achieve exceptional results.

While other teams were sleeping, this green machine lurked in the shadows. They climbed to the ceiling and frightened those below. Mike the Monster and Maple River Robotics are the winners of Innovation in Control.

This student driven team, from a small community, is creating an AMAZING K-12 FIRST pipeline! They are fully embracing diversity with their whole team completing the FIRST DEI training leading to ~50% diversity of their team! With the impacts of COVID-19, this team his helping all youth by writing model legislation to support mental health for all students in their state!
Climbing trees as efficiently as a cat, This bot waits above for it's chance to strike It's an all around precision hunter.

We need to cultivate more people to create a better world. Spreading STEM thru shared designs, team training and regional events can multiply a team’s impact. Everyone has the potential to contribute, but if you don’t even have access to electricity, you remain dis-empowered. By bringing solar phone chargers to many, everyone can have the opportunity to contribute. We want to congratulate Team 5006, Apophis as the 2022 Iowa Regional Chairmans Award recipients.

When Covid arrived everyone had to stay home, This team leveraged their strong reputation and helped STEM roam. They accessed the internet and then moved to the airways - from YouTube to the television.

In spite of this team's challenges, their robot saw the limelight and planned to pin a win. The judges were impressed with the ability of the SE Iowa team to weather the storm and leverage school mergers. This rookie team thundered its way to the top.

This team from a small town is making a big impact on social media They know that they need to build their future by reaching out to the next generation This group of NERDS should be proud of their SQUAD

Their enthusiasm and their colors awaken our spirits. Using tech, they nurture young cubs with their creative curriculum. We can hear their roar throughout the stands. Three one oh two, Tech-no-Tigers, we applaud you.

This team can score from the start. Their root always knows where it’s at. Modulated intake and turntable spin, helps them win. It only takes 15 seconds to know the autonomous award goes to team 6036, Peninsula Robotics…

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Despite not having much experience, their unique, creative design had us very impressed and lifted our spirits. It really had us HOOKED. The Magic Valley couldn’t be any prouder of this rookie team.

This team displays outstanding entrepreneurial enthusiasm business planning and team building actions. Every team member participates in fundraising phone calls, which develops strong long-term relationships with their supporters. Together, they raised more funds this year than any other year in their 14 year history! They also received many new team members, of which 80% are Freshmen and Sophomores They are reaching their goal of having a permanent home in the Big Sky!
This experienced team paid attention to all the right details. With a quick and modular design from the start, this team was able to spend more time on the details to FORGE a stronger robot.

How is it possible for a team to be in two places at the same time? They split their team and became two WHOLES and not two HALVES. Everywhere we looked, a flash of purple caught our eye. Don’t run from this team, their sting brings success!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.teamName: Victorian Engineered Robotic Nation or V.E.R.N.
records.script: Extraordinary help, ingenious robot, time travel not required. While a close-knit team, they don’t wear stocking hats but they are dapperly dressed for their many outreach activities. Retro-futuristic aesthetics—goggles, vests, and matching robot panels—we select V.E.R.N. for Imagery.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team isn’t afraid to change the field with their robust and simple design. Compact and efficient, this team packed a lot of robot into a small space. The small stature didn’t stop this robot from taking charge on the field.

This team used their many years of experience and team spirit to create a uniquely functional design. Their shaft in shaft intake method had us impressed while other teams took to the sky, this team takes a different approach for their rapid reaction.

Don't Be Afraid At our opening ceremonies on Friday, Brigadier General Pepper challenged us to not be afraid to fail when it comes to learning and trying new things. One of our teams here has an ingrained set of values that makes this concept part of their culture. Have a LaCrois toast at your team cheer tonight!

In order to perform well in competition, a machine must be both robust and be built with quality in mind. Despite fierce opposition, this team MASHED the competition with their unstoppable machine. They drove it like they stole it and it never let them down.

From little children to neighboring schools, this team is in the business of making wishes come true. Whether it is by inspiring the creation, housing and mentorship of numerous FLL, FTC, and FRC teams or speaking to legislators in search of funding, our Chairman's Award Finalist truly invests in the community around them. With a comprehensive and thorough business plan, this team shows just how far a dollar invested in FIRST can go and how to make them count. Their wings are ready. Watch them soar. Congratulations to Team 4598, Team Icarus Innovated!

Whether they are hosting an FTC competition or showing off their robot in their community, this team is bringing engineering to their small, rural town. With dedicated teaching mentors and community buy-in, this team inspires on an elite team level. Helping start new teams in their valley, as if by MAGIC, Hank and his Operators are just beginning their rise.

From humble beginnings in the neighborhood, now with a season and a half under their belts, this team is doing it right. Starting with a single grant, they became pros at getting funding. They used this to unite a diverse team, start outreach, and provide lifelong skills. This team is on a straight line path and will not break.

Trying sums up this team of Rookies. Inspired to build little successes upon little successes. This team shows promise in their future endeavors, even if it isn’t, to quote this team, “the robot their mentor would build”.

For a team to have spirit you need to know them when you see them. Hear them even when they’re far away. Feel their presence like they are breathing down the competitions’ neck. And…smell them? <wink> I’ll let you judge what that means. This team’s culture of diversity stands out more than their amazing jackets they’re sporting.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team established an outstanding overall visual appearance for the team. They deployed the theme in the pits, on the robot, and on team uniforms. Congratulations to the Eagle Army, we salute you!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: With demos and events, this team is always on the move. This team gathers feedback to constantly improve themselves and their events. Using grants, this team fills the FIRST pipeline by starting and mentoring FLL and FTC teams. This "pack" is sitting on the edge of their "red" chairs. Once a Huskie, a Huskie forever!

This community team inspires youth in STEM with scouts and summer camps. Their STEM video helps us all grow in spirit and name. And if you can't make Lollapalooza this summer, make sure you join their scouting-palooza app.

This team is working towards mastering their craft, getting wiser both on and off the field. This team didn't let their "small size" get in the way of making a big impact their first year. They truly went the DISTANCE to show that they understood what FIRST is all about.
This rookie team focused on quality over quantity. They looked local and found strong support among their community. Their robot does it all, proving they can HANG with the big dogs.
Having team spirit is more than being loud. It requires enthusiasm and a good use of props. Say hi to mom, add the mustard, hold the ketchup.

Getting to the top of the robotic world isn't easy, but this decorated team makes it seem automatic. Autonomously picking up and shooting multiple balls, differentiates this team from others. This colorful team can be spotted anywhere.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s unique design has helped them climb to the top. A guided vision system allowed the turret to position and shoot indiscriminately. Storming the castle walls takes creativity, but it's easier when your pirate ship can climb the walls.

This team exemplifies the vital planning and business skills necessary to thrive. They maintain a strong entrepreneurial spirit, while flying high in math and science. Their enthusiasm is explosive! They fly at 50,000 feet and encourage everyone around them to soar.

Like planning for the Iditarod, great detail and process must be set forth. This team has developed the “Gangline” needed to connect a large team to the robot, so when the “Musher” is ready they can give the command “Let’s Go!”

This long-time team knows how important it is to lend a helping hand. Providing training and making parts for other teams, helped make sure everyone could succeed. This electrifying team knows that eagles do not always fly alone.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team begins their identity on a wing and a prayer. They encourage individuality while gearing everything - their incredible fashion, their pits and their pretty cool robot - to the their team image. However, what put them over the top, is hanging over their heads in the pits - their chandelier.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team has been flying around the field and racking up points. They have honey of a robot that buzzes up to the traversal rung. This team that dresses like bees, performs more like a bulldog.

This team's ability to control its Drivetrain, Intake, Shooter, Conveyor, Turret and Climber allowed their robot to Own this year’s challenge with on-the-go shooting. Their consistent autonomous performance seemed like it was being controlled by a pro gamer. Their excellent controls execution helped them Blackout the competition.

This team is a group of high achieving, gracious professionals who are all around good eggs. Though we may question which came first, the chicken or the egg, you’d be on the wrong part of the farm. This team proves themselves on the field and doesn’t try to milk their accomplishments.
This team has a robust design both in design and function. Quality is baked into this team, from their pits to the machine. The recipe is tasty and the Casserole is always ready.

During the pandemic, this team Rapidly Reacted by starting new teams while mentoring others. They have shown increased RESOLUTION, transporting STEM to the future. With inspiring outreach, they make awesome FRIENDS and COMPANIONS, including EVERYONE in the mission of FIRST. They've found the right GEARING ratio to inspire generations to come.

Outstanding collaboration with other teams and the community drive a team’s success toward winning this award. Mentoring students and hosting offseason events is not “outside” their norm. Breakfast fuels these innovative passions, which delivers communication and collaboration.

This team celebrates not only their own team, but all teams, through their exuberance and showmanship. They cheered till they were red in the face, making up cheers for their alliance partners. And, they always kept their heads in the game.

For most teams it takes two drivers to operate on the field, for this team it really only takes one. Successfully automating the controls, sometimes this robot drives itself, the judges were impressed by this team's stealthily meow.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team got a BIT more creative with how they approached the game. With a unique strategy and scoring mechanism, the NOM-NOM-inee for this award has CATAPULTED them ahead.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This team is proving to be a diamond in the making. They impressed the judges with their engagement and understanding of sponsors. Whether as a gravy boat or fancy socks, this Argyll team really rocks.

A well thought out mission and vision statement put this team above the PACK. With a realistic evaluation of risk, their sustainability profile ensures their present and future goals are able to be achieved. These DOGS have obviously learned some new tricks and can RIDE comfortably.

This team created a pipeline of engineering design processes from the ground up to the final version of their machine. Breaking down this complex effort into bite size chunks, using GANT to stay on schedule, their engineering efforts helped them to not break any teeth while chewing through the competition.
This team ensured that no one was on their own preparing for competition. They have shown DOGGED determination in bringing other teams into their PACK.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From their shirts, to their pit, to the wheels on the ‘bot, this team stands out with a consistent theme. This team embraces all the colors of the rainbow, but their LUCKY color must be GREEN.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team’s robot was designed with a focus on programming potential. Their iterative process created a reliable, accurate, and agile robot worthy of GOLD that could run with the BULLS.

This team has integrated controls throughout the features of their robot, coloring the field with bright LEDs, telling their operators when to strike. With their fast AUTO TARGETING TURRET, this robot was FEROCIOUS.

The judges were impressed by this team’s efforts on and off the field, helping other teams GEAR up for competition. When it comes to climbing this team puts down their remotes and lets the auto climb do all the work. This PHYXT climber impressed the judges.
With modular capability and clean implementation, this robot has an amazing DIGITAL quality. Swerving around the field, scoring with ease, and consistently climbing as quick as a mountain GOAT.

With hosting FIRST tournaments, making their practice space available, manufacturing parts for other teams and the community reaching out to them for advice and technical support, this team has proven they have the good SENSE to make STEAM accessible for everyone. RACING to grow FIRST locally and globally, this team is GEARED for success. They are establishing themselves as a CROSSROADS for FIRST.

This team Inspires throughout their community, and by growing their team innovatively, have demonstrated an excellent recruiting plan. Through aiding FLL teams, Girls Scouts, and Boy Scouts to succeed, they have advanced respect and appreciation for Engineering from all ages. This team is a dream come BLUE.
This rookie team got their feet wet in a local FIRST pond, developing a vision to grow a FIRST FLOCK in their community. They have rocked the field and the competition with their DISCO tunes.
This team applauds the others with style, with cheering that lasts for quite awhile. For their enthusiasm we would like to thank the team with the HIPPO robot name HANK!

records.eventName: FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
records.script: By staying on track and thinking in 3’s their auto shined through. Their robot’s speed and consistency makes it worth its weight in gold. Having them on your alliance is like gaining the Midas Touch.

records.eventName: FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team has used creativity to their advantage. Their robot’s unobstructed vision enables good offence and defense. This team in green and black is powerfully moving forward as an inclusive pack.

records.eventName: FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their dedication to inspiring the FIRST message in the younger generation. This includes working with Girl Scouts, mentoring all levels of FIRST teams and summer camps, to name a few. Innovation is at the center of this team. Their work has impacted the lives of both those in their community and abroad. Benji would be proud of this brilliant and diverse group of students. We hope they continue to spread the mission of FIRST. Challenge? - Accepted!

records.eventName: FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
records.script: This team’s community respects and appreciates all they do. Their female focused outreach is running full STEAM ahead. They’ve made inclusive engineering all the RAGE across Indiana.

records.eventName: FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
records.script: Despite losing financial support sue to the pandemic, this team reacted by maintaining sponsor relationships and performing community outreach. Each year they create a precise business plan to achieve their objectives. The judges were googly-eyed reading this well-designed and the executed plan.

records.eventName: FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
records.script: This team decked in purple delivered on both form and function. When it came to problem solving, they did not rely on voting, but used engineering tools and a logical approach. These purple tigers demonstrated their engineering skills on the field with their agile robot with an impressive climber.

records.eventName: FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
records.script: This team was rapid to react when others were in need. As gracious professionals they demonstrated that they were led, as well as try to lead. They were hungry hungry to help as they mentored many, loaned parts, and led by example.

records.eventName: FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: In a time when the world needs a hero, this team aims to impress. Their machine design; clean and bright. The image their pilots display; professional and dressed for the part. This team flies in for the rescue ready to strike.

records.eventName: FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team described their robot just like their robot played the game, simply and effectively. With their multiple shooter prototypes and improved climber design, they quickly traversed up the rankings. This robot was designed strategically, not by luck. And it certainly wasn’t a sham.

records.eventName: FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
records.script: On and off the field this team utilizes advanced computer techniques. The cargo can roll, but once spotted cannot hide from this bot. Their control mechanisms best suit them for intergalactic travel and beyond!

records.eventName: FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
records.script: The judges recognize this well-rounded team for their outstanding community involvement, unique method for gathering more students, and robust design. Being a part of their team is like being a part of the family. These mini movers are really taking flight!

records.eventName: FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
records.script: This team reinforced their robot to withstand the rigors of competition. Their unique serviceable trolley never gave up! With this team you don’t have to open the door to see the light. Let’s kick this into PARTY MODE!

records.eventName: FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
records.script: They acknowledge that the gracious professionalism of others helped them get to where they are today. This team is strong in membership and consistent in autonomous and end game. They have a great foundation, and are confident they will continue to dance to their own . . . . . quacky beat.

records.eventName: FIN District Columbus Event presented by Toyota
records.script: This team showed great enthusiasm cheering in the stands. They geared up for the heat if the competition by cooling down with some Mountain Dew. Their sense of spirit is FEARSOME!

FIN District Kokomo Event presented by AndyMark
