Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: This team used color to identify their targets. Their three-ball auto was a huge hit. Our judges decided to add a FEATHER in their CAP.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team intakes cargo like a pro which had them really Rankine. Fedex would be proud of their appropriately named hometown. Their hot robot set the field aflame.

It is FREEING to have a well-designed business plan. This business plan was both visually appealing as well as informationally well put together, just like their multi-school team. The judges found it a pleasure to review because all the PIECES came together perfectly.

This team had the entire package. Their robot was robust, its programming was excellent, and their drivers had superb control. The only question left unanswered was which side to use to collect some cargo.

records.teamName: Blue Valley CAPS Metal Mustang Robotics
records.script: This team made sacrifices to help three other teams. For these students, helping others get their wheels on the field took priority over helping their own team. HATS OFF to a model team with a SWANKY robot.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team ROARS onto the scene with an adventurous theme. These students celebrate high-flying escapades. Their canary robot sings the praises of Amelia Earhart.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: From servos to sensors, this robot never broke down. They used their apps to graph a reliable design. They don’t get down when it rains, they like a purple rain.

Hailing from a famous college town, this team brought their best. Their robot was well engineered and its appearance was stunning. The only thing better than its looks was its great control in autonomous and in teleop.

This team has created quite the BUZZ this weekend. They’re not afraid to look a little silly in order to put younger children at ease, and the payoff is creating dividends in growth. Their willingness to share the spotlight with more arts-oriented peers allows them to provide their very own drumroll!

From the finely machines glossy black frame to the entire “pit” and finish, this team exudes quality. Their robot survived quals with only a few scratches on their door. This is no ‘Frankenstein’s Monster”, it’s a quality robot.

This team brings together FRC teams multiple times a year to prepare for the competition season. They start, fund, and mentor teams for other FIRST programs and volunteer at competitions. They light up their community through food drives, presentation, and robot demos, and help scouts earn merit badges. Their program’s sustainability is DRIVEN by educating younger students with Bricks to Bots, Robotics Summer camps, CAD-ettes, and Junior Robotics League.

This team made others red in the face with their efforts to spread STEM to students through summer camps. They BLAZED trails for younger students with their work with scouts. This team STAMPEDED through their school spreading the word of FIRST at community open houses and school events.

There are rookie teams, and then there are teams even newer. This FTC and FRC team decided that they wanted to fly even higher, and we’ve been watching them climb all weekend. We expect this team to continue soaring with their recruitment of eaglets and their district partnership, building their AERIE by broadcasting their matches to the school.

From the very beginning, this school created enthusiasm and excitement with contagious cheering and visual stimulus. Long before this event, they rallied new teams and encouraged them to compete. Using light sticks, pom poms and a large lighted sign, they infected everyone with a strong dose of enthusiasm.

This team’s use of multiple autonomous modes was truly SHOCKING. Designed to work in PARALLEL with the alternating abilities of robots on their alliances, they truly AMPED up this category with over one dozen pre-mapped, autonomous, waypoint defined CIRCUITS. All of these SUPER NODE paths were sync’d with a bit of MOJO MAGIC.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team took the path less traveled to develop a unique dual intake system. Their system does not get “bogged” down when pulling in more than one ball at a time. They really AGITATED the competition.

When it comes to big plans, this team really sparkles! Their business plan sets the gold standard and their outreach program rescues FIRST from the dog pound. These big dogs have led the pack in earning this Award!

The ability to “track” a robot from conception to completion is not an easy task. Yet, explaining how they moved through the design process, providing evidence of iterations and modifications, and describing their numerous manually milled components was “smooth sailing” for this team.

Setting their sights on the young and far-flung, they “make everyone better and learn together”! By sharing their talent, their things, and even their team members, there is no obstacle stopping this team when it comes to fostering relationships. An example for others, this team truly embodies Gracious Professionalism!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When this team rebranded a few years ago, they created a colorful, unified, eye-catching theme in their pit, robot, and clothing. What sets this team apart is that this theme is more than just a color, it is their identity. The judges were tickled pink!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The students from this team produced a visually appealing bot. Their machine design, from the auto adjusting turret to their functionally elegant truss webbing, is truly out of this world!

This team worked together using each other’s strengths to develop…creative, detailed, and well-scripted routines. They showed up to this competition prepared to be a flexible alliance member by using their strategic programming to compliment other robot’s strengths. While reviewing this team’s controls system, the judge’s thought this team’s code distinguished them as “phenomenal”.

The judges were impressed with the outreach efforts of this team. They recruited team members and sponsors through a variety of methods including toy drives, neighborhood fliers, and taking their robot to the streets. They now mentor 2 FLL teams and 2 FTC teams. The team also addressed a unique need in their community by developing a program that engages youth in reading writing and math camps in rural locations. The certificate the youth receive in this program is recognized by the wider educational community.

This team’s robot exemplifies workmanship, robustness, and functionality. They focus on all areas of the competition, including automation, shooting, maneuverability, and climbing. These subsystems were “perfectly merged” together at “high velocity.” Their robot demonstrated superior quality and performance, all the way down to the “sub-atomic level”.

Do you want the recipe for …How to create a pathway to systemic change? How to foster a culture that embraces STEM and all of its opportunities? This team has found the right ingredients… Passion, tenacity, diversity, and leadership. Building on their past successes while adjusting to new challenges, this team formulated and acted on a vision for the future… A vision of having every school in their district implement a STEM curriculum. Add to this base the seasonings of …Outreach, community engagement, university partnerships, and resilience… this team has perfected the recipe for putting STEM FIRST!

Brining students together from a variety of places, this team has learned to connect with each other, their local community, and surrounding areas both in person and through social media. They have worked with community organizations to repair routers and build bicycles for those in need. They are committed to working together to provide leadership opportunities to every member of their diverse team. They have all the right tools to be a strong team and despite their name they don’t play dirty.

As newcomers to the field from all walks of life, this team is a rising star! Focusing on the trifecta of diversity, inclusion, and equality, this team is rapidly establishing themselves as a force for good in their community and to be reckoned with on the field of play. With all their powers combined, they already demonstrate what FIRST is all about.

This team weathered the storm by building strong relationships with sponsors, focusing on establishing a network of peer support, and even shared their “booty” with teams in need. Even fire and flood couldn’t stop this team! Their flag flies highest for this award!

Through their strong partnerships and tight-knit culture, this team inspires others to pursue STEM and FIRST. Their comradery is not limited to just their teammates but extends to their community and sponsors as well. This team is always seen with a positive attitude and a willingness to support others. Even when this team’s spirits are low, they don’t scream, they just eat ice cream.
This team’s Lime Light kept them on the right path to win this award. Unlike your car, this team’s odometer resets when they see their goal. Great on field navigation is nothing NEW to this team.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team spent much of their build season working to take this unique mechanism along a journey from CAD, to small scale prototypes, into a fully-fledged solution to the Transversal Climb. They understood the risks and were excited to find a creative way to make this large mechanism fit inside their robot alongside the other effective scoring mechanisms. In the Offseason, this robot will probably be on the playground, swinging away with its friends on a swing-set.

This team has worked hard to maintain communications among team members as well as the FIRST community at large over the last several years. Hours upon hours of outreach service provided support to rookie FRC teams, FLL Teams, as well as several teams from around the world. The forest this team has planted is most definitely enchanted, with poise and with grace they've taken first place Their openness to share what they have learned since 2016 gave this team a true advantage.

Faced with a crush of rookie and inexperienced members, this team spent their pre-season on training so they could hit the ground running. But their efforts to spread STEM education didn’t stop at their school doors. When it comes to inspiring younger students through summer camps and FLL, connecting with sponsors, and planning community events, this team does a “smashing” job. We just can’t lie: through their commitment to science and technology education, every member of this team has earned its stripes. Qualifying to compete for the Engineering Inspiration Award at the District Championship:

This team has recognized the importance of guarding the future of their team through a successful plan of action. They're well along their way by having raised over $46000 this season alone, and making sure their "Rapid Cargo Delivery Team" is powered for many years to come.

This team went out of their way to think ahead about how to maintain their drivetrain, found and fixed multiple failure points, and strive to continuously improve their robot. While this team hops off their wheels to stabilize their robot when shooting, you can Hop online find this team Blogging away about their robot, its design, and helping other teams implement the lessons learned up in the Vermont weeds.

This team originates from a small region where participants come from many towns & communities. Despite their geographical challenges this team has gone to bar raising lengths to collaborate with other teams, sharing ideas and strategies virtually as well as traveling extra ordinary distances to contribute to scrimmages and in-person idea exchanges. This team aims to Take Flight into the realm of robotics and their commitment to accessibility, inclusiveness and collaboration almost requires just that!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s appearance was like no other, with their costumes and robot perfectly in sync. It looked as if they had jumped straight out of a screen, gobbling up cargo and dancing away from ghosts.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Stuck between a rock, and a tight space to place their intake inside the robot, this team jumped into CAD to design an effective linkage to deploy their rollers and stow them back inside the robot when necessary. The way their swerve drive maneuvers around the field in Autonomous and Teleop commands the attention of an audience, and we’ll be darned- That 4-Bar intake just “looks cool”.

This team has kept their eyes on the hub the entire competition. They have learned how to create the right amount of tension to keep us on the edge of our seats. But in the end it was their custom swerve that really made the difference, and left them as outliers

The Judge's are recognizing this team for creating a Specific and Attainable goal while seeing it through to the end. Through strong partnerships with their sponsors, this team has made a significant impact on increasing their diversity and inclusion, particularly with young women. We hope to C this team continue to sail towards the future.

This team can be seen loading catering on to airplanes in the off season. Its not often a single mechanism intakes, sorts, scores and climbs, while maintaining robustness in its execution. This team well has walked themselves down the yellow brick road to set it apart from the competition.

This rookie team has embarked on their FIRST journey with fair winds behind them and smooth seas ahead. They came to Greater Boston with a solid rookie robot and they’ve used their time in the pits and on the practice field to get even better. They’re building their All Star brand, with their distinctive pastel team shirt and their cute little robot sailor mascot. Qualifying to compete for the Rookie All-Star Award at the District Championship:
They focus on inclusion and diversity. They created plans and places for everyone to feel safe and spread awareness. They created a buzz throughout the stars.
Their themes are consistently seen by the judges. You can spot them in the stands and the pits. They’ve celebrated and adopted “Live Quack Love”

This award goes to the team that the judges admired most for their homemade qualities above all, especially during the autonomous mode. During the 15 seconds they elegantly sink a bushel of cargo into the hub, and their success is measurable with 2 cups of sensors and baked at 350° for 6 weeks. The Autonomous Award Sponsored by Ford goes to team 2067, Apple Pi.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This teams climbing system allowed them to power themselves link by link to new heights. The chain drive in combination with various sensors was unlike anything else. The Creativity Award goes to team 2712, Power Surge.

All actions create an impact. When your actions all align, you have maximum impact. This team currently mentors 18 Jr. FLL and FLL teams. Week zero events and FLL scrimmages are hosted annually. They have a reoccurring Stem segment on local TV news. This team has developed a scalable virtual curriculum that allows any group anywhere to start a FIRST team. This year's improvements include many FRC specific modules. This team directly mentors 4 teams from Africa. Their virtual curriculum is used worldwide in 40 countries. Two hundred teams credit their existence to this curriculum. As Morpheus said to Neo, sooner or later you’re going to realize, just as I did, that there is a difference between knowing the path and walking the path. This team takes the path by storm.

The judges cannot overstate how impressed they were with this teams inclusive and welcoming recruitment of students into FIRST programs. If any other team is in need of assistance, this team will swoop in to provide tactical support. Additionally, this team took to the air waves during COVID and spread the community of robotics on their local radio as well as through their partnership with FIRST ladies. The Engineering Inspiration Award goes to Team 78, AIR Strike. Qualifying to compete for the Engineering Inspiration Award at the District Championship:

This team can work out of any space – what a super idea! When the worst-case scenario occurred, this team analyzed their weaknesses, shifted their space and was able to stay on their Gantt-charted path to ensure a self-sustaining program. This team really “wound-up” impressing the judges! The Entrepreneurship Award goes to team 3467 – The Windham Windup.

This team's design process spanned from day 1 through to milestones on competition day. Their modular design is enabled by standard drawing templates for collaborative manufacturing processes with their partners. They are poised for great success. The Excellence in Engineering Award goes to team the Aluminum Falcons.

This team exemplifies FIRST Core Values. Their involvement in all aspects of FIRST programs was very impressive – From assisting 3 FLL teams and one FTC team. Working together, this team has hosted a FLL Qualifier but has also planned and set up a FLL scrimmage for teams to participate in. They host a summer camp and block coding classes for their community. Both on and off the field, this team was kind and showed that gracious professionalism can cross over all aspects of FIRST. The Gracious Professionalism Award goes to Team 1100, Inverse Polarity.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has a theme for their robot and their team. You can’t miss hearing them in the pits and in the stands. Though their robot name changes every year, it always fit one theme. This year their social media presence aligns with their robot name and the theme of irony and making people laugh. This team, named after their mentor, shows their longstanding history and appreciation for mentors. You better Goggle Up Gondoliers! The Imagery Award goes to team 5112, the Gongoliers

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot was designed with modularity in mind. Robust and compliable is the name of their game, with their ability to easily swap out mechanisms. Their one-inch hole pattern allows their linear shooter to easily “Bolt-On”. The Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors goes to team 1768, Nashoba Robotics.

This team’s control system allowed them to “soar” to success in qualification matches. Their trajectory planner, joystick shaping, and shooter controls were expertly described and implemented. The Innovation in Control award goes to team 230, the Gaelhawks.

This team impressed us across the board with their team and their robot. They made sure to maintain their technical skills during the 2021 season and are even bringing it down to the middle school level. Their impressive and robust control system allows their robot to shift into a higher level of competition. The judges award goes to team 4048, Redshift.

This team impressed the judges with their overall workmanship, machine robustness, and risk mitigation. They planned ahead using sensors to mitigate problems but maintained an eye for machine reparability through component design. They showed a “Hachiko” like commitment to quality. The Quality Award goes to team 1153, Timberwolves

This team is very involved in their communities – coming from several schools, they are able to reach out through summer camps, STEM fundraisers, and pep rallies Their documentation of EVERY aspect of their season stemmed from defining team roles, to their numerous CAD models, and the day-to-day activities. They laid out their all of their teams five levels of certifications and had robust safety rules. They have a succession plan that could make them a Chairman’s team in the making. The Rookie All-Star Award goes to Team 8709, Pathfinder Tech.

This rookie team really demonstrated their passion for STEM and FIRST all around their community. They took their passion for engineering from their founding mentor into a farm event and elementary schools around the area. Tying a bow on their first competition, they impressed us by allowing middle school students to be inspired by FIRST and get in on the fun. The Rookie Inspiration Award goes to team 8544, Reinforcement.

Like many teams here today, this team showed enduring team spirit and energy in the face of the COVID pandemic. In a rebuilding and recovery year, this tiny team impressed us with their excitement for the competition, robot and future of their program – with creative plans, ideas and demos planned into the summer. With their amphibious mascot, Pablo and infectious enthusiasm – Who can this team possibly be? The team spirit award goes to Team 716, Who’sCTEKS.

This team’s autonomous capabilities have them climbing high in the rankings. Their impressive suite of robot software senses its environment and reacts appropriately, controlling mechanisms so their red-and-black-clad drivers can focus on strategy. From raining cargo into the hub at the start to their impressively fast climb at the end, it’s hard to remain NEUTRAL about this team’s successes.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team fired high and accurately with their revolving shooter then climbed rapidly to the top with powered and articulating arms. No trojan horse here.

They gave an informative and interesting presentation. Telling us about how they sponsor many FLL teams, inspiring kids from K to 12 and onward to their own FIRST-focused university. They foster a culture of STEM education with a new innovative lab, their own STEM curriculum and support for grant legislation. Dean would be proud of their TENACIOUS outreach to inspire the next generation. This action resulted in 10% of their high school student body participating in FIRST to achieve galactic domination.

This team WEATHERED the pandemic by expanding their engineering outreach both locally within their community and beyond. They create sustainable FLL-In-A-Box kits GEARED to bring engineering to the masses. One of their primary goals is to create a LINK between FIRST teams across the world by creating a free FRC training website available in 40 countries.

The entrepreneurship award celebrates the entrepreneurial spirit that is alive and well in the North Shore! This team makes their sponsors proud AND even let the sponsors in on their accomplishments. They have a safety plan, the support of their friends, a feeder pipeline, and they have packaged all of this in a clear and concise business plan.

This team focuses on strategic development for process improvements. Their professional planning and community involvement is an important aspect of creating an impressive machine. By coordinating with alliances and blasting away at the hub, calling on their sensors to climb like a Jedi mind trick.

Sportsmanship, teamwork, and collaboration are what this team is all about. They focused on sharing their knowledge across the open alliance and engaged their community about FIRST. Their no-cut policy increased participation, allowing them to lead summer camps, FLL tournaments, and design challenges for the hearing impaired. Their colors are orange and black and red and represent gracious professionalism in every way.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Imagery is very important for this team in everything they do. It is found on their mascot, their artwork, their shirts, and their robot. Legend has it this team’s image evolved from the moon! But one day that changed when they followed the yellow brick road and found a smile on their faces.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: A tall golden hero, taking the elevator lift up with their beautifully designed woman. At first she was Pamela then she became Poison.

This year’s award is given to a team that excelled in executing their well-planned trajectory and traversing programs. The results of their dreams and hard work were revealed to us mortals in autonomous mode. Congratulations to the team of dreams, Morpheus!

This team rebuilt robotics teams in their community, reestablished their VEX teams and funded the teams, they started MANY NEW fll teams and recruited 100’s of new team members. This is an entirely student run team that promotes STEM in their community through unique avenues. They promote healthy relations and a safe place to talk about abuse through Melrose Alliance against Domestic Violence. Congratulations to team 2713. We wish you luck and that your love for STEM grows and glows.

This team is dedicated to making their robot last for the long term and are constantly making improvements. By working with alliance teammates to strategize, especially in autonomous, they can SPRING forward to climb the highest challenges by lifting safely and being prepared. The quality of this team and their robot is strong and impressive, may use their robot to inspire others, and see the COLORS ahead of them.

Botball was not enough. This FRC team started in a garage with a team of 6! They run STEM workshops, participate in STEM expos, and share their experience at school and in their communities. This team convinced their school to give them space and a budget for their next year.

This close-knit team’s spirit is visible everywhere. In the pits and in the stands – where their supporters watch from afar – to their school and their community. They even tagged every team here with their spirit.
This team’s robot navigates the field and with high results when left to it’s own devices. Their consistency in scoring during autonomous fills the sky with a flurry of balls during every match.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Their sights were set up high but on spin was their goal. Prototypes from strainers preceded PLA designs. Two catapults named Bert and Ernie chucked cargo into the hub.

This team’s focus on the mental well-being of their members has helped them fly to the top. They come soaring in to support their community’s most vulnerable members. They dove in to improve their school, getting involved at every level to alleviate STEM deprivation. Their work to spread STEM both locally and globally while also rising up against world-wide hunger h landed them above the competition.

The Engineering Inspiration Award celebrates outstanding success in advancing respect and appreciation for engineering within a team’s community. Inspiring others to respect science and technology requires passion, knowledge and commitment. These qualities were best exemplified by this inspiring team of “Amanda admirers” who has a mission to grow STEM education in their community and particularly for girls around the world.

This team makes a splash with spirit to get kids making stuff. They are engaged in all levels of FIRST. The team is goal-oriented, with a student-first pipeline, supporting others near and as far as Nigeria, bridging cultural differences with their passion for technology.

This team knew this year’s design needed to meet the challenge with a different process. Limited access to tools, small space to build, and no place to test were all solved by building a highly adjustable mechanical and parameterized software. Their ability to tune created a near-perfect shooting machine.

This team is always willing to give their two minutes to others. Whether opening their practice field to other teams, serving those who served first, or changing in to tear down a field at competition, they always remind us to be gracious and be kind.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When the lightning strikes and the thunder roars, this team will move heaven and earth to tie everything together. From past to present and through space and time, tians could not stifle their designs.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team consistently builds and competes with strong, robust robots. This team believes in functionality over fanciness. They have always been a natural predator in New England, but always have all four paws grounded.
This team’s use of vision and code make picking up cargo so easy. Its value is as good as a golden hoard. The haptic feedback lets their driver know, “Here there be Dragons.”
3D printed parts galore supported their simple, consistent design. The printers were pushed to the limit, but this revolutionary team made it look as easy as pie.
This team built a robot hat is no bust and has a strong constitution, building in controls to help prevent damage. Their 8-step process let them climb to new heights and achieve quality results.

This team’s safety plan focuses on overall heath and mental well-being. They had all of the judges buzzing about their outreach. They collaborate with their entire school and community in the fight against domestic violence. We can’t wait to see what they do in the coming years.

This team works hard to encourage interest in robotics in their school. They put an emphasis on safety and planning in their innovative design. Their team organization and record-keeping would make any business proud.

From t-shirts to buttons, this team exudes spirit that reflects each year’s game theme. The use of social media to spread “Meme”ful Monday sparks joy over social media that sometimes turns mentors into waffles. Their energy will always float them down the canal to success.

This robot chases down balls in a way that grabs your attention. It's no illusion, it does it all with the press of a button. How does it work? We don't know, it is Black Magic! The winner of the autonomous award goes to team 237 Black Magic from Watertown, CT

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's creative climber helps them climb the ladder of success. All through competition, balls slide and shoot through the frame of their robot. This team really gets hyped as they slide their way to the top. Congratulations to team 69, HYPER.

It is evident that this team embodies a strong team spirit, innovative solutions, and aids those in need. The core values of this team clearly align with those of FIRST. This team aims to inspire their community and values exposing younger students to STEM. This team uses their local library to teach robotics; they attend local festivals and take museum trips to demonstrate their robot to the community. They mentor a local FLL team and annually host an FLL competition. They also actively volunteer in the Special Olympics and have been working to develop a STEM based curriculum to students with special needs. This team annually attends an advocacy conference each year to maintain relationships and build new connections with local political figures while promoting FIRST and STEM. If all of that wasn’t enough, this team created an assistance technology program, creating Hydration alert, to help people remember to drink and stay hydrated. It is our privilege to award this district competitions Chairman’s Award to: The Intimidators, Team 61 from Upton, Massachusetts.

Ain't no mountain high enough for this awesome team. Like their state bird, the hermit thrush, they're singing a distinctive sweet song to grow the FIRST mission across their green state. Congratulations to this pioneering team the iBots for Engineering Inspiration Award!

This team's student led, well organized structure really stood out. This team views risks as valuable learning experiences, and they have a strong desire to teach students new skills. Their tiered financial plan that includes student grant writing will help them ensure a strong financial future. Congratulations and fly high Team 2342 Team Phoenix!

This team has a real-world engineering structure with a CEO and multiple VP’s for each core team division who are selected through an interview process that occurs prior to competition season, they also developed their own User Requirements before they started any design work. Their design process integrates all aspects of engineering including business, and safety by allowing each department to backcheck designs during their team-wide design reviews, additionally they manage their CAD through a dedicated Discord Server, In the words of Darth Vader “The force is strong with this one”, the Excellence in Engineering goes to team 1073 The Force team.

Pridefully embracing FIRST values, this team makes vital contributions to creating a welcoming and inclusive community. This vibrant team has removed financial barriers to allow maximum access to FIRST. The strong team synergy of team perSEVERE has earned them the Gracious Professionalism award. Congrats to team 5962, perSEVERE!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team's whimsical theme is integrated in everything they do. From their creatively decorated pit where their skeletal Safety Manager stands guard, to their cephalopod adorned robot that takes a ride on The Flying Dutchman. Congratulations Team 5846 - RELEASE YOUR KRAKEN!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team blew away the competition. Starting their design process with cardboard and box cutters, they created a functional, high-performing robot. There can only be one. The winner of the Industrial Design Award goes to Team 126, Gael Force.

This team shoots with great accuracy using their Limelight vision system, they use PID loops for error compensation in position and velocity. Their turret only starts tracking when they are in possession of two balls, they lock their field position by zeroing their drive with 4 absolute encoders. The Innovation in Control award goes to team 1757 the Wolverines.

This team used their recourses and technical acumen to positively impact during a time of need. Their safety protocol is a role model for us all. Congratulations to Aetos Dios for winning the judges award for holistic engagement!

This team's robot withstands the rigors of competition by maneuvering around the field and shooting from their set points across field. Their zero spin cargo shot helps them shoot their way to success. Their 3d printed components kept them centered and helped them traverse their way to the next galaxy. Congrats to team 4905, Andromeda One.

This team really understands what FIRST is trying to accomplish. Against the odds, this team started in the midst of the pandemic and brought together students from three different communities. They have a unique team model that incorporates both High School and Middle School students and creates a pipeline for team sustainability. This team definitely REINFORCES the Core Values of FIRST! Congratulations to Team 8544, Reinforcement!

This team was founded based on the idea that there is room for anyone to be involved in STEM. They met with other teams to find out where they could focus their efforts in this mission and create a diverse group of minds. Their outreach efforts have gotten them town funding which has allowed them to expand their programs for education and advocacy. We know this team will shine bright in the future! Congratulations to team 8567 - Ultra Violet!
From multiple points this team bonds together as a clowder. You can hear and see this team a mile away. And now it's time to let the cat out of the box, congratulations team 3958!

Creating their Matrix from Scratch, we are beginning to believe in Neo. Done right, Homemade is BEST - designing for consistent operation, alliance complimentary strategies, and clear updated documentation on GitHub - for Autonomous Operation, the Autonomous Award goes to... Team 5813 Morpheus.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The sun is shining bright on this team and now they are dialed in. Rosie the riveter would be proud of this modular robot design that looks like a praying mantis. The creativity award goes to team 157 Aztechs.

Not such a long time ago in a town not so far away, a FIRST Alliance was formed to share the vision of FIRST across the land. They expanded their Alliance by adding members from a struggling, but very SMART team from a school nearby, as well as mentoring and supporting multiple FIRST Lego League teams in their region. When they are at Lego Robotics competitions, community events and festivals, their robot mascot is never far behind. This year’s Pine Tree District Chairman’s Award goes to the Team 6153 – The Blue Crew! May the force -er- FIRST be with you.

This team is FIRST across the finish line of engineering inspiration. Their community outreach ranges from creating lego islands with kids, to STEM day with elementary school children, through working with a FIRST team in latin america. The engineering inspiration award goes to team 166 Chop Shop.

Focusing on "team business" growth by partnering with chaos. Sponsor funds, or barter, it's all appreciated for raising "doe" and supporting the team. Mentoring new members to join the herd while raising the big Bucks! Entrepreneurship Award goes to: Team 6329 Bucks’ Wrath

They're cranked into gear for a season of excellence There is nothing this team GAANT do They "take from the best, invent the rest." The award for excellence in engineering goes to Team 3467, Windham Windup.

This team puts Safety first, but also takes a risk by helping others. With collective students from four schools, this financially astute team is a go-to for parts, tools, and less tangible forms of support. The gracious professionalism award goes to... Team 4906 The Collective.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Guided by their spirit animal you will find their colors high above in their pit and down below. This award goes to team of a different stripe, so watch out for a flash of orange in their garden--Cheeto their mascot. The winner of the Imagery Award is team 4041 the Iron Tigers.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: They are climbing fast ’cause they’re light and strong. They cram many functions into a single printed part. The atomic parts add up to performance that matters. The Industrial Design Award goes to Team 125: the Nutrons.

This team used their not-so-artificial intelligence to make their machine learn how to throw. Their robot would do well in a jungle, climbing like a chimpanzee. And when your team does not fit the trend, you are "The Outliers". The Innovation in Control Award goes to team 5687.

Did the pandemic spin you around or blow you off course? This team created mental health resources for their community and essentials for students in need. With Karma definitely in their corner, the judges award for uplifting their fellow students goes to team 7314 Tornadoes.

Their hair is on fire, but they are built to last. Their electronics are safe under the wooden deck. They are a quality crew but they won’t cause a riot. The Quality Award goes to team 58, The Riot Crew!
They are racing through the competition, with flags waving. Their energy is electrifying. Proving some ships look best in neon, the Spirit Award goes to Team 172: Northern Force.

This team SWARMED the competition with their autonomous capabilities that get the DUB. Their robot was LIVING RENT FREE in the heads of their competitors consistently scoring 5 balls during auton. When it comes to teleop, this team SLAYS. The judges were SHOOK by their color sensors for ball detection and BUSSIN’ one-button climbing sequence. Congratulations, Team number 33, the Killer Bees.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The NUCLEUS of this team did not take any CHANCES! They FLEX their robot’s double cargo sorter, and a shooter that can detect distance and fire reliably from anywhere in the PASTURE. Their approach is a BUSSIN’ design that CATAPULTS them to 100% success, NO CAP. MOOOOOOVE over everyone else. Congratulations, Team number 5050 Cow Town Robotics

This team HIGHKEY understands the importance of the FIRST progression, utilizing their own PEEPS to mentor over 20 teams at the FLL-E, FLL-C, and FTC levels. They run off-season events to get the KIDDOS ready for real competitions, hit their GLOW UP, and hopefully leave with a BIG DUB. With almost 20 sub-teams, they create an environment where students can identify their interests, evolve their talents, and indivisibly bond with others. A strong relationship with sponsors, an intelligent financial strategy, and an incredible ability to adapt has proven that this team will continue to be SUS………tainable for years to come. From leading hunger walks to repairing puppy incubators, they remain active and engaged in their community. Strong advocates for inclusion, these BOTS invite all to join their NUCLEUS. Come get this DUB! Congratulations, Team number 245, the Adambots.

A team’s impact on their school is PIVOTAL to an engineering inspiration winner. Their efforts SLAP. They incorporate career and technical education classes, including mechatronics and CAD. They fundraised to purchase a new CNC machine for their whole district. Aside from their A+ robot, this whole PACK hosts summer camps impacting hundreds of students. They LEVERAGED their school presence to reinvigorate their FLL & FTC efforts. By mentoring 3 FTC and 5 FLL teams, their POSITIVE FORCE can be felt by over 150 engaged students. Their community volunteer efforts pass the VIBE CHECK, NO CAP. After interviewing this CAT, the judges were like SHEEEEEEEEEEEEEESH. Congratulations, Team number 2137 The Oxford RoboCats

This team’s school didn’t have the tech programs they needed, so they innovated and their entrepreneurial spirit drove them to start their school’s CAD and computer programming classes. They don’t rely on LUCK to find sponsors to get that BREAD. They have many sponsorship partners giving them financial sustainability and their amazing recruitment system growing little future LEPRECHAUNS will keep their team going for years to come. Congratulations, Team number 7660 The Byting Irish

Their robust intake system grabs balls left and right. They shoot LIGHTS OUT because they have all the sensors they need to SECURE THE BAG. They can POP OFF a shot in one second with the use of their reflective sensors. Their robot ROARED through the competition. Congratulations, Team number 1684, the Chimeras

This team exemplifies the importance of the PRIDE by mentoring other teams and hosting in-person and virtual competitions. This team doesn’t let others TAKE THE L. Their sustainability allows them to help teams locally and even in Mexico GET THAT DUB. They POUNCE on opportunities to assist other teams whenever they can. Congratulations, Team number 5436, the Cyber Cats.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This veteran team had the judges BUZZING about the FUTURE. They demonstrate FIRST core values with FLARE and HAIR. They’re a TIGHT TEAM with a TIGHT THEME that makes their presence shine in their community and the competition arena. We’re sure they are creating a brand that will be identified all the way BACK TO THE FUTURE. Congratulations,Team number 6344 Yale Jiggawattz

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team uses their SUPERHUMAN game analysis to design a LITTY FRESH robot. They have the ability to HOVER over the field and SWOOP in to score with their accelerator tower design. No TALONS are needed for this team to SOAR to the highest rung. Congratulations, Team number 2834, the Bionic Black Hawks

This HYPE team is READY FOR BATTLE with their unique side load and DRIPPIN’ turret launcher. Their 10 motor encoders with feedback help them quickly DIP around the field. Their EGGcelent onboard gyroscopic sensor helps them FLOAT wherever they want to go. Congratulations, Team number 3656, the Dreadbots

The Judges give the BRIGHT FUTURE award to this team that just HITS DIFFERENT. It’s like they have a particle accelerator. They are a MAIN CHARACTER in FIRST with their student leadership, outreach, and community programs. On top of all that, their robot SLAPS! This team ain’t MONKEYING around, they are one big FAM JAM. Congratulations, Team number 469 Las Guerillas

This team knows that building a quality robot begins early on with a LIT chassis. They overcame challenges with their intake system and the mechanics of this robot were the FEATURE PRESENTATION. Their on-field performance delivers on their stellar design. All EYES are on them as their highkey VR camera is on the field. Congratulations, Team number 7211 Hollywood

You may not know WHOOO this team is, but their perseverance ensures a DOPE future. With only 7 members, they are already recruiting with posters and outreach to grow their team and raise awareness of FIRST. They ain’t takin’ the L, No cap! Congratulations Rookie Team number 8519, Bubo’s Parliament

This BAND OF HEROES in their first year created a foundation that will last for years. Their HIGHKEY approach helped them create 8 departments for success. Their hands-on approach helped them sustainably SLAY their way through ATHENS. Congratulations, Team number 8728, The Argonauts

This team understood the assignment to BRIGHTON their community with their contagious energy and positive spirit. Their support and recognition of other teams is STRAIGHT FIRE. This team’s POLISHED presentation emphasized the importance of environmental sustainability and coopertition. This group is full of GEMS who shine above the rest. Congratulations, Team number 4362 CSPA Gems

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award
records.script: This year's winning team has “ONLY JUST SET SAIL”, but it is already heavily collaborating with the First Robotics community and demonstrating the principles of Gracious Professionalism. They are actively promoting FIRST in many community outreach and school events... And “LIKE THE SIREN'S SONG”, their social media presence has lured major sponsors and continued to swell the ranks of their team, well on their way to a “BAND OF 50 HEROES”. Jason would be near as proud as First Robotics is to call this rookie team “ALL STARS”. Congratulations, Team number 8728 The Argonauts from Athens High School from Troy, Michigan

This BUSSIN team acts as FRC BETA testers. Their T shirt Cannon is pure FIRE. TECHNICALLY, with over three thousand outreach, volunteer, and mentoring hours, there isn’t anything this team can’t do. They FOUGHT to have a team in every school in their district, and they work with the local fair to spread FIRST beyond their community. They play Connect 4 with robots to boost their team sustainability. Congratulations, Team number 302, The Dragons from Lake Orion, Michigan

This team is FIRE! They FARM other teams and raise awareness of technology and FIRST with grants that provide copious amounts of options. From lunch and learns to school board meetings, they are spreading FIRST throughout their community and are even reaching abroad. You can hear their HOWL from DC to Lansing and they have big plans for equity and inclusion in STEM. Congratulations, Team number 1718, The Fighting PI from Armada, Michigan

This team comes from a small farming community where they created an alliance to help and support surrounding teams. Community outreach is a core part of their program, and their network presents almost INFINITE possibilities for the expansion and sustainability of FIRST and their own PACK. They integrated FTC and FLL concepts into their elementary curriculum for every student in the school district. They have a practice field IN THEIR LAIR where they host nearby teams. Continuous learning is all part of this team’s Growth Mindset. Better call John Deere because there’s a new tractor in town. Congratulations, Team number 3655 Tractor Technicians from Petoskey, Michigan

This team’s DOMAIN may be small, but they create big opportunities and watch their community bloom. From involvement in FIRST at all levels to their eco-conscious initiatives, these canines are eating STEM PIE for breakfast. Their work ON THE FARM is never done, you could even say they’re always in BETA. Congratulations, Team number 6637 BetaWolves from Carney, Michigan

records.eventName: FIRST in Michigan State Championship - DTE Energy Foundation Division
records.script: In school this team would get much better grades than C PLUS PLUS They would never receive a D or F, but just might earn a “P and I” ????? Their autonomous is so awesome the team GLOWS even without the limelight. Congratulations Team number 3538 The Robojackets Auburn Hills, MI

records.eventName: FIRST in Michigan State Championship - DTE Energy Foundation Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: They prove their prowess through accurate scoring, and effective climbing. Their creative method for traversing the rungs puts them in a class with, KING of the Jungle. This team stands above the pack with the unique ruggedness of Erik the Red. Congratulations Team number 2054 Tech Vikes Hopkins, MI

records.eventName: FIRST in Michigan State Championship - DTE Energy Foundation Division
records.script: This PATRIOTIC team developed a concise and impactful business plan. Their summer training workshops, electrical codex, risk analysis, plus their divide & conquer attitude, were outstanding. This team knows that building for now and the future will sustain FIRST, proving that they are AGENTS OF CHANGE. Congratulations, Team number 201 The Feds Rochester, Michigan

records.eventName: FIRST in Michigan State Championship - DTE Energy Foundation Division
records.script: This team’s design process is so robust it could stop a BULLET. They set goals, prototyped, HUNTED down and resolved issues through thick and thin. They POUNCED on problems and really earned their STRIPES. Congratulations, Team number 5114 The Titanium Tigers Fenton, MI

records.eventName: FIRST in Michigan State Championship - DTE Energy Foundation Division
records.script: This team is a FEARLESS defender of the FIRST Core Values They are not only honorable contestants on the field, but they also HELP CONSTRUCT the field everywhere they compete. When it comes to finding a way to help other teams, the GEMOLOGISTS leave no STONE unturned. Congratulations Team 3618 Petoskey Paladins Petoskey, MI

This team has done a great job mapping out their surroundings and understanding the field of play. Their robot climbed to the top in autonomous mode more than once. You can tell all the factors are well thought out and nothing has been RUSHed Congratulations, Team 27!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team came into the competition by striking a Warrior 2 Pose. Their cargo intake utilized a unique material that provided enough traction and surface area contact, while only utilizing a single motor. This team could be a strong contender for the next OPERATING SYSTEM. Congratulations, Team 5260!

This strong and durable team is positively reactive to any challenge. Leveraging their strong relationship with their sponsors to spread, impact and inspire the FIRST mission, they've reached tens of thousands beyond their community. Tripling in size, they grew their FIRST pipeline, ensuring sustainability and retention. This lustrous cat has never lost its roar. Congratulations to Team 5114, the Titanium Tigers!

Sharing STEAM in their community is a walk in the park for this team. They have taught younger students to code and have inspired a new class at their middle school. This team doesn't ramble when they spread the message of FIRST while strolling the streets. Congratulations, Team 4377!

As you CONSTRUCT your team you are sometimes met with adversities and unexpected events. This team ASSEMBLED more funding with fewer sources. Understanding the goals of the competition, this team UNITED to FABRICATE a successful business plan. Congratulations, Team 5166!

This team knows that you may STRIKE out a few time, before you win. Even if they slip on a BANANA peel, it's an opportunity to get back up. During the competition, this team targeted the moon but blew past it and made it all the way to SATURN. Congratulations, Team 5460!

This teams positive attitude gave judges the CHILLS. They opened their doors, shared their tools and knowledge, which had a few younger teams HUMMING with praise. Gracious Professionalism is a dish best served REFRIGERATED. Congratulations, Team 5084

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This convocation sets its sights on high achievement. The team displays majestic style and graceful innovation. Not only do they look the part, but they back it up with a fierce strike on the field. Congratulations, Team 3322!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This award wasn't a random SHUFFLE of the cards. The electronics of this teams robot were carefully arranged, with extra attention given to protecting wires from the motors' heat. This robot is more stable than a HOUSE OF CARDS, with purposeful weight placement to keep a good center of gravity. Congratulations, Team 4994!

Talk about a clever robot! This team has integrated mechanical pneumatic and software controls to demonstrate unique machine functionality unlike any other. When not on the field, this robot can be found in the gym working out their METAL and flexing their MUSCEL. Congratulations, Team 1506!

The judge award we are presenting today has been deemed the Community Hero's Award. The fluorescent caring of this team showed through the pandemic. Their colossal contribution of thousands of PPE and thousands of books, protected their community and fostered knowledge. This GRAYT team had made a GRAYT impact! Congratulations Team 1322!

This team heard about the space race, so they RUSHED to complete with the earthlings. The use of varied materials and manufacturing processes, from 3D printed joints to repurposing wheel treads, made a robust machine that was ready for an adventure. We better call up Elon Musk because this team is heading to MARS. Congratulations, Team 494!

Although this team just galloped onto the scene this year, they are rapidly reacting to learn the principles of FIRST. With a little help from friends and family, they are proving to be a force for change. You can tell that this DARK HORSE has a bright future. Congratulations, Team 8767!
Ready to compete, energetic when they get there. Strategic in their play, tireless in effort. This rookie team is an inspiration to the REST of us. Congratulations, Rookie Team 8774!

This teams competitive CALL can be heard across the field. Their energy was felt in the stands, the pits, and even in the judges room. During the COVID lockdown, they were even able to grow their NEST! Congratulations, Team 7202!

When it comes to autonomy, this team’s outstanding design and programming helped them shoot for the best “AND” climb to the top. Everybody knows that self-driving vehicles are the future, but this team knows this “MO” RE than others.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This enthusiastic team maximized the COVID pause to make their robot better, lighter, and faster. The modifications to their intake system, parts, and limelight control increased their shooting frequency and consistency. This “FIRED- HAIRED” team will always catch your eye- today and at the parade on the 4th of July.

This team really knows how to use their ANIMAL INSTINCT to promote FIRST in their community which has helped them to dramatically increase sponsorships. They’ve “CLAWED” their way to the lead by involving over 25% of their entire school in FIRST programs. By constantly evolving and adapting, they’ve shown that sometimes the “BETA” Wolf can become the leader of the pack.

Just when they were getting started, this team had to power down. But time was not wasted as they employed cyberspace to challenge themselves for virtual competition, recruiting and sharing their design for personal protective gear. They have also focused on brining robotics to younger students through FTC mentorship and through classroom Rubix Cubix. Rising to meet the need of local teachers, this team used their 3D technology and Makerspace resources to print communication blocks for visually impaired students.

This team is determined to “SOAR” to new heights. They are involved in a true partnership with their community, working with their local Lions club and 4H. Using unique sponsor levels and perks, they have been able to fundraise for multiple championships. Even though most of their team is ready to leave the “NEST”, they have a plan to ensure FIRST continues in their community for years to come.

This high strength -2- ratio team was unfazed by a little metal on metal sliding. Looking beyond their “ELEMENTAL” namesake for a sticky hook, this team employed carbon fiber hooks for a stable hang allowing them to change their “STRIPES” within the competition jungle.

This team “FLIES” above the rest with their brilliant demonstration of FIRST core values. They prove that not even a hot chocolate shortage can block them from supporting other teams and their community. This award goes to a team of “BUSY BEAVERS” whose big impact benefits everyone they meet.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder. Not only does this team continue to “RE-PURPOSE” objects in their robot and station, but they have made it their whole theme, including their logo. Who says you can’t teach an old “DOG” new tricks.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: It's no “LIE” when we say this team’s elegantly CNC’d robot had it all from it’s modular swerve drives to it’s flexible intake. They also didn’t “HORSE AROUND” with their fully automatic turret shooter.
This team’s robot is known as a “SUUUUPER” climber. The two-sided ball intake and dual camera system feeds a superior control system.

For their outstanding performance both on an off the field, this team has proven their “FIRST- TIERED” talents again and again. Their innovation and excellence in engineering, control, and quality have made them the “SUPERIOR” choice for this award.

This team gives you more than a “PENNY” for your thoughts when you talk with them. One of the main “ELEMENTS”, of their robot was a completely modular design, not to mention their “FISH TRAP” ball intake.

This team doesn’t let the fact that they are a “WORK IN PROGRESS” hinder their spirit. All team members demonstrated enthusiasm and infectious energy both here and in their community. They prove that “NERDS” really do have more fun!

These scavengers use their autonomous feature to their advantage. With five autonomous options and auto targeting, the competition has nightmares when the harvester of sorrow comes around. These Royal Ravens rule through automation.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: A unique pair of HORNS allow the robot to slide smoothly across the climbing bars. Two balls picked up thru this side or that. The sound from the field is a distinct THUMP THUMP!

Community outreach is a part of their flight plan. They ROSE ABOVE by introducing STEM activities to students that may not have access. They TOOK OFF by inspiring girls to pursue STEM early in life. Their journey is a play on THEIR NUMBER, taking them to the ULTIMATE DESTINATION by igniting passion and demonstrating inclusion. They didn’t have any FREE PIZZA for the judges, but they didn’t need it to impress them. Let’s GO-BABY-GO.

These dedicated students support multiple FLL and FTC teams by mentoring them. Focusing on future seasons the student leaders are advocating for a dedicated building to advance engineering knowledge at all levels. No matter what they ZOO…They ZOO it fast, frequently and forward.

Reaching out to the community and sponsors there is nothing SECRET about this division. From TEAM ORGANIZATION to SCOUTING and everything in between the plan is in place to sustain the team. With a framework in place this teams GOOSE will never be cooked!

Equipped with or without a TURRET is ok. When you tirelessly made all of your parts from detailed CAD drawing and CNC cuttings, then hang all of your hard work on thin poly carb hooks you need to KNOW YOUR LIMITS will all work.

This small squad ROAMS the pits looking to assist teams with programming, wiring and parts. Quicker than a QR SCAN you can learn all you need to about their team members. It is SAFE to say these students are more HUMAN than MACHINE.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: With their bright colors and attractive pit the judges were drawn to it like a MAGNET. They turned up the heat on the competition, but KELVINATOR was CHILL under pressure.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Levitating into the air with hard stops and off the shelf parts, their wizardry turned simplicity into function. This student built team reached into their bag of tricks to design a magical robot!

With variable speeds they are both fast and slow, they keep their eyes on the prize they know where to go. Climbing to the top like CURIOUS GEORGE they can’t be stopped. A sharp shooter like a RANGER puts other teams in danger.
Rise & Aspire Award They are a six-person team, with the reach of EIGHT. Knowledge is BLISS in their vision for growing their team. Even BRUNO is on board with their plans!
The body is solid and the code is clean. Why it is just one tough machine. After a closer “PIKACHU” the judges JAUST knew this DOGE would hunt.
Determination and a “can do” attitude describe these aspiring technicians. As easy as A,B,C, they have ACCEPTED their place in FIRST.
With enthusiasm in the pits and stands, the judges didn’t need a BIRDS EYE view to see their spirit. As their bot soars over the competition field this FORCE roars to life.

This team ROARD to victory with a clever design. Their robot has a fully automated targeting system to speed up their shots and improve their aim. It's no surprise this team's robot has the EYE OF THE TIGER.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: When trouble arose, this team didn't BUTT HEADS. They made a WELCOME addition to their ball intake by creatively adding a common household item. While unconventional, this team has no need to feel SHEEPISH.
This team has strong roots in ALL First programs. They cultivate growth of STEM throughout their school, their community, and Michigan
This team soars above the rest. Through their outreach efforts, they will make more connections than Facebook.

This team's agents secured sponsors and developed relationships in the field. Their efforts in FLL, FTC, and with other FRC teams help recruit top talent for their organization. Their focus on organizational sustainability and the future of FIRST ensure mission success.

After kickoff, this team wasn't DRAGGIN. Before they put pen to paper, they practiced this game by pretending they were the robots. They weren't afraid to feel the burn themselves to get a jumpstart on their design.
This team had a dream to come together without a seam. They collaborated with other teams to keep others learning STEM. Thier impact on surrounding communities gave them this opportunity.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: In the spirit of design, they even made a sign. Engineered to bring inclusion and reduce exclusion.

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Community College Event presented by DTE Foundation
records.script: This team is from a small school but embraced the mission of FIRST by adding a lower school science teacher bringing STEM curriculum to the classroom, instilling the idea that STEM is for everyone. This effort created over 20 new FLL teams. They are very active with FTC, sharing equipment, mentoring an all-girls team, and hosting an FTC Qualifier. They formed partnerships with FRC teams to share build space, supplies and volunteers. This team answered the call to action during the pandemic by making and donating PPE items such as masks and face shields. They host 2-3 blood drives per year. They spread the mission of FIRST to a diverse set of demographics ranging from all girl events, robots at the library and church, presentation to a Native American tribe, and a retirement home. Outreach includes Trunk or treat and donating socks to the Pontiac teen center. This teams MAGIC shows at their school, their community and in everything they do. Not all magicians wear capes, STEM magicians wear safety glasses.

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Community College Event presented by DTE Foundation
records.script: This team really impressed the judges with their extensive outreach within their school district. They’re ready for the big screen having made multiple customizable videos focused on STEM learning. When the marshmallow towers come falling down, this team knows how to roll with the punches.

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Community College Event presented by DTE Foundation
records.script: This cohesive team will always have sparkling passion for FIRST. Team values, leadership training, risk analysis, and strong bonds with sponsors ensure this team has a bright future. This team knows the key to success is a strike of lightening.

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Community College Event presented by DTE Foundation
records.script: This team has a complete cornucopia of capabilities: • Clever cargo color coding, • Crafty collector, • Consistent computer control, • Calibration Camera And they can climb…..(pause)…..Cooool!!

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Community College Event presented by DTE Foundation
records.script: The judges heard and saw all weekend just how gracious these professionals are. The practice of inclusivity inspires the whole community. Their moonbeams for sweet dreams make the thunder roll.

FIM District Macomb Community College Event presented by DTE Foundation

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team built an all-around strong contender. With carefully considered design they angled for the win. A well thought out design kept them from going in circles.

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Community College Event presented by DTE Foundation
records.script: Against strong head winds they kept track for the whole competition. Their sights and sensors complimented the crew’s touch to shoot, move, and climb. You’ll find plenty of innovation in this wheel house.

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Community College Event presented by DTE Foundation
records.script: The Spotlight Award This team illuminates the field with their excitement for robotics. Their rotating drivers impress even NASCAR enthusiasts, constantly bringing new energy to the game. With their dedicated mentors, more stars will rise.

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Community College Event presented by DTE Foundation
records.script: This team can withstand the rigors of space-flight. They were able to build a reliable way to climb high! NASA sure needs more quality engineers like this to reach the inner planets.

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Community College Event presented by DTE Foundation
records.script: This rookie team amazed the judges with their love for the FIRST community, or as they would say, family. They have big plans and are already finding ways to help others, and grow their sponsors. Get ready to see these Eagles fly.

records.eventName: FIM District Macomb Community College Event presented by DTE Foundation
records.script: You can see this team flocking together all around this event. Their interactive pit and flashy headwear exemplify all the spirit they bring. Just so everyone knows, pineapple on pizza is winning.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: This team's decades of knowledge has made them consistent and reliable. Their understanding of field sensing controls and navigation positioned them well for greatness. Their vision guidance system allows them to shoot from any angle with thunderous success.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team impressed us with a complex intake arm that was *blessed by the gods*. Their design allowed them to excel at picking up cargo, effectively *conquering their enemies* with high match scoring. All roads lead to Rome...and the Creativity Award winners!

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: This team was not *poisoned* by the last two year’s pandemic restrictions. They were able to persevere though the difficult times using their *brain* power. During the last 3 years they advanced STEM in their region like no other by funding, constructing, and opening a new STEM center.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: The Engineering Inspiration recipient *hooked* us with their inspirational internship program and rookie handbook. They showed excellent engineering documentation for their iterative climbing design, which helped them *blitz* their way to the traversal rung in matches. This team has risen *Ollie* way to the top!

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: This team *blue* us away with their business plan. The *leadership* in each of their sub-teams shows that they *can drive* themselves into the future. Their success with sponsorships and grants demonstrates *top level* skills and excellent *executive* decision making abilities down to the *atomic* level.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: This team strives to continuously improve their robot. They put their *nerdy* minds together to create a simple, yet effective system to get the job done. Sailing through the competition, these *Polish Vikings* have risen to the top.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: With great power, comes great responsibility and with exceptional performance comes respect for your opponent. This team displayed success in the field and extended a helping hand in the pits. Way to provide a *jolt* to the competition!

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team took this year’s theme to heart by not only thinking about how to accomplish the task today but also considered how they would do it tomorrow. While some might say they went too *rogue* when thinking about the future, we can’t help but marvel at they what they accomplished at home.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The Industrial Design winners made us *green with envy* of their clever, holistic design. They *spiked* to the top of the competition with a consistent auton routine, accurate, rapid shooting, and *lightning* quick climbing. This team leads the *charge* in team aesthetics and overall performance in the game challenge.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: This team controlled the competition with their *vision*on the field with multiple autonomous options to *soar* from the starting line. Their automation conquered obstacles in the field with the accuracy of a *falcon* striking its prey. Their out of the box *free* thinking has *landed* them much success on the playing field.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: Like Gilligan, this team has overcome numerous obstacles to be present at today’s event. They chewed up old parts to refabricate mechanisms in this year’s robot. They rebuilt their lodge from the ground up after the pandemic and preserved despite the small size of their colony.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: This team displayed its clean and compact design while holding up to the rigors of battle. Their *red armour* defends the blows on the field with weapons of deadly accuracy in defending the *empire*. The *Duke* would be honored to use the force in collecting this team's *bounty*.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: This team’s strong connection with their school and mentors has helped lubricate their team’s start and get it pumped up for the future. There was some heartbreak when a team in their area disbanded, but this team pleasantly surprised everyone and restarted their climb up Mount FIRST.

records.eventName: FIM District Midland Event presented by Dow
records.script: This team has *ascended* from the competition with their unparalleled enthusiasm. Their *coral* and *cerulean* clad fans infused the arena with their *warrior spirit*. Everyone, please *rise* for this team!

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Proving Grounds
records.script: This teams’ autonomous capability makes scoring points basically SECOND NATURE. Their auto-ball reject, their auto-travel to balls, and their consistent autonomous shooting allowed them to LEAP to the top of the standings. With MOVES LIKE JAGTAP, the Autonomous Award goes to…

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Proving Grounds

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Proving Grounds
records.script: Today we recognize a truly inspiring team with extensive contributions in developing the local, state, national & global STEM community. They are a FIRST CONSTANT with their influence in advocacy, education & funding programs. Established, structured, and never IRRATIONAL, the team has come FULL CIRCLE. This team is credited with their involvement at the Michigan Advocacy Conference and is one of the five teams which created the Student Association for STEM advocacy. Additionally, they host and run the annual FLL district qualifier in their community. Freshmen learn, Sophomores do, Junior's lead, Seniors teach. It’s a winning formula for success with INFINITE POSSIBILITIES.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Proving Grounds
records.script: PROCESSING INFORMATION is key to this team’s outstanding success in advancing engineering within their community. Like a LIGHT BULB turning on, this team’s ideas are implemented in the community with lunch-and-learns for senior citizens, free summer camps, FTC mind over matter, and a newly opened STEM center. These BRAINIACS use their MATTER to inspire passion for engineering.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Proving Grounds
records.script: This team doesn’t just sit around hoping to be LUCKY at competitions. They strategize, work hard, and execute their well detailed business plan resulting in a strong balance sheet. WE BELIEVE the team can accomplish anything including influencing the CULTURE at their school. Their marketing approach goes far beyond the internet and touches people directly by conducting community events which is no SHAM.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Proving Grounds
records.script: Proudly wearing PLAID this team cruises down the Pacific Coast Highway. From concept selection to requirement definition to weight management, this team is a CONQUERING power. They are not green with envy but ORANGE with VENOM.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Proving Grounds
records.script: This team graciously and professionally MINES others to emulate its SPARKLING behavior. Working together on and off the field, this BRIGHT team mentored others, created a coloring book for kids and actively promoted recycling. Shining brightly in RED, congratulations to this GEM of a team.

FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Proving Grounds

records.script: The intake on the MYTHICAL robot illustrates the teams’ attention to detail. From their FLASHY attire, theme and spirit it IGNITES a FLAME of FIRE for STEM and FIRST. Their LAIRs appearance and coordinated robot and cart make many GREEN with envy but not these DRAGONS.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Proving Grounds
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This electrifying robot was designed using with a clear VISION of how to prioritize and interpolate the perfect shooting ARC with fast scoring and accuracy. They executed their robot from concept to design, STORMING out ideas that led to their modular system design. They NULL and VOIDED the competition.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Proving Grounds
records.script: This TECHNICALLY sound robot shot its way up the leader board. With automatic ranging and impressive shooter design, this team overcame the DIFFICULTY of the game. Watching KEITH play will put a SMILE on your face.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Proving Grounds
records.script: Award for Continued Excellence Keeping BOTH EYES on their core values and competitive spirit puts this team above the rest. After their past success they continue FLYING HIGH and reaffirm their HALL OF FAME status. These MECHANICAL AVIANS impress judges year after year.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Proving Grounds
records.script: This teams’ opponents tend to break out in sweats. Using their outstanding engineering skills to achieve precise fit and finish gave them ELEVATED consistency and repeatability on the field of battle. These HEROS have been observed kicking tires and lighting fires on the road to a brighter tomorrow.

records.eventName: FIM District Milford Event presented by GM Proving Grounds

The atmosphere this team has created was hard to ignore with their cohesive uniforms, mascot, and enthusiastic cheering, but don’t worry they won’t BYTE. From PPE to first aid to custom awards this spirited team was also more than willing to share their POT OF GOLD.
