records.eventName: FIM District Walled Lake Event presented by Magna
records.script: This team has developed a robust pipeline of over 20 FLL and FTC teams, donating 10% of their budget and over 700 student mentoring hours, to helping those teams thrive. Through parades, summer camps, science expos, festivals, and national advocacy conferences, they’ve promoted STEM and FIRST awareness at 70 events, contributing over 3,000 outreach hours. This team has co-hosted 9 FIRST-related events totaling over 2,000 volunteer hours. Their sustainability efforts have grown to include one team in every school in their district, enabling for a 200% increase in FIRST participation. They’re certainly not DRAGGIN’ in their enthusiasm for STEM! To quote this team, “A community is only as strong as those who engage it”. This team has prepared monthly meals for those in needs, adopted a portion of a local trail, and designed and fitted a wheelchair attachment. Their efforts were recognized by our state senator with a local community service award. They are truly em-POWER-ing their community! In conclusion, even during sporting events, this teams’ number is chanted by adoring fans! They’ve really ignited a FIRE, big enough to be seen across THE LAKE! Congratulations, Team number 302, The Dragons!

This team’s SINGULAR goal is to be inclusive to everyone, and their actions have resulted in a PLURALITY of data and information sharing to the community. Congratulations, Team number 5066, Singularity!

records.script: When the chips were down, this team merged to come back stronger. They are carving a path through the snow while making sure no oil gets spilled on the field. Congratulations, Team number 8873, Rockefeller Robotics!

records.eventName: FIM District Walled Lake Event presented by Magna
records.script: The robot may be their LAST HOPE, but this team has CONQUERED this award. Their infectious spirit and playful sense of humor has proven to these judges they are a TEAM SPIRIT ARMY to be reckoned with. A FLOCK of PINK FLAMINGOS may be their mascot. “WHY NOT” would be their reply if you asked. Congratulations, Team number 5048, Spartronics!

Bringing a raiding mentality to self-driving effectiveness, this team was abundant at pillaging points during the first 15 seconds. Perhaps they will apply their skills to the long ships of future transportation.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s strategic use of light weight materials, symmetrical design, and cargo intake will leave you BLUE with envy when you battle their creativity.

All the teams that submit for the Chairman’s Award have extremely impressive accomplishments! Wonderful impact by all of them on their FLL and FTC feeder systems and community – it was a difficult and close decision. This Chairman’s team’s presentation to the judges was flawless, well-practiced, enthusiastic, and engaging. The award criteria of “Spreading the FIRST Mission”, “Impact on the FIRST Community”, and “Inspiring the STEM Future” were systematically documented and well discussed. The judges also greatly appreciated the submission of the “Chairman’s Documentation Form”. Facts matter. Their promotion of FIRST and STEM can be seen through school spirit, community outreach, and far beyond just face-to-face. Through social media, they communicate to sponsors, alumni, and future students and reach teams around the world! You may want to brush up on your foreign languages!! This team has expanded its community outreach and engaged fellow FIRST and STEM enthusiasts from many other countries including Niger, Tanzania, Tunisia, Comoros, Namibia, Brazil, Norway, Iceland, and Romania. They even sent 50 books to expand the library of a small island country off the east coast of Africa!! There’s such a focus on global outreach that “EGR” has been rebranded as “Excellence in Global Outreach”!

This team’s passion and commitment shines through as a powerful inspiration to their community by combining robotics with outreach. You need a rotary and a librarian to catalogue all of their demonstrations, activities and events across multiple areas and school districts.

This team developed a business plan that leverages its long history in FIRST and manages risk to prevent tales of WOE. The marketing plan makes sure their BOT is a familiar face at LEGO camps, parades, relay for life and the wings of mercy.
This robot can climb better than Tarzan through the trees! It showed consistent performance and execution in the climb. “Julianne Lyn” enjoyed the swing on the top bar and wins Engineering Gold!
This team “meshed” with another, “PURR-fected” a “wireless” scouting tool, then graciously shared stats and code design with other cool cats.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Keeping with the 2021-2022 season theme focusing on the future of transportation. This SPICY team shows off their image highlighting travel and flight. Cayenne, jalapeno, serrano, RED HOT CHILI!

records.script: While most teams avoid tipping, this team excels through tipping, flipping, and kicking. With a tower that tips to allow easy access for maintenance, a shooter that flips to allow shooting from both front and back, and a mechanism that kicks out opponent’s cargo, this team rocks.

This team exemplifies the saying, “If at first you don’t succeed, try, try again”. Quality is this team’s “Job-1” with iterative prototyping to improve the quality of their robot. Their attention to design documentation releases and control, and robustness in design and materials make this team a quality standard-bearer.
We commend this team for continuous improvement with effective goal setting after every match. Talking to their team was truly inspiring! This team is going places!

This team fosters an enthusiastic spirit in their community and was a source of light in the stands at this competition. As they loudly cheer everyone on, they create a tornado of energy to further the FIRST mission. Their constructive form of chaos consistently unifies an awesome group of mentors, students and sponsors.

records.script: This team celebrates creativity that enhances the strategy of play. They CRUSHED the risk of failure by developing a graceful intake / delivery mechanism. Their Betsy ensured proper payload with a high degree of Vitamin C. Congratulation Team 5531 - Orange Crush from Dearborn.

records.eventName: FIM District Woodhaven Event presented by Ford
records.script: This team has made it a priority to promote diversity and inclusion within a small community resulting in a 1 to 1 ratio of girls to boys. The Covid pandemic did not stop them from positively impacting their community through providing safety glasses and masks to front line workers. They fully understand the future of FIRST lies with the youth, so they mentor FLL teams and host robotics summer camps for elementary school children. They promote the ideals of FIRST through their involvement with DADARA and participated in Detroit Maker Faire putting their sponsors in the spotlight and showing their tremendous appreciation. This team never forgets the end game is fun, so they spend time with other FRC teams on and off the coopertition floor. Their success has not gone unnoticed, as their school now pays registration fees for any FIRST teams in the district. Rising from the ashes, this team rebuilt itself with STRONG BONES fortified in sibling rivalry. This rivalry does not hold them back, rather it DRIVES and FEEDS their success. Their impact can be felt from Detroit and Downriver, to the Covid frontlines, across the open FIELDS of Asia. They use their wisdom to NOURISH young robotic minds in the summer heat and help them PASTUERIZE all obstacles. By MOOOVING the crowd at Detroit Maker Faire, they look to CORRAL sponsorships for future RUNS. These BOVINE are too busy to TIP, but always happy to share Spanish desserts with fellow teams. The MOM and her CALF have already claimed the blue ribbon and best in show, please join us in congratulating the rest of the HERD, Team 5050 Cow Town Robotics.

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: This year the team who best exemplifies gracious professionalism is one whose focus all season has been on creating and sustaining a welcoming and supportive community - both within their own team and in the robotics community at large. They invested time in building their robot and equal time building their team. For this exemplary group, it doesn’t matter if you’re from across the street or across the globe, because it isn’t just about the robots for teams that practice gracious professionalism, it’s about the people who love them. From their bright yellow bucket hats to their friendly duckie mascot, the winner of this year’s Gracious Professionalism Award is Team 2264 Trojan Robotics.

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team put a lot of effort into rebranding with a new website, social media, logo, and branded guide. Their creative imagery 'dominated the sport' and held the judges’ attention. Success was just in the cards. Congratulations to Team 7850, CARDS!

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team clearly did their pushups and chin-ups, because their design was strong and sturdy. Each part blazed as bright as the team color, from elegant controls and efficient climbing to a star example of an electrical system. This team’s industrial design made them an animal on the field. Congratulations to Team 2202, BEAST Robotics!

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: Early in the season this team decided they needed to make changes so their robot can follow its own path. Software was modified to make this task easier for all. Now this team's robot can tell what is blue and what is red, and it even knows all its shapes! So, the deed is done...there is northern lightening on the field of play. Congratulations Team 3018, Nordic Storm from Saint Peter, Minnesota.

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: This team was very deliberate and organized in all activities from securing several new sponsors, partnering with charitable groups, managing tasks, and devising a new strategy. Their primary emphasis on people and the overall experience also resulted in a nice, simple robot that can move and spin at the same time!! Congratulations to Team 4624, Rebel Alliance!

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: From start to finish you emphasized quality, your single mechanism climber was a real priority. Wearing hard hats after getting concussed, you built a bot awesomely robust. With ‘design, prototype, fabricate, test, and then iterate’, quality can never wait… Not even a ‘second’-bot for the ‘Minute’-bots. Congratulations MinuteBots-4536…Best in Quality 2022!

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: Once upon a time from a heartland CITY came a robot built by kids that were GRITTY. It was a LEAN, MEAN, scoring MACHINE; one of the best on the RAPID REACT SCENE. MORE THAN ROBOTS was their THEME, which is the force that really drove the TEAM. From CODING, to COVID, to the CORN DOG CLASSIC, Kenton’s Kids have always been PRAGMATIC. This year’s winners aren’t bumps on a LOG, they’re the Hawkeye State’s Team 525 SWARTDOGS!

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: This team WOWed the judges through their outreach presentation. They had 29 STEM outreach events over the past year where they taught more than 4,600 students engineering principles by engaging them with their hands-on robotics programs. They taught 126 elementary school teachers how to program their NAO robot and even helped to get more than 200 senior citizens active with their Obie game system. Congratulations to Team 6420, Fire Island Robotics!

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: While this rookie team has big dreams for 2022 and the future, It knows success comes from hard work and careful planning. Prototyping, a sound business plan, and root cause analyses Are all part of their strong foundation. While they spread the FIRST message in their school and beyond, We're all Wired Up imagining how far this team will go! Congratulations to Rookie All Stars, Team 8516.

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: FIRST Robotics teams inspire one another to get better and better every year. When a rookie team inspires others, it is because its members are committed, creative, and enthusiastic in ways that let their admiration and respect for engineering and engineers shine through. The winner of this year's Rookie Inspiration award hit a bullseye with the judges when they presented a team that worked overtime to find sponsors in their community, applied for and received grant money, and still plan to hold a community event after the competition season is over. This team, and their beloved coach, are a wonderful example of joyful optimism and a real inspiration for the teams who will come after them. This year's Rookie Inspiration Award goes to Team 8878 The Arrowbots.

records.eventName: Minnesota 10,000 Lakes Regional presented by Medtronic
records.script: In the stands, you can’t miss this team’s blazing color and stylish flairs, and as the countdown starts, a fury-suit driver is focused and prepares. records.script: Su robot combina sistema de visión con programación avanzada de trayectoria, logrando con esto poder lanzar desde cualquier posición de la cancha, haciendo su desempeño más eficiente y preciso.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Mediante la implementación de poleas, lograron optimizar de forma eficiente el torque de los motores para tomar y lanzar el cargo de una manera simple y eficiente

El equipo comprendió y puso en práctica su plan de negocios con gran eficacia trascendiendo más alla de las fronteras de su institución, logrando que el robot, y el espíritu de FIRST sea también de sus comunidades involucrando las bondades y beneficios de la ciencia el bien vivir y el bien estar con el otro.

Este equipo plasma sus años de experiencia en el diseño, programación, operación y documentación de su proyecto, buscando dejar huella de generación en generación. Tanto en los pits como en la cancha, maximizan sus recursos buscando equilibrar la forma y la función para el logro de sus objetivos.
Acalorados pero entusiasmados de compartir conocimientos, herramientas y mucha diversión, llegan desde el lugar de la arena y la sal……… y no es la playa, para recibir este reconocimiento;

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Este equipo norteño destacó con su diseño asimétrico, funcional y a la vez eficiente. Cada parte, con sus funciones específicas y diseñadas de forma adecuada, lograron resaltar su espíritu felino.

Siempre se basaron en los QUE'S de su robot. Innovando en el control de su tiro por medio de un servomotor, su tracción de doble velocidad cambiada por piston y el intake doble para mayor posibilidad de anotación.

El ganador de este premio demostró su gran pasión por la robótica. Por su estructura de proyectos sociales, son un ejemplo de como la juventud puedes desarrollar a su comunidad a través de la ciencia y la tecnología. Sin duda este equipo sabe que ganar no lo es todo, por eso estamos seguros que sus integrantes llevarán el nombre de México muy alto.

Desde tierras tapatias, demostrando robustes en su diseño, aplicando protecciones a todos sus sistemas y asegurando con limitswitch su agarre. Ustedes... 6602, Arcadia, se llevan el premio de calidad.

Es un equipo destacado que se ha mantenido competitivo durante muchos años. Tienen su propia metodología para garantizar que su éxito sea transmitido de generación en generación. La pandemia no los detuvo, se dedicaron a fabricar caretas, dieron apoyo en línea a muchos equipos y ayudaron a sanitizar de manera automatizada a la Laguna, entre otras actividades. Se sienten orgullosos de resaltar la importancia que tiene para ellos el trabajo y la participación de todos, ya que esto es lo que los hace un equipo fuerte. Su pasión, orgullo y su historia los han llevado a grandes logros y este será unis mas para enriquecer su gran trayectoria Ahora requerirán de una maleta adicional de las que llevaron a su presentación para su viaje al mundial

Por su capacidad de adaptación y su compromiso durante tiempos complicados en la pandemia, no sólo inspirando sino materializando ese esfuerzo en resultados tangibles con equipos semilla en las ligas FLL y FRC, a través de programas de mentoria. Así como brindar apoyo social a comunidades vulnerables como personas con débilidad visual y adultos mayores con Alzhainer. Gracias por ser inspiración... Fly higher!
Renovados y entusiastas, surgen de debajo de las piedras como el alacrán que representa su tierra, hicieron resurgir la filosofía de FIRST en su comunidad.
Este premio lo recibe un equipo que hace honor a su corrido, donde las personas tienen decisión, unidos y entusiastas llegaron a ganar en esta bella región.
Viajaron hasta La Laguna para vencer el desierto como un Corcel invisible demostrando su entusiasmo, compañerismo y trabajo en equipo. Nos complace presentarles a los ganadores de este premio
While others wondered what to do, this Bot went to work. With a mind of its own, it gobbled cargo and shot at will. They rolled through the first 15 seconds with ease.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team’s design helped them climb the ladder. They welcome ROS as a friend to make them move and rise to the front of the herd. They are a stripe above.

This team has soared over the seas, spreading its wings across FLL, FTC, and FRC, starting and mentoring teams and hosting competitions. Their diversity reaches boys and girls, backyard and streets, impacting people from kindergarten to college. At cruising altitude, they brought maker carts down the aisle and delivered a booty of treasure, ensuring their community outreach is “sky high”. Welcome aboard Flight 2642!

This team started as an ember and became a blazing fire. They reached out to thousands of students and even shared their drive team when asked. Their inspiration of the community to get interested in Engineering is sizzling!
This team has a business plan Silicon Valley or the Himalayas would envy. Comprehensive and clear, it covered all the bases. They embody entrepreneurship.
Ironically, this team lit up the scoreboard with their bot. They can spin their approach to building a great shooter. The Excellence in Engineering award should be a bright spot for this team.

This team’s tines, or members, fly in all different directions and are quite multifunctional. They scoop up all the other teams to help out however they can. Gracious Professionalism, catch-all for the ethos of FIRST, is exemplified by this team, the catchall of silverware.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: They bring others in with symbols from the past…way past. Their carnivorous social media, pit design, uniforms, and team theme ingest the competition. There’s no escaping this prehistoric image!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: The call went out for a Rapid Reaction. This team swooped in with redundant systems to make the delivery. These birds came to play!
When it was time for the limelight, this team embraces the lime. They closed the loop on their controls and on their competitors. Their PID controller will always take them Ohm…
This team came to play by air and water. A few warm bodies was all it took to inspire and design a competitive machine. In the end, the venomous mammal caught the judges’ eyes.

Of all the umm…unconventional things we’ve seen this weekend… One team had a hallmark visible in their work. Shooting for the hat-trick of flexibility, robustness, and competitiveness…that’s not just strange, it’s…
From the start, they opened their house to others. They indexed every move of their robot. Software went with minimal glitches.
The city of Charlotte just got a little louder. Competing for the first year and showing new students that they can fly higher with STEM. They’re sure to energize a new generation of rookies.

Not only is this team sharp, but they showcased their athleticism by jumping to new heights! All the other animals in the pond know exactly who they are. Their ability to hop onto a new theme this season ensured that this army of frogs gets to wear the Team Spirit crown!

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.script: This team has come a long way from their old automated VACUUM to building a top-rated automated robot. Their limelight-based SHOOTER ensures accuracy, consistency and high scores. Their STRENGTH-TO-WEIGHT ratio is GREEAATT all the way down to their WHISKERS.

records.eventName: FIRST North Carolina District State Championship
records.script: This team was born in the DARK FOREST of North Carolina. Their robot can see 360 degrees, faster cycle time with more than 90% shooting efficiency. They “WORK HARD AND PLAY HARD”.

records.script: Their hearty team spirit BLOWS OVER other teams like a GALE. BATTEN DOWN THE HATCHES when this team pulls into PORT. YO HO HO, a FIRST life is for this team.

records.script: This team really sprang into creative solutions. Their design approach is something you can take to the bank. This award goes to the Team who’s climbing approach is like their name, a series of irreversible steps.

In true entrepreneurial fashion, this is a team clearly run by the students. They focus on, and exemplify, the mission and goals of the FRC. As entrepreneurs, they recruit through, fundraise for, and innovate with their machine all in concert with a 3D printer made to build parts for battle tanks. Let’s hear it for the entrepreneurial Mighty Morphing Banana Slugs, and their robot: ‘the Father Archduke “A-Slug-Us-Gloop” Esquire, CPA.’

From the frigid north come a team with a strong engineering mindset. Speed, accuracy and control were engineered into a robust, elegant robot that ate the competition. They are the team that engineered a killer machine.
With a fiery passion this team believes in helping out their neighbor And that keeping the venue clean is key. When asked for help, this team brought the heat.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team has displayed a pattern of excellence. In a world full of stripes, they’re bold enough to be plaid. When it comes to the competition, they KILT it.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Many teams made a robot, this team took the time to design a robot. When it broke, it was repaired in short time, getting them back in the game to compete and win. They are by design the droids for the award.
This squad came together with a common aim. Using several sensors to onto their target with precision. This award goes to an innovative troop.
With a wide wingspan, this team embraces inclusion. Despite their name, this team is ERROR free.
A high-quality design from the Minnesota Lakes Area. They continuously are improving their robots quality and performance. All patriots stand up and salute.

This is a team that avoids building bridges to nowhere. They build bridges with a purpose and destination in mind. The journey this team has been on exemplifies community and inclusion as they build on their heritage and inspire others. With their final destination in mind, their impact is enduring as they embrace a new brand and team culture. This is a team without borders!!
In a relentless pursuit to spread the spirit of engineering. This team is an inspiration to the community. A coalition with a mission to tell the world the value of FIRST.

Like a baby bird learning to fly, this rookie team soared to a new challenge. They exemplified the values of first through their community involvement, school activities, vision and spirit. This baby bird is on fire!!!

Despite arriving to battle with only their armor. This squad of gallant knights braved the field and fought fearlessly. They quickly forged relationships with allies and their efforts are well worth watching.
More than just a cool outfit. This team spreads their enthusiasm in their school and their community Their chilly dance blew us a way.

records.awardName: District Championship Rookie All Star Award

records.script: As most teams did during the pandemic this team had to change their trajectory and adjust to the new world. They helped their community with printing face shields and ear savers and sewing masks. They have a unique system to rate each members leadership capabilities to select the best leaders. They measure success by the number of people whose lives they help to improve including those at the local women’s shelter. They have started and continue to support FLL and FRC Teams in their area. These tigers assist GirlUp and Girls Who Code.

This team lost their workspace during the pandemic due to their sponsor needing it back. While searching for a new workspace they focused on outreach to spread the message of FIRST and weathering the storm. They have designed a course to teach new students and new teams the fundamentals of FIRST. They're also heavily involved in FLL and FLL Jr teams and cultivating the future of FIRST. Have you heard of STEAMSplash? Then you've heard of Team 5422 The Stormgears of Westford Massachusetts.

This team’s inclusive recruitment strategy has allowed them to develop a robust FIRST pipeline that extends their local community. Their extensive community outreach efforts are worthy of both confetti and fame. When spreading the community of FIRST, this team never AIRs on the side of caution, but gives their full focus to teaching through competitive robotics.

This team impressed the judges with both the extent and measurable effectiveness in their community outreach and furthering of STEM education. They have a pipeline that starts with community, they educate the community about STEM and FIRST, and bring students into FIRST. They have strong partnerships with their sponsors, not only have multiple alumni gone to work with several sponsors and come back as mentors, but when some sponsors have had real problems (like a broken 3D printer, or production line issues) this team has stepped up to give back and work the sponsors to overcome.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Calcium Division
records.script: This team does not miss a single angle on the field. Through use of their two limelight cameras their autonomous mode is ready and waiting to detect six balls near their presence. It goes without saying that this team is ready to rumble.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Calcium Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team make the others green with envy. With the wizardry of fusing two mechanisms in one, they have elevated the competition to a new level.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Calcium Division
records.script: This team has created a strong bond within their school for almost ten years. Through their grants they’ve not only been able to support their own team, but their philanthropy has helped start many FIRST teams in Massachusetts. Their solid business plan that is truly focused on sustainability of their team and others is out of this world!

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Calcium Division
records.script: Using the KISS principle, this team can remove any subsystem with just eight bolts. A cross functional review process and parametric design, it enabled them to pass on their legacy to other teams and adapt to any situation. You will not find a better engineered robot if you looked to the north or the south.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Calcium Division
records.script: This team exhibits Gracious Professionalism both on and off the field. In their own community, they demonstrate FIRST core values by expanding their STEM Programs in Elementary Schools and encouraging their students to mentor and support other FIRST Programs. Whether it is in the US or Africa, this team wants FIRST to be heard around the world. They truly take FIRST to the Max!!

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Calcium Division
New England FIRST District Championship - Calcium Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: From the pit to the robot to the stands you’ll always know where this team is. Their red and gold flames bring the fire to the field and makes the phoenix rise from the ashes.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Calcium Division
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With dogged termination this team never stops looking for ways to improve their robot. The smallest detail is not left to chance, they are able to see the tree through the forest.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Calcium Division
records.script: A completely modular code, this team soared above the completion. Flowcharting, graphing, and frequency synchronization made this team a predator on and off the field.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Calcium Division
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their tight inclusive community. Their attention to the mental health of their members and the safe space they have created touch many. Their motto of “One-Team” will keep their mojo going for many years.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Calcium Division
records.script: Fast on its feet, this robot can sink shots looking over its shoulder. A solid design process, smart use of sensors and programming, and rugged construction helped this team achieve a 95% shooting success rate. Not only that, they can claw their way to the top in under 5 second.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Calcium Division
records.script: This rookie ream stood out amongst the crowd. They take their robotic skills beyond the competition fields and into their local communities. Whether it’s making a robot to scare the crows, plant flowers, or save Halloween, 4H will never be the same.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Calcium Division
records.script: Spirit takes many forms. Is it an urban legend or a true story? Did a sleeping student wake up during a brainstorming session, yell a name and go back to sleep? Perhaps we’ll never know, but one thing we do know is the legend that is Bob.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Titanium Division
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their consistent hub scoring both in autonomous mode and throughout teleop. They clearly explained how the robot will react to interference and overcome. Their auto-targeting turret, makes shooting from anywhere on the field as easy as pie.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Titanium Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: The creative use of all three laws of physics; 1. Intake, 2. Shoot, 3. Climb, were impressive to the judges. However, skipping steps during law 3 calculation was a surprising twist that clearly yielded RP acceleration. TEAMS! Remember to turn off all personal hotspots! Have no fear, this team will provide free WiFi!

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Titanium Division
records.script: While making decisions to continue their legacy, this team prioritizes strong relations with their sponsors, from small businesses to large corporations. They cut to the point with budgets and reason, shoring up their shop for their competition season. They race all around town, showing appreciation, consistently spreading their checkered flag nation.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Titanium Division
records.script: The yellow blur commanded the arena today and for years stretching back to thirty. Some would call the path a journey, some would better call it a crusade.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Titanium Division
records.script: This team’s mission is to spread FIRST’s core values across Western Maine. This year, the team welcomed students from a nearby school that could no longer support their FIRST team. They are hoping their active bill to fund Main FIRST programs passes….. the judges “R2”.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Titanium Division
New England FIRST District Championship - Titanium Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team displays outstanding aesthetic integration on their robot and team appearance. From purple jackets to purple hats and even purple shoes laces, the team wears their colors with pride. Not only do they show their colors in their apparel and pits, but they are able to explain the significance behind their purple colors and owl mascot.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Titanium Division
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This teams robot was elegant in all forms and functions. From the consistency of their autonomous program to the reliability of their climber, this robot shined on the field with their color coordinated powder coating, proving that they truly do rule the sky!

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Titanium Division
records.script: This team implemented a machine learning pipeline for a ZED camera and tamed their differential swerve drivetrain. They were able to “lay out” their process of designing their control system very clearly to the judges, catapulting themselves to the top.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Titanium Division
records.script: Fish don’t fry in the kitchen and beans don’t burn on the grill You can’t sell tickets to tour around, unless you climb up that hill. Healthy communication for you and me, maybe, there ain’t nothing wrong with that. So we clean the pond up with robots and lift up FLL teams…… To the SKY … I ….. i…

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Titanium Division
records.script: After a furious fall, this team went buck to the drawing board. Their iterative designs paid off, with repairable and durable subsystems. You won’t want to face this team’s wrath.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Titanium Division
records.script: With guidance from Waterbury and Wilby, this school turned around and embarked on their FIRST journey. Consistently being an asset to their alliance with their robot “Tyrone”. It is certain we have not seen the last of this team.

records.eventName: New England FIRST District Championship - Titanium Division
records.script: It is honorable the dedication and commitment that this team has put in towards this competition season. This small team is passionate and engaged. This team celebrates every win and adds a weeble to their bot in recognition of the win.

This team works hard to get more young women involved in STEM and bakes for veterans. This team is actively analyzing how to improve their team and their feeder system. The team has restarted their summer STEM camp. This team has helped make a virtual FCC competition for use in the COVID environment. Congratulations to Team 467 - The Colonials.

The team is advocating state legislators for continued robotics grants to public schools. With a focus on combining STEM excellence with mental health awareness, diversity and social justice, Team 6328 - Mechanical Advantage is awarded the Engineering Inspiration Award.

This team had an infusion of 8th grade students last year and quadrupled in size. The students operate the team as a small business and they have a solid business plan to back it up. They make a point to create safe and inclusive spaces for their members. The Entrepreneurship Award is presented to FRC Team 4909 – Bionics

This team set clear goals for fast cycles and quick climbs. Through their iterative and robust design process they recalculated their robot's trajectory and hopped their way to the top of the field. Congratulations!

This team arrived like a tsunami of sportsmanship and kindness. They displayed a wave of support for all their competitors. They continually demonstrated professionalism in the pits and the arena. The winner of the Gracious Professionalism award is Team 1721, Tidal Force.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: With an ever improving logo, this small team wears their design on their back. Their use of laser etched polycarbonate panels is the “Mane” event. The Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen is presented to FRC Team 8013 the Boston Lions.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This decorated robot swerved around the field to victory. Their agility and towering presence catches the eye of predators. They caused an uproar for Industrial Design. Congratulations to Team 131 - CHAOS.
No one can keep this team under control. Calculation in the simulator made driving a breeze. The Innovation in Control Award goes to team 7407 - The Wired Boars.

A team that came in like a hurricane! A force to be reckoned with in the areas of design force and innovation. The judges were blown away with their commitment to community outreach and involvement. The Judges' Award "Jack of All Trades, Master of Fun" goes to Team 126 - Gael Force.

This team developed a resource focused build plan and swung into action; however, you may have noticed their robot doesn't. With a well-constructed climber and intake, this team would up wowing the judges with the quality of their robot.

This team's heart, their robot's height, Halloween celebration and hunger for success prove that being a new team doesn't have to be overly complicated. The Rookie All Star award goes to Team 8708 - Overly Komplex

Unexpected challenges are always part of FIRST, but this team's rookie robot "blue" us away with its performance. This rookie inspiration award is for the team that came through adversity to cause new Mayhem.

This team flew in like a collection of friendly birds. A team as colorful in personality as the hats they wear. A flock that demonstrated a high level of pride and commitment. The winner of the Team Spirit Award is Team 811 - Wild Cards.
Let's chat about a robot that sees in blues, reds and always in green. Acting alone, but getting a good boost from Ernie, a childhood friend. Congrats to BERT, Team 133.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: They created this robot intentionally a sweep and shot, so professionally with a unique design and strategy divine. Congrats to S.R.T.C Anomaly, Team 3451.

This veteran team lives free or dies for their FIRST STEM celebration. They work with local businesses to fund raise in a unique way. They 3D printed PPE for their teachers and school staff. We will circle back to this team 2027 to determine if they completed their 5 year plan. This team is reaching out internationally to start FRC teams. Parabens to Team 166, CHOP SHOP.

This team's leadership structure has a vision for the future. With strong business planning, creative fundraising, community outreach, and making safety a priority, this crew's robot will always float you a beer, root beer, of course. Congrats to Team 6153, the Blue Crew.

This diverse team has a comprehensive business plan that provides for current and future financial stability. There is no slacking on this well-organized team as it is completely student led and run. From their active recruiting to their grant writing camp, this team has rocketed to a bright future. Congrats Team 4761, the Robockets.

With hooks slashing forwards and backwards, a purple and green beast took to the field. Its shorter stature was engineered to withstand all manners of mayhem and wrath. Congrats Team 6329, Bucks' Wrath.

This team strived to help both on and off the field. They flew in wherever needed, in the machine shop and on the grill. Thanks to their support, the concessions were devilishly good. Congrats to Team 6324, the Blue Devils.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: When it comes to FRC, teams strive to have themselves and their robot and their pits look the best. Thought and effort drives this team to fully integrate their theme in everything they do. Rounding the corner as they near the finish line and flags flying high. A cohesive and vibrant look from their hair to their nails, LED and spirit. This team easily outpaced the others with their checkerboard appeal. Congrats to Team 172, Northern Force.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team leads the way in both robustness and aesthetics even if they had to bend a few hooks to get there. Make sure you paint the new one yellow. Congrats to Team 238, the Crusaders.

This winning team impressed the judges with their automatically targeting shooter and their ability to change their robots behavior as they gathered cargo. Thanks to their Nav-X system, they always know their location on the field. In spite of their team name, this robot is always well controlled. Congrats to Team 131, CHAOS.

Close only counts in horseshoes. A runner up time and time again would make most teams turn red. Their accomplishments got them through the storm, and these cape wearing heroes saved the day. Congrats to Team 509, Red Storm.

This team impressed the judges with their quality workmanship and balance of robustness and base of repair. Throughout the event as they were making improvements they maintained a focus on risk mitigation to withstand the rigors of competition. They proudly display their sponsors on fictional shields which protect their intake system. Congrats to Team 4564, Orange Chaos.

This team was spirited on the field, in the pits, in the stands, and with all the volunteers at the event. Even their remote members did not fall flat. It was clear to the judges that this team was an easy prospect for this award. Congrats to Team 319, Big Bad Bob.

records.script: This team’s autonomous self-guidance was observed throughout match play. By employing 9 sensors during end game, this ‘bucking bronco’ makes a 4-bar traverse both elegant and highly reliable.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team was most creative in their shooter design. Always out of their den, showcasing their performance, direction doesn’t matter for their agile bot as they shoot in both directions.

Whether big or little, this team works together to have a large impact on their community through various initiatives like mentoring other FIRST teams, organizaing food drives and various STEM camps. All teams can follow this team’s compass to learn from the past, work in the present, and SOAR towards the future.

This team wisely advances the mission of FIRST through many new initiatives. Holding all team members accountable, their reach spans from local fairs to congress. Coming through the Hills, these Raiders are here to help.

Turning a weakness into a strength, this team recognizes the importance of sponsors. Planting their flag at a new space, they turned their home into an opportunity. This team knows that a good business plan is the best suit of armor.

Eyes set on the upper hub, this team diligently tested multiple wheel profiles to improve their shooter’s aim. With a professional eye, the team kept iterating their simple design until it was perfectly tuned. The judges were impressed each time the team took to the field to demonstrate their newfound SPIKE in performance.

Instead of bringing competition to the field, this team brought a field to the competition. Opening their doors to numerous teams, they go all out to support their FIRST community. This team really ROCKS the competition.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: With a cohesive color scheme through the team, this team’s stripes show off their bold appearance. From machine to uniform, this team swims through the competition with style.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Bringing the heat to this competition, this team’s wheels leave SEARING marks. Their design featured rigidity and robustness with hot-swappable components. Burning the competition away, even this team's pants caught fire.

When looking to control the field, this team really knows how to excel. These Robos combined advanced sensor usage and complex math to shoot and climb very well It’s no question, when it comes to controlling their robot, these warriors are swell.

This team’s enthusiasm is contagious, and their 3D printing is unique. As they sail the competition seas, they find treasure in the hunt for team funding. This team is truly a rising star in the Judge’s eyes. The Judge's Rising Star Award goes to team 8139 - Pirate Robotics.

From a well-designed pit to a robot performing well on the field, this team shows quality in everything they do. With two-pin access to their electrical panel and colorful flag pins promoting diversity, they showcase both workmanship and inclusivity. You can see that quality is a Central focus for this team.

This team displayed great enthusiasm, teamwork, and consistency in play. With a plan already in hand to increase their outreach next year, this team is one to watch. Though now a part of the FIRST family, this team will always be Sisters First.
Inspiration comes from many places and takes many forms. With their intentional design and clear enthusiasm, we can all be inspired by this team.

Our team spirit winner stands out in the crowd with their alliance chants, helping spirit, and sea of teal. They are a team who takes pride in their regrowth and exudes enthusiasm in the pit, on the field, and even just passing through the halls. There’s no question that this team’s spirit passes the TEST.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: While you may not find these animals living together, this team combined smarts of one the strength of the other to execute their vision.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team, whether they are swerving side-to-side to serve the greater good or climbing up windmills to clear off the roses, this team doesn't have to depend on prayers for their solutions.

Hailing from the foothills of the Santa Ana Valley, this team is small but very mighty. From their STEAM with teens and tweens program to their partnership with the Boy Scouts of American and the public library, they show up for the community like CLOCKWORK. They truly embody the entrepreneurial spirt that is so revered by FIRST.

This team demonstrated in short order the value of a professional approach to engineering and design. Not only did that lead to a highly modular, effective robot, most notably in their 3D turret, but also created a team that was equally modular and elegant in its organization. Specifically, their epic CAD group blew us away.

records.teamName: Kingman FIRST Robotics Team 60 (The Bionic Bulldogs)
records.script: You couldn't be blue because this team was ready, willing, and able to help. Even though this team was an animal on the playing field, they were the other team's best friend off the field.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Judges are wowed by this compact robot, their team’s pit, robot, cart, and shirts are all greenishly professional. Quoting from their school’s namesake, Patrick Henry, they directed the judges to: “Give us imagery or give us Death.”

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team does not horse around when it comes to their winning attitude. Their heritage guides them to great success and a mantra of being excellent to each other.
This team’s use of LEDs to track turret position left the competition GREEN with envy. They were a BRIGHT spot on the field. Having a well-functioning 4-ball autonomous put the STINGER on this robot.

This team is creative in their approach to this year’s challenge. This flock of students worked together to create their robot even while scuttling among all their artistic activities. For putting the A in STEAM,
This team is known for their ability to take the high road when they traverse. They continue to strive for success, even it means going “All In.” This team scores high in quality.

The judges were impressed with the team's efforts to bring STEM education classes to their school. This team ROCKS and creates opportunities for underserved communities. In addition to their local services, they also had a positive impact on the national level. The team members, who consider themselves family, shared dinners together during their build season and created a one-of-a-kind bond. They SOAR as they build for a better tomorrow.

This team's robot excelled at begin a straight shooter with a team who is proud of their "Heritage." From their Ninja moves to smoothly accelerating past the pack, this team clearly outshines the competition.
This team impressed the judges with their teamwork, fundraising, and solid robot. They slither to the mid-range bar showing that cartoons are not the only things this viper team does well.
This new team defended their alliance partners admirably. They discovered through robotics the necessity and value of relationships - both professional and social.

This uppity team is anything but down. They persistently cheered for their team and even invited other teams to horn in on their FUN. Let's out-cheer these noisy Nordics, as we present this spirit award.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: This team wowed the judges with their autonomous operation. They worked on improving their ability to score as many pieces of cargos as quickly as possible. Their snapshot turret could shoot from anywhere in the field. When it comes to scoring they don’t settle, the keep sailing. The Autonomous Award goes to Team 870 from Southold.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Their robot is small but don’t toy with this fierce predator. The way it picks balls is uniquely ferocious. Their beetle like mimicry makes them stand out.

This team empowered each other to develop to all of their abilities, to create opportunities and inspire others. They successfully went out of their tech-bubble when they were thirsty for funding. The Entrepreneurship Award goes to app developer and bubble tea maker 2601, Steel Hawks.
Every student on this team had intimate knowledge of their robot. Their documentation clearly and concisely described their electrical and mechanical engineering process and that’s no bull.

For this team, Gracious Professionalism comes naturally, representing the FIRST Core Values in every interaction. The judges were thrilled to learn that this team works and collaborates with other teams on a regular basis. Additionally, they demonstrated their Gracious Professionalism by giving up their place in line to assist others.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team’s appearance is coordinated perfectly with their machine. Their original theme plugs in their team. With a strong look and positive current, let’s plug it in for team 5298.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team is one of the founding teams of SBPLI and is marching to success. Their clean and robust frame design was rigid and light weight as well as aesthetically pleasing with a professional look. The frame was machined and assembled by students from stock aluminum and acrylic panels. The robot relies heavily on gearbox and chain-drive mechanisms providing clean design and reliable operation. The Continental Army wore red and blue but for this team purple is the color they like best.

This robot’s control system functions using clean and concise code. Their game play and scoring is a direct result of great programming and human interfaces. The judges were very impressed with the science and wisdom behind their design process. The Innovation in Control Award goes to the downtown team 694 from Stuyvesant High School.

This team exemplifies the values of FIRST with its diversity, inclusivity, and outreach. With the variety of languages spoken there is no chance of mis-communication. Striving towards life-long learning along with eliminating hunger, there are no limits to what this team “CAN” do.

This winning team crafted a clean, robust, modular concept with quality through and through. Their crisp shapes are well-executed by student fabrication, and this design has served them well on the field. When new challenges come, they just shake it off.

This team is a model for the values of FIRST. A diverse group of individuals promoting STEM within their community by implementing curriculum and forming and mentoring numerous FLL teams. When the pandemic hit it was a slam dunk that this team would support our front line workers by providing PPE. This team was inspired to expand their outreach beyond the local community to a broader global community. The future is secure as this team is preparing the next generation of scientists to enter the sea of orange.

This team’s outstanding success in advancing STEAM in the schools and community wowed the judges! Their commitment to the sharing of information and ideas advances the ideals and foundation of FIRST. Despite the pandemic they found creative ways to continue this outreach to the community. So let’s scream it from on high: Congratulations to team 2869, the Screaming Eagles

Young in years, rich in spirit. This team is laying the groundwork for a successful and far-reaching program. Between their summer program, internship workshops, and Parent’s Day, this team works hard to spread the message of FIRST beyond competition. The judges agree that in years to come, this ream will certainly fly high. Congratulations to team 8739, Redhawk Robotics!
The energy in this team is infectious with elementary kids wishing you luck. You can’t help steam up with joy. The Award for Team Spirit goes to 7717 – Steam Punks.

Your robot is so autonomous Even though you’re blind as a bat Gobbling up balls like a hungry hungry hippopotamous Because you know where they’re at Using your alignment plate You gather up all the freight And then you make all the shots Congratulations to the Ossining O-Bots!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Machine tentacles with hooks of Velcro Your boxy design prevents you from catching an elbow Grab, shoot, run up and down Steady she goes, with aligned shots on the ground Claws articulate to ensure balance Reaching the summit is not a challenge Talented, ingenious, admired by peers Without further ado, the award goes to the Rocketeers.

The well prepared presentation to the judges was no lacking, so insightful Open source application developed for resource management was no wasting, so helpful Facebook, Twitter and Instagram management was no stopping, so amazing 300,000 views over the past year was no joking, so impressive With this we present the Entrepreneurship Award to no other, Team 6911, the SO BOTZ

This year you had a challenge to move cargo for transportation and developed a plan that rose to the occasion. With a solid design that prioritized key functions, climbing, hanging and even preventing malfunctions. You iterated on your cargo loading with several prototypes and tested your shooter till you got it just right. You played offense and defense and thought outside the box Congratulations team 2601 Steel Haws.
Whether giving rollers to others or assisting a grieving full Metal Beaver. This environmentally focused team has demonstrated their altruism exemplifying Gracious Professionalism.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: The imagery award was not a mystery Especially for a team dedicated to ‘her’story This team’s delivery was great with their crew We raise our flipper to the wave of blue Let’s tip our hats to the major And all her steampunk engagers

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: When Omicron kept this team from prototyping They made a totally adjustable robot instead of griping The distinctive squat bot alters its center of gravity And along with spring loaded arms makes hanging a certainty They have variable points of contact on their shooter and intake Which combined with pre-programmed shooting locations to make scoring a piece of cake So for taking a path that’s a little unorthodox We’re excited to recognize team 3419, the Rohawks!

For those high performers, They’ve mastered their encoders If a ball doesn’t belong It is sent right along They know that to be in the zone They cannot innovate alone So for the robot that treats the field Like a dance floor…

During the course of the competition, the judges panel may decide a team’s unique efforts, performance, or dynamics merit recognition. When you feel like you can’t go on further and normal has been tossed This team found their inner flame when they realized what would be lost Creating graphic designs and partnering with Maker education They were able to grow from 3 to a 30 member nation From practicing during school lunch This team will help anyone in a crunch They will be the Knights in shining armor for the next generation Providing mentorship, guidance and whole lot of motivation Mr. Ramdas was more than a mentor, teacher and coach He opened the eyes of his team encouraging without reproach Congratulations to the Team 3004 Bronx Knights For making your coach & mentor Mr. Ramdas proud tonight!

Quality execution at every level You can’t miss the magic of their swivel Not letting quality slip through their claws This team works to a list to keep them from flaws Purring while navigating on the game floor You can’t miss their colorful lights when they score With their neon green bot named sourdough We are excited to see RoboTigers go!

In keeping with FIRST’s mission of transforming our culture They donated spark kits that will impact that FLL team’s future. Teaching and mentoring on sensors and CAD This team now includes a lot more than just lads. This Chairman’s Awardee is always bringing the light Doing demos and town halls and sometimes into the night Community building with Robots-in-a-box Even glow LED lights on their feet but not their socks Helping their school basketball team as well as their teachers Having impact teaching 2D to 3D and creating creatures This team also touts a 100% graduation rate Let’s all Congratulate the Team… 5298!! Again, Congratulations to team 5298 E-Tech Chargers that will be invited to a FIRST Championship where they will compete for the Chairman’s Award against winners from other qualifying events.

From swim to STEM, they spread the word Making sure the message of FIRST is heard Adding STEM to humanities bot by byte Building programs to make the future more bright They lead STEM wherever they can They are the 8-bit Rams.

This team was cutting edge and diverse They embody the mission of FIRST For their outreach they showed their skills Spreading their wings gives us chills As we watch them build their flock We were inspired by Redhawk

Cheering and dancing along With the tunes; always on their feet From morning to noon With their pom-poms in the air You can see them from everywhere Purple and green and all girls too This train is arriving all aboard, “Two Two Six Five”
This team is no stranger to the limelight. It has a turret that can target and multiple balls aren't a challenge for these warriors.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Bounce, Bounce, bounce, in and out of the hopper went the shots, coming back out of the top- points lost. How to fix? More back spin, less spin or change the aim? Overnight inspiration! With a new design with double wheels and circuit updates flying the ball. A prototypes to make it fly and score with elegant architecture overall.

Nuts and bolts form the base of a strong business empire. Using the force of statistics, analytics and budgetary control fuel this rebel alliance. With the safety of a strong balance sheet this team’s outlook is bullish.
Preparation is 90% of the battle. With mind maps and role play this team attacked the challenge with military precision to build a machine ready to roll on to the field.

Sharing knowledge throughout kingdom this team came to the rescue of a bot in distress. Unlocking code in another castle saved the day. Selflessly focusing on others is the spark that starts their fire.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: SONG- TUNE OF AMAZING GRACE Amazing boat, how sweet they sail they saved a wreck like me I once was lost, but now am found One eye, but now I see

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Durability was this team's goal for their robot. Their fully welded frame is definitely up to the task and impressed the judges.

This team takes control of the hanger with a double hook allowing it to hang whether it is coming or going. Their bot combines vision and drivetrain data as it passes you low or high All of this control eliminates skidding on the tarmac, making it a worthy forza competitor.

THE RESILLIANCE AWARD Confronting mechanical failure, an electric storm and Murphy’s law, this team sat static through the start of FLR. With small numbers, limited experience, and nothing fancy, they dug in and got to work. Demonstrating resilience, fortitude, and a range of FIRST core values they kept their spirit alive and are ready to launch into the future.

This Team had a well designed approach to all parts of their robot- and their team. Their sleek machine shoots fast and climbs high. Even dangling by a single hockey stick couldn't stop this strong, high scoring robot.

This resourceful and enthusiastic team showed resilience and growth during Covid's challenging times. Their volunteerism is benchmark with activities to support homeless shelters, refugees and other underserved populations. They've shown leadership by starting and supporting many FIRST teams and running offseason events. FTC and FLL team mentoring by team members, combined with advocacy efforts with their school leadership has resulted in doubling the number of engineering courses at their school and opportunities for team members to earn school credit. Their advocacy with alumni resulted in a $6 million donation for constructing a dedicated facility for their local FIRST alliance. Get together with your BFFs and Choose Your Own Adventure to help cheer on our Chairman's Award Team.

The members of this team are ALL stem evangalists, ignighting a passion for the expansion of the FIRST kingdom. Their super powers extend from the classroom to the boardroom, from the boundaries of the US to the shores of South Africa and Mexico. They believe that with FIRST "Everyone can go PRO"

A standout in the stands, they merged to become stronger together with the strength of 2 giant cats. This team gives us PAWS- Pit Assistance With a Smile Give it up for 2228! Congratulations Team Cougar Tech

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: In developing their code, this team embarked on a saga quite like their friend Rocky. They proved that their robot is the Top Gun, and that they embody the Scottish spirit. Fast and smooth, they will travel far and HIGH! Congratulations, Team 4499, The Highlanders!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.teamName: F. R. O. G. - FIRST Robotics Organization of Grove
records.script: This team really swerved around the competition, HOPPING their way to a unique and RIBBITING design which really LEAPED out at you! Their unique actuator really threw a CURVE at the competition. Congratulations, Team 3160, F.R.O.G.!

This O.K. team is a great EXHIBIT of a team that has a great plan for success. They plan to cement their place in history with a business plan that is more than O.K.. See how they live up to their goals while surrounded with future scientists. With foundations well established, they launched like a rocket right to the top. Give it up for team 2718, Team OKC

Good things come in small packages. This team designed a compact, modular robot that avoids interference inside the robot and on the field. Many voices create design excellence when they work together throughout the engineering process, even though it might sound like a scream. Congratulations Team #4522, Team Scream

This “claw” of gracious professionals are second to none. With their “cat-like” reflexes, they stepped in to assist multiple teams this competition, from tools and troubleshooting, to even driving for another team. This team consistently exemplifies FIRST core values with “no robot left behind” Congrats team 1108, Panther Robotics!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Their image is more than meets the eye. Agile, loving and stealthy until they transform into competitive cybernetic felines. These kitties look pretty puuuurrrrfect! Congratulations, Team number 4256 Cyborg Cats.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team explores unknowns ahead like their forefathers did in the mountains. This apple of Newton's eye brought a wave down on their opponents heads. Travel upstream and you'll find this huge team!

You have to get up early in the morning to compete with this team. They can sort the balls and shoot from anywhere to dominate the competition. They have a lot to crow about. Congratulations Team 3931, Cockadoodle Dominators.

This team moved around the field quite well, but that is not what they’ve earned this award for. Off the field, they help others. Locally, they are heavily involved in starting up FLL and FTC teams, working to run Summer STEM camps and “FIRST at Home” events. They were involved with Covid and storm relief efforts. The item that stood out, no pun intended, was that they have been working on a device to help with mobility. Much like a young dolphin over a decade ago was in need of a tail, this team from off the Gulf has built a leg to help a boy be more mobile, with the design targeted for cycling. The team and its design has been featured on CBS news. Let the good times roll as the Judges’ Award goes to Team 3616, Phenomena.

This team prowled thru the build season to create a robust system. They quietly designed-in redundancy and mitigations for what could go wrong on the field of competition. Like a panther in the night, this bot just snuck up to take the award. Congratulations Team 6424, Stealth Panther Robotics

Like many of the Chairman’s award teams, they have outreach to FIRST teams and organizations stretching the globe and supported various Covid assistance efforts during the past two years. On a local level, they have worked with starting many FLL and FTC teams while also illuminating the minds of their state’s legislators to support STEM initatives. They take the time to drive Go-Baby-Go, but “CONVERSEly”, this team knows how to walk the FIRST walk, just like Woody. Congratulations to Team 3284, Camdenton LASER

This team flew high above the competition, inspiring economic development through the promotion of science and technology at home and abroad. "Linking up" with partners in their community, they have created multiple pathways to careers in STEM, with "sinking their teeth" into hosting their own off-season events. From bowling for cancer research to workshops for all ages, community outreach is just one thing this team won't LEGO.

This flock is bright, seen day and night. On the road they go, to help STEM grow. This unique team builds robots all day, and moves large birds all night. Congratulations Team 8711, Midnight Ostrich Runners

This team is great at BUILDING team spirit, BREAKING down with outstanding dance moves, and INNOVATING new chants. These felines are not ashamed of supporting their team. This team is wired up while staying stylish in yellow and red. Stand up and cheer for FIRST robotics team 2996 - Cougars Gone Wired

This team battled their way to the top. During the autonomous period, they were consistently ready to ship out cargo at a moment’s notice. Their hunger for victory could only be satisfied by one BIG “Cupcake”!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: A small team looking to make a big noise in the competition can’t be Lion around. A design that combined the shooting and climbing mechanisms let this team come ROARING out of the gate.

This team's business plan was a critical-roll in their game on the way to success. Entrepreneurial Spirit of this team reaches broadly across their region and is focused on multiple events and groups of younger kids through the FIRST Program to build a sustainable future. That their business plan and outreach touches so many directions like tentacles of an octopus is why the Entrepreneurship Award goes to
Sometimes the best engineering solution is to doggedly apply what worked in the past. Ironing out design problems early and quickly is the key to success!

When the deck seemed stacked against the field, this team had a few ACES up their sleeve. They continuously flew in for other teams in need. From building bumpers, to lending parts, to flat out repairing their fellow competitors’ machines, this team was the very definition of Gracious Professionalism throughout the week.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team hatched the dreams of imagery through innovation. They have sustained their coop by preventing bad eggs and encouraging “eggcellence”. The team dominates the competition by ruling the roost through color and brand coordination.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team was SIMPLY the best at manufacturing all of their custom parts. With MULTIPLE iterations on their climbing mechanism they were able to rise above the rest. Ultimately, they were able to build a BEAUTIFUL robot and win our golden seal of approval!

Any good driver knows how critical a good dashboard is to success. This team was ready for each scenario, and was able to calculate their trajectory at the competition. They decided to take command of their future and extended a hand to other teams by providing an open source software to any who would take up the challenge!

This team does not STOP on the road to success and never lets any SIGN of adversity get them down. This team’s robot does not YIELD to defeat and makes every effort to MERGE with others to seize the day! Whenever the situation gets HAIRY and GRIZZLED this team of three will BEAR down to get the job done.

A robot of top quality that excels in design, appearance, workmanship and performance can be as rare as precious metals like silver and gold. This “show me” state team delivered a robot exceeding even a gold standard!

As instilled by their team motto… This team challenges their community to dream bigger by learning more about programming and how robotics can assist the community in overcoming obstacles. This team works harder to learn more, do more, be more by reaching out to all age groups both young and old by leveraging their internal values of responsibility, trust, commitment, respect, communication, and sustainability. By engaging in improving team member skills in language, programming, and healthcare this team encourages its members to fly higher with STEM. We accept their invitation to fly with them.

This inspiring feline team with a killer bot sneaks up on the competition with a very low RADAR cross section. They exemplify FIRST Core Values spreading STEM class packs and slime bombs across their community. The pipeline of STEM is flowing where the “Reaper” rolls!

These runners have worked tirelessly with FLL, FTC and FRC, as well as helping girl scouts get their robotics badges and promoting how FIRST Rocks. This award is a proud feather in their cap! The Rookie Inspiration Award goes to the large birds moving all night!

This unified team has swarmed over Green Country with obvious enthusiasm. If you need a jab of encouragement, this team will sting you with positive energy and maybe a little noise. They don’t tell time very well, but they have FIRST spirit!

Through solid design as exemplified by clean in-house powder-coated components, incredible consistent lift system, and replaceable wheel threading design. When the competition raised their level, this team ‘bit’ back with the tenacity of a “wolverine” showing persistent success on the floor that left other teams “Green” with envy.

This team is extensively involved with all levels of FIRST programs. For many years they have been inspiring students and communities through innovative events and by rolling out their engineering education initiatives locally and beyond. Like thunder from an approaching storm, this team’s advocacy efforts to increase funding for STEM can be heard rumbling throughout their state legislature and in multiple national conferences.

This team inspires their community and the world with a hunger for STEM by their outstanding global outreach skills. Their passion for excellence and commitment on and off the field is as strong as Steel. These girls are therefore the Real Deal.

Their cheering was so loud, another state could hear them from afar. Their outfits may hide them, but their team number can be seen from across the arena. When they start chanting, you might think that you’re going to “Wor”!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team really understood the meaning of Industrial design by creating an aesthetically pleasing and highly functional robot. The judges were "hooked" by their choice of materials and their entire machine "forging" process. With their teeth and their carbon fiber claws this team really "means" it.

With balls everywhere, intakes were important. This team automated theirs for blue and red, all leveraging one type of sensor. This robot detected ball color to release it when it isn't their fave. All using one button and two sensors making it easily behave. Such an advantage the simple system gave . . .

Today, the Judges have defined the following special award as the Science Everywhere Award for one deserving team. This team got creative when they needed to go remote, using the oddest of supplies. They bring STEM kits to schools and hospitals, leveraging groceries and toothbrushes inside. From the lab to your table this team can teach you STEM.

This robot's clean lines, robust design and craftsmanship drove this team's performance through the tension of the event. A design balanced between the heavy and light side to climb and shoot for success, was supported by a team that worked well together and proved failure was not an option. With an organized pit, team values focused on reliability, and a double intake for redundancy this robot STORMed the field.

This team impressed the judges with their amazing outreach and their extensive support for FIRST programs. Their efforts were rewarded with team membership more than doubled during the pandemic. They even stepped up on short notice to host an FRC competition. When faced with adversity, they don't retreat, they react! The second Pacific Northwest District Championship Chairman's Award goes to 2412 Robototes.

Small towns do not mean small dreams. 45 active FIRST teams, a documentary, and a museum display are all in their dossier, With such an impact, even on projects as small as Gus, this team's outreach is hardly a secret. The first Pacific Northwest District Championship Chairman's Award goes to Team 4125 Confidential

They have bright smiles and creative solutions that switch things up. This team inspires hundreds of students with STEM education outreach for all ages. And their mentorship model comes from a galaxy far far away. This Engineering Inspiration Award goes to Team 2557 SOTABots
This team doesn't just focus on their own spirit, they also watch out for other teams. One could say they spread enthusiasm like wildfire. They've definitely cracked the code.

This team proved their "metal" in their innovative design process, producing a well engineered robot that performed well every time they put it "in motion". Congratulations Team 343, Metal-In-Motion, from Seneca, SC.
