Congratulations Team 1293, the Pandamaniacs, from Columbia, SC.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With a turret shooter, double intake, and 5 ball autonomous, this team "fused" together multiple complicated design elements and went "nuclear" on the field. Traveling all the way from the Magnolia State, congratulations Team 364, Team Fusion, from Gulfport, MS.

This team used a "bowl full of ideas" to create a robot that rolled into a high seed. With a single-button climb, they didn't need luck to ascend in the standings. This team followed the rainbow all the way to the "pot of gold." Congratulations Team 2393, the Robotichauns, from Knoxville, TN.

This team "clawed" their way to success. They keep their freshman active with future plans by tackling the challenge of a t-shirt launcher. This pink team likes to keep things dramatic by impressing the Judges. Congratulations, Team 4073, the RoboKatz, of Myrtle Beach, SC.

This South Carolina team "tapped" into their potential to create a robust machine. These caped crusaders tightened their belts to make the other teams "green with envy." Congratulations to "Belton John" and Team 281, The GreenVillains, from Greenville, SC.

This well-rounded team did not let the loss of their space due to COVID deter them from spreading the message of FIRST. They play their part in making sure FIRST and STEM opportunities are accessible to everyone no matter their educational interests, gender, ethnicity, or socio-economic background. They achieve this mission through hosting and volunteering at FIRST events, mentoring over 50 teams in the past 3 years, writing grants to have the ability to distribute robot kits to rural middle schools, and implementing a curriculum that brings robotics, agile engineering, and digital design to their area. This team makes no secret they are passionate about FIRST. They may be from the Secret City but they are not hard to find. This year's Chairman's Award goes to Team 4265, the Secret City Wildbots, from Oak Ridge TN.

This team is starting to go mobile, by sharing their love of engineering and STEM. Get ready for the "Storm"! The Engineering Inspiration award goes to Team 3489, Category 5, from North Charleston, SC.

Y’all better get ready; this team is nothing but 5 stars. So y’all saddle up and head west, because y’all’s newest FIRST team didn’t come for a draw. This year’s Rookie All-Star award goes to Team 8575, The Due Westerners, from Due West, SC!

This team is full of energy and will have you "burning" in your seat. They are shining as bright as a shadowless Charizard and they know how to play their cards right. Congratulations Team 342, the Burning Magnetos, from North Charleston, SC.

records.script: This robust robot really stood out during heated competition. Their single team design method combined their components like a recipe. This team's recipe allows them to serve up their opponents from the pit, and welcome everyone to the hot BBQ.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.script: United by their love for robots, this team developed a machine that impressed the judges to no end. With their intake system on rails, this team is sliding through the competition. This team is a BOSS on the field and in the pits.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.script: This team "flew" to new heights when they "clutched" their school's attention in a unique way. They built several robots, including a party bot! This team is so royally excited about robots, their robot was even nominated as homecoming queen.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.script: This team's robot was designed to work hard, play hard, and look great. They learned lessons in the school of hardknocks and mapped out a path to a quality robot. Some teams find troubleshooting "shocking." This team was so organized they have worried about getting zapped.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.script: This team is helping to shoulder the weight of the FIRST world on their backs. From hosting career nights to raising $6,000 through their summer camp, they are quickly becoming a Titan in the FRC community. While this team bore the weight of starting during Covid, they are persevering with the gracious professionalism of a veteran team.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Apollo Division
records.script: This team pounces on the opportunity to represent young girls in STEM. Their inclusive attitude spills into their robot, pit, and the teams around them. They are filling FIRST with their team spirit, one rhinestone at a time. It must be game time!

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division
records.script: Geometry, trigonometry, odometry - what didn't this team do to the "green?" They have a custom vision system, color sensors to sort cargo, and feedback lights for their drivers. All of this, however, was "background radiation" compared to the team's web based autonomous development tool.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division
records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team came up with a creative approach to the end game. This bird of prey digs its first talon into the mid bar and the other into the transverse bar, never needing to hit the third bar.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division
records.script: This community team will greet you with Texas style. Their business savvy ensures they are well-funded year after year. Watch out for this Danger Noodle!

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division
records.script: This team really "dips" into success with their robot design. With their adjustable hood, custom locking gearbox, and double intake, they really stand strong in excellence. This team is much more than a chip off the old block.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division
records.script: This team makes the FIRST mission "visible" to the world. They offer help to other teams in the field, the pits, their city, online, and through the Open Alliance. These students represent "all the colors" of FIRST.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division
FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division
records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team shows their "Illumination" of spirit with color coordination of robots and tracksuits. They shoot cargo with the accuracy of a "Squid Launcher." This team impressed the judge by "stealing the moon" and getting full rights for the use of their team's mascot. OH YEAH!

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division
records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This robot is the perfect balance of aesthetics, form, and function. This cool cat loves to pounce on the balls, shoot in the hubs, and use their pocketed trusses to climb to the highest bar.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division
records.script: This team took our breath away the "moment" we saw them. They didn't just use a limelight to aim, but they used odometry to calculate where the hub was to line up for every shot. This team locks their swerve drive into an X, truly showing us what happens when the "unstoppable Torque becomes the immovable object."

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division
records.script: The team "blew" the judges away with their commitment to their community and other teams. From the pants to the pits, they exhibit many FIRST values. Their influence has been "titanic."

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division
records.script: From concept to fabrication, this team tries various sizes and materials until lightning strikes with the right design. This robot charged through the field with their custom designed hub and wheels, and stiffener in their frame.

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division
records.script: Led by a FIRST Alumni, this team inspires their school to make robotics a priority. Overcoming their shyness has led this college prep school to realize they can be who they truly are and succeed no matter their background. Papa Bear? Mama Bear? No, it's Baby Bear!

records.eventName: FIRST In Texas District Championship - Mercury Division
records.script: This team wow-ed the judges with their love of traditions and inclusivity. With their exceptional spirit, they will be an inspiration to future STEM Ladies. Led by Patty the Platypus, please congratulate team 3103, Iron Plaid, from Houston, Tx.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation

records.script: This team exemplifies Coopertition and Gracious Professionalism online and in person. This team works to spread STEM knowledge and FIRST values throughout their local area and beyond. Their impact reaches far and wide. Volunteering at food banks, helping Habitat for Humanity, and running blanket drives. They even found ways to help their community during the pandemic by distributing PPE and working to create a low-cost respirator. With their “Open Shop Policy” and willingness to share knowledge and resources, we would like to share an open congratulations to team #3481, Bronc Botz.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: Cargo automatically disappears when this robot is on the field. They consistently traverse the competition, their talons grasping the bars. Their swift flying maneuvers make them hard to catch.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Old technology rarely disappears, especially when someone finds a creative way to fuse it into a new solution. A pencil can draw a new design or erase a problem. Cutting to the chase…

COVID did not slow this team down. While they sat perched, watching their community & the world shutting down around them, this team pounced on the opportunity to help others by providing PPE. The ‘Clowder’ met and decided…. “We’re not stopping there!” They also provided new STEM opportunities to females by creating multiple ‘women in STEM’ initiatives. These steel felines like to play basketball and bring FIRST robotics to all students no matter their age or capabilities.

This team shows “inclusion” no matter your age, gender or capabilities. “Inspiring” others by 3D printing components. This “inquisitive” team even took time to ask judges how we became involved with FIRST. Please help us congratulate this “innovative” team.
This young team is a diamond in the rough. Their cashflow is in the black. This team will not fold with their “full house of cards”.

We have seen many teams demonstrate their commitment to excellence in navigating the competition. Conquering the cold expanse of space, this robot bravely ventures forth and traverses the stars. When white and gold appear over the horizon, we can all expect a stellar display.

This team embodies and exemplifies FIRST values within their community. They are creating radical change in the community with their sportsmanship attitude. Their Gracious Professionalism roars with Woodie Flowers throughout the community supporting fellow teams and mentoring rookies.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This student-based team can be heard and spotted from miles away. Their professionalism, enthusiasm, and dedication to being the best and LOUDEST in every competition is truly extraordinary. Whether they finish on top of the leaderboard or come up a bit short, their effort is to “tie-dye” for.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: From far away you can hear the roaring of pistons. Being apart of this alliance, your primal instincts will stomp the competition. This prehistoric bot swerves their way up the bars with their piston power.

Innovation is not just about the target but the process to reach the target, even without palm in hand. This team wrangled themselves away from the herd with 330 degree shooting around the position. All these features integrated together under precise engineering control which was executed by a team who slayed in black.

You have all heard, “If you cannot take the heat, stay out of the kitchen”. This team went above the rest, diving into the fire head first, tackling an important engineering challenge. With its patent-pending design, they protect others who dare to do the same.

Rapid React has seen many competitors traverse with speed and consistency. This robot stood out to the judges with their commitment to consistent and quality strategy, with reliable execution on the field. When this team “SWOOPS” in, it is wise to get out of the way before they sink in their “talons”.

This team has demonstrated outstanding work to promote women and LGBTQI in STEM. They have started building a “pack” of FRC teams with grand plans to bring FIRST to the school board. They may be young but do not discount these “pups”. Let’s give a loud “howl” for these rookies!
This team feels that FIRST is a family. One team pushes the others to move forward. Growing their outreach to younger students. The judges “overall” pick for rookie inspiration is…..
Are you all as excited as this team? With their numbers and headgear, their spirit is infectious. “Beep-Beep Boop-Boop Bop”, goes Rosie the robot!

This team’s robot is HIGH-ly autonomous. The bot lends a helping hand to the drivers during HIGH stress portions of the match. This high energy team lights up the field with their consistent auto functions!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team's nimble and quick scoring ability would make Steph Curry proud. While shooting is key, intake is critical. With efficiency in mind, this team came to the game with a shin-take, accelerating both of these important features.

Great Chairman’s Award winning teams have an ability to nurture a passion for STEM, engineering and FIRST core values in their communities, to plant the seeds of their program both within their own school community and with the next generation of students. This team has done that, and more. They have lit a fuse on a future explosion of talent in STEM – hosting summer camps, info sessions, and partnerships with community organizations. They are even looking to a greener future with a focus on finding innovative solutions to clean up Texas beaches. Pour yourself a tall glass of OJ!

Building robots is hard work, but building respect and appreciation for FIRST in your community might be even harder. This team has done that work, taking little bites at it each season – building relationships with younger students in elementary and middle schools as mentors for FLL teams .They even host a robotic ‘bowl season’ event of their own that helps build passion and interest in robotics their community! Grab your favorite bag of salty crunchy snacks and congratulate this team.

This team is working hard to cultivate the team’s size, knowledge, passion and impact. As their motto states, they are not just building a robot, but helping to shape future female STEM leaders with a STRONG focus on helping underrepresented communities. They specifically added a historian role to the team this year to ensure the success of “Franken-Climb” is documented for years to come!

The engineering process this team created was colorful throughout. They created a comic book hero that stands proud and strong. Their overall Patriotism will lead them to their MARK 3 that lies at the end of the rainbow. Don't let this technology fall into the wrong hands!

Whether traversing down I-45, around Beltway 8, or straight up 288, distance is no deterrent for this team. They mesh with and mentor other teams on and off the field and are always willing to lend a helping hand!

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team will shock you on the field and make you green with envy. From their uniforms to their robot to their pits, these electric rebels are going green!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team turned their detailed process and design into an efficient reality. Their bot moves gracefully both on the field and during the climb. The Simpsons character Disco Stu says "the judges picked you!"

Do you even automate, bro? This team does. And you might think, with their name, that they are focused only on linear problems – automating single operations … one to the next, on and on forever – but you’d be wrong. They are not just focused on single vectors – they have built a dynamic shooting algorithm, putting the high goal in the ‘lime light’ and firing away with accuracy from anywhere, automatically.
This team snuck around the pits like cats in the night, spreading awareness of pit safety. Black cats might be unlucky, but this team ensures safety isn’t down to the luck of the draw.

Like the M1 Abrams, this robot is battle-ready easily withstanding the rigors of the game. Like a high clearance vehicle, this team’s machine can overcome any obstacle. Built to take on the game from any angle, the elevated, reinforced corners were an unstoppable force on the field. Although we won’t be going here today, there is no way that captain Sully can avoid this today.
This team left their HOME with a vision to excel northward in FRC. Their never-give-up attitude is consistent throughout the team and proceeded to continuously improve in competition.

This rookie came roaring into the competition and have shown an appreciation for science and technology. They clearly take pride in hard work and perseverance and will be building appreciation for engineering in their community.

This team stuck together throughout the contest with spirit and a stapler. They brought the community to their medical clinic to practice and create, but most importantly they continue to Reach to the sky with their enthusiasm and unity.
This team proved that they are HEROES during autonomous. Their custom path-planning and user interface makes their opponents GREEN with envy.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: With creative thinking, this team netted a simple, effective solution to expand functionality. This team took the PLUNGE to reacting rapidly to enable a shot at the top and raised themselves from the autonomous abyss to success.

From Houston to Spokane, USA to Thailand, Romania, Afghanistan, Vietnam, Mexico, Africa, and 20 additional countries, this team’s message has global impact. It’s PLANE to see that this team is ENERGIZED about FIRST. With LANDINGS in over half the world’s continents, and FIRST’s message spoken through sign and science. This team is cleared for takeoff with award in hand

This team inspired the judges with their FIERCE commitment to sharing STEM wherever they go. When the pandemic shifted outreach online, this team took it as an opportunity to expand and reach farther than before, while building their pipeline at home. This. Is. Inspiration!
Like Steve Jobs at Apple, starting off in their parent’s garage helped plant this SEED. Their outreach is the ROOTS that drive innovation. Hopefully this growth will spring you high in the SKY.

While all teams here incorporated the S, T, & E of STEM, this team also heavily focused & utilized the MATH element in their iterative design process. Their theme colors may be yellow & green but their robot was initially COLOR BLIND. But after tireless effort in troubleshooting, they realized the solution was a simple as JOINING point A to point B to give their robot the ability to see BLUE & RED.

This team works hard to be the LIGHT in their community. In both assisting and mentoring teams, they FOCUS on their online presence. While they lookout to the HORIZON, they exude this FIRST core value.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Always blue but never sad this team suited up to create a unified and striking image that soared above all others. Not many birds can leave he atmosphere but with the wind under their wings, these birds cross the channel to reach the stars.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Modeling their steps showed how they danced through the air, spinning to the top with 2 thumbs up. This team might fall but they will jump right back into the dance.
Clear LEGENDS in their own time. This team SPED UP or DOWN for their alliance, ensuring a successful battle strategy on the playing field.

During the course of the competition, the judges were SHOCKED by the ability of this team to excel in many different categories. Even this team’s bright yellow color scheme helped enlighten the decision to award this team
This team designed their bot with quality and consistency in mind. This HURRICANE of a team SWEPT throughout their garages for a mid-season rebuild. They’ll SUCK you in to their modular build.

This rookie team is making waves throughout their community. Their passion for first shines throughout their outreach programs, their vision, and their team spirit. They want everyone to jump on the BUS.

With the focus on inclusion and a mission to bring STEM to all, this rookie team is creating blizzards for FIRST. These high achievers are keeping it weird…and chill. Their little baby bear is inspiring us all.
This spirited team took the hits but not any CYBER-ATTACKS. PVC and wood became their 2 new best friends. Their electrifying spirit JOLTED the judges and their community.

This team's autonomous left the judges awestruck. They reused to HEEL to their competition, scoring those ever-important first points. After pawing their way from New Mexico, we want to congratulate team 5613, Thunder Dogs, on the Autonomous Award.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: To the team that greatly SPARKED our interest, you were able to accomplish what many could not. Your turret mobility turned our heads and showed us your incredible electrical potential. The custom, compact design shocked the judges and that's why we would like to award Team 3005, the Robochargers, the Creativity Award.

This team gives STEM a voice with leadership. Offering unique access to all, helping seniors go pro, and building a broad community three minutes at a time culminated in their rise above a field of many. Everyone appreciates a home run! Congratulations to Team 2468, Team Appreciate, our 2022 FIT Waco Chairman's Award winner.

This team is truly a FORCE to be reckoned with. With their widespread influence and community outreach, they really turned it up a notch. After DOUBLING their team POWER this year, we'd like to congratulate team 1477, Texas Torque, on the Engineering Inspiration Award.

For the engineering entrepreneurship award, this team soared above the flock. They used their sharp talons and focused eyes to create a comprehensive business plan that grows their team and creates effective young engineers and teachers in their team and community. That is why we would like to congratulate Eagle Robotics, Team 5417 for the entrepreneurship award!

To the team that has grabbed the competition by the horns. This team showed all around excellence in their autonomous navigation, shooting and agility. They innovated on nearly every aspect of their robot, but their automation and unique climbing mechanism impressed us the most. Congratulations to team 148, the Robowranglers, for winning the Excellence in Engineering Award.

This team can be seen helping both on and off the field here in Waco and within their community. We want to tip our cowboy hats to this team! Join me in saying HOWDY and congratulations to the team 6377, the Howdy Bots, for winning the Gracious Professionalism Award.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This team was FIRE on the field and in the pits. The judges drooled over this team's image and machine. They RISKED IT FOR THE BRISKET!! Congratulations to team 2714 BBQ for winning the Imagery Award.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: With their vibrant colored robot and stylish weight-reduction design, this team was able to combine engineering and strategic style to allow for optimal performance throughout the competition. The Industrial Design Award by General Motors goes to team 2881, the Lady Cans.

This team never took their eye off the prize, and always knew where they stood. Their innovative vision targeting system allowed them to virtually guarantee that their robot was in position to score max points. Congratulations to team 624, CRyptonite, on winning the Innovation in Control Award.

Here in the great southwest a robot like no other deserves an award like no other. In their completely unique and out of the box design this team developed a new style of robot that shows incredible potential and efficiency of design. We would like to award team 4717 the Judges award for their unique four sided intake design and hands-on execution.

To the team who swooped in and snatched victory from the competition. This team's unique design helped them climb to the top, all while their chain and cord system allowed them to hang around. Congratulations to the winner of the Quality Award, team 3310, Black Hawk Robotics.
This Rookie Team really made the judges' smile. Their First core values were off the map! Congratulations team 8858, Atlas!

Taking flight for the first time, this team showed a fresh energy for engineering. They've made their nest in the community, with plans to grow. We're RED-y to see what's in store for team 8879, REDBird Robotics. Congratulations on winning the Rookie Inspiration Award!

When this team is around, you can never be blue, and you can always find them cheering their hats off. They motivate each other to get into gear, and were ready to volunteer whenever needed. It's plain to see that we're "dye-ing" to congratulate team 5431, Titan Robotics, on winning the Team Spirit Award.

This team can sit back on the couch as its robot takes shots that are far out. They performed consistently well during autonomous operation and used autonomy during manual play to track the hub and initiate climbing. These spuds fried the competition.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This TALON-ted group swoops and lifts the balls to the nest and quickly grabs their perch. Eight Falcons flew this team to victory.

Solutions to complex problems are not always black and white. This team has an extensive and strategic business plan that has helped them to grow a diverse, responsive, and enthusiastic team. Their web of contacts fueled their victory.
This team Pounded out a complex motor wiring system. The KIDS were able to design an intake, lifting, twisting, and shooting system that preformed with amazing accuracy.
This team consistently gives a hand to others. They routinely demonstrated a positive attitude on and off the field. This team's grand gestures show us how much they care.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Competition can be mayhem. This group's integrated visuals kept the team, robot, and fans in sync. We hope this team graciously allows the freshmen to accept this award.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: Brilliant brains build beautiful bots. This team’s modular, maintainable robot was clever, simple, and quick. This team wasn’t bluffing!
The IMU helped this team reach balanced heights and with autonomy shoot faster. With control and innovation, they rarely missed or fell short. This wild horse climbed to mountain heights.

The "CURRENT" team considered for the Judge's award has a genuine impact on the Utah STEM community. This team demonstrated a shocking amount of strength in many areas of the competition. The judges today are truly "AMPED UP" to select this team.
This team tamed their wild shooter in autonomous and the match. Their quality was evident in their unique size and compact design. This team has HORSEPOWER to spare.

This team’s outreach, mentoring and community service are impressive examples of FIRST principles. From sustainability, financial support and advocacy for the underserved, these young adults are colorful examples of the true FIRST spirit that will leave a legacy. In a NUTSHELL, we are Nuts about these ambassadors of FIRST.

The judges “PEELED” through the teams to find one with a genuine mindset to build the future. This team created a fun, inclusive, and diverse environment that fostered engagement in technical roles for early team members. They “SWUNG” through Utah this year to capture this award.
These cubs are so a-MAZE-ing. They got so much done in their backyard. We’re not LION when we say we see promise.
An enthusiastic group of best “SPUDS”, I mean “BUDS”, raised the energy level of this weekend’s competition. This team engaged in a successful “STING” operation to outcheer the rest of the field.

records.script: This winner automatically made it to the top. You would think they were climbing up a tree. They "Bear-ly" had any faults. Congratulations to team 2046... Bear Metal

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team has 3D printed mechanum wheels They have 3 Autonomous programs that can shoot 4 balls They also have a traversal mechanism that latches on with Xtreme accuracy. What time is it for this award?? Of course its 4 88!! Congratulations to team 488 XBot

As a true community partner, this team seeks to make a lasting positive impact on everyone around them. They have created programs to make STEM and engineering accessible to all students. This team has it all. They set goals for themselves and have consistently met them; making those around them better in the process. This team looks and acts professionally right down to the black shirts they all wear with honor. Their efforts for FIRST include working with other teams to start over 80 FLL teams in 19 different schools, and personally mentoring 38 of them. They are a constant presence in the FIRST community by volunteering at FLL, FTC, and FRC events. Consistent with their efforts to bring Robotics to everyone, they work with three Unified Robotics teams and host the Unified Robotics championship. They are great representatives of their school, their community, and FIRST. We are proud to present this year’s Auburn District Chairman’s award to team 4131, the Iron Patriots of Liberty High School.

This team is not science fiction or from the late sixties… They boldly go to Egypt inspiring other FIRST teams with their robot named Mugatu, The Engineering Inspiration award goes to Team 4450, "ORF" the Olympia Robotics Federation, ORF

This winning team has come far over the years. Organizing this team's budget took turning some gears. They were willing to show us their weaknesses and threats. For this award, they were by far the best. This team reaches out to a city full of scholars. To help them raise 1 million dollars. The judges were simply stunned...when it came to this team's endowment fund... This revolution will be televised... Congratulations Team Number 360

This team aimed for a very high bar... They also shot their cargo very, very far!! The judges were impressed with a complete climber rebuild When telling us about their design process we were very thrilled!! This driver station has no need for octometry... Their robot has that covered by utilizing its odometry!! Congratulations to team 2976 -- Spartabots

This team has truly embraced Gracious Professionalism From sharing tools and space with others to lending a helping hand during competition You can see these knights in red and gold from a mile away! Congratulations team 948 NRG

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Their cheer can be heard throughout the lands, Their colors are consistent through the pit, robot and stands. The judges love this friendly-feathered team.. They even hand dye their costumes from red and to green.. So with this team that's vibrant as a lime, Let's huddle together and chant 3...2...1....9!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: A Design that elegantly attacks the game It may even efficiently propel itself through the water... They clearly inked their place for this award Congratulations to team 4918..The Roboctopi..

This team's impact is super Their documentation left the judges in a stupor... We're impressed with the amount of events they are doing here and now... It left the judges saying "Cool" and "Wow"... In Volume 12 we read about these hero's stories Just like the Avengers, the Chargers are known for their glory! To the winners of the "Comic Award" Congratulations Team 3786 --- the Chargers!!

This team's robot is simple and reliable It is a quality robot that much is undeniable The judges were impressed that their pulleys were reswappable The depth and grip made these cords unstoppable This a good robot, through and through We'll remember this channel that's orange and blue! Congratulations team 5683 - Hello World!

This is a list that may not rhyme.. We wanted to create a poem but ran out of time... They have great spirit, you could hear it and see it.. More important is their community impact...spreading the word of FIRST with tact!! Showing full enthusiasm, sticking together like glue.. Spreading the stem.... ever feeling blue! Congratulations to team 4915 Spartronics
At the start, this team winds themselves up to an autonomous win. Cargo springs from their bot without any human touch. They quickly HIGH-JACK the score

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team were some of the coolest CATS in-town. They really turned things AROUND with their innovative climber. Which took them to the top in their very OWN GYMNASIUM!

This golden team has outreach claws, and their girl scout workshops gave us pause. We were impressed with their programs for hands-on learning though they were not to be outdone by their community gardening Best said by Green, the judges think this is a truly remarkable team. The winner of the the District Chairman's award is TEAM 2046 Bear Metal
This team works on robot and team intake. They Swerved to offer summer camps to middle-school youth. This team's dedication to serving their community is as strong as IRON.
Our winner has fenced in their future objectives. Multiple management systems will lead to perennial successes. This team has no weak LINKS in their chain.

This flashy team SWERVES around the competition as they delivered cargo and traversed the hanger. During the offseason theses BRIGHT young PADAWANS improved their engineering prowess as they SHIFT into JEDI MASTERS. This teams robot stands out just as much as the YELLOW JUMPSUITS their engineers wear

Wow, just like Steve Urkel. This team wears purple. While those judges write scripts, come see us on June 26th! We will be bringing everyone together with hopes to continue forever - the robot IRSD - not those tax folks.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: This vivid team can be seen from miles away, even in the deepest, darkest waters. They basically reach out and suck you in with their exceptional incorporation of visual elements and team cohesiveness. This creative team is a fast swimmer, strong competitor, and definitely has a lot of heart.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This "old number, new people" team rose from the fire of COVID even stronger than before. Their innovative solution to supply chain issues let them traverse the competition with ease. It did not take the judges long to turn their heads 120-degrees to watch this "PHOENIX" of a team
This team uses color sensor and code to eject conflicting balls. And, a forklift for ball translation is innovative. LED's signal the progress of shooting. Congratulations to team 4469!

This week's judge's award is the "Witness Protection Award" The name has been changed to protect the innocent. But from all their outreach they cannot hide. They used to be the TOP, but now they lead the PACK.
This team's quality has been known since BC(before COVID). Competitors are green with envy when they enter the field. Their quality shows from their helmets to their toes.
This team's pack is rapidly growing. Their leaps and bounds of improvements are an inspiration to rookies everywhere. The judges are happy to recognize Wolftech Robotics!
This team leaves a trail of enthusiasm in their wake. Their attitude brings other teams out of their shells. For this spirited team, SNAIL-ure is not an option.

This team wowed us during autonomous competition. No matter blue or red alliance, they moved so fast the colors blended together! They showcased a steady capability to shoot *4* balls consistently and accurately.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: Their compact agile robot darts around Easily tracking the hub as they bound This team can aim from wherever they please With a turret that rotates four hundred degrees.

Reacting rapidly with *super speed* this team made the most out of distanced learning and sought solutions outside the box. With *super strength* they shaped and forged online curriculum and developed free summer camps. Then using *x-ray* vision and data this team made sure these programs reached those who would benefit the most. Becoming *superheroes* in their own right this team charged forward making STARS in their community.

This is a big army in blue, doggedly evangelizing STEM in the community. Their podcasts go well beyond scratching the surface. Their assistance for the differently abled is especially touching. Everyone cheers when they go marching in.
This team had a majestic write-up for their business plan. They executed successful solutions to resolve their listed threats. This team swept the board to capture the entrepreneurship award.

This team sailed into the competition on a sea of clever diagrams, and a carefully prioritized process to conquer the design. This resulted in a unique ejection mechanism for cargo captured from the opposing alliance, and a forceful climber to pillage the traversal rung points. Their integration of material weights and FIRST's field CAD into their design shows this team really knows how to put on their thinking helmets.

This team has shown that their attitude, respect for others, and also emphasizing the rootness of professionalism, boldly defend the kingdoms with their defence of graciousness. Any team would gladly have them. *Go forth* to uphold FIRST Core Values.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: You have to be *brave* to stand out like this team does. If you walk by their pit, you will certainly want to *paws* for a good look. Redesigning their logo was a real bear.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team impressed the judges with their diligent design process and their zeal for improvement. They have *climbed* their way to even greater success with an excellent re-design. And the improvement they achieved is as plain as *night* and day.

This team impressed the judges with a unique climbing feature. You might try to tell them otherwise, but they’ll never *fall* for it. With this team, as the judges never tire of saying, *X marks the spot*.

*Rebounding* from the pandemic, this team *ultimately ascended* to *assist* other teams in *recycling* their parts. With a *stronghold* in the community, this team *Steamed* ahead to *Power up* teams and free up *deep space*, *recharging* before their next season. It's time to leave the Danger Zone so Pack up your parts. The Judges are pleased to present the Recycle Rush Award to:

This team’s robust design was able to take a beating and *claw* it’s way up to the traversal rung. Their *polished* workmanship *purr*fectly ensured that they always land on their feet. This *fur*midable feline’s design is *paws*itively *purr*fect.

This team had energy that was bubbling through the roof, and led the pack when it came to showing everyone just who they were. They symbolized what it means to be a supportive alliance you could rely on, yet also a beast to contend with. But most importantly, this team embodies the true spirit of engineering, wielding science and knowledge as an instrument to positively impact those around them.

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: This team impressed the judges with their adaptability and determination to overcome all obstacles. Sprawling spaces to cover? Make your own transportation. Covid Impact? Just call to action and adaptation. Creative curriculum coupled with community cooperation keeps this team at the forefront of FIRST. Congratulations A-05 Annex!

This team does an outstanding job at spreading interest throughout their community and school. You know this team by their performance and supportive fans. They own the room when they waltz in. The core values of FIRST are always on their mind during and in the off season, and towards the end of fall when *WINTER IS COMING* the team prepares to meet with other team to exchange knowledge, ideas, and data to even the playing field.

This team of the night has a clear concept of building a team and working as a cohesive system. From Organizational structure, to marketing and finances, these pups mean BUSINESS. Here to take home this year's award celebrating a true entrepreneurial spirit...
Their reach goes beyond their school moving into their community. Their Gracious Professionalism both on and off the field is no secret. Want to know why they won this award? Sorry its CLASSIFIED!!!

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: CnC'd sheet metal is nothing new. Fold it up, and from the first try, it works perfectly, is NEO. Congratulations to the NeoBots!

This team impressed the judges with their innovative control system. They say you should work smarter, not harder, and one of the smartest ways to work is to have a robot do it for you. An extensive and comprehensive autonomous control helps this team get those sweet double points and stay on top while they sit back and watch. To their talented Robot Casey and the team

The Judges liked this team for their careful attention to assembly detail. Well done riveting, conduited cables, and attractive layouts make this a beautiful robot. It's clear this team isn't horsing around
This team is always easy to find on and and off the playing field due to their flashy attire. They climbed to the lights to achieve their goals. These Vikings made their Balder Proud!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team turned being a little crooked and a bit off center to their advantage. Their strobile intake was a genius alternative to complete their intake circuit. Nothing broken here! Congratulations to 4513 Circuit Breakers!

Big dreams are no longer under wraps, though quarantine and COVID gave traditions the taps. No COVID pity party here, meal deliveries and 4x4 were clear. This team transforms culture both far and near. Congrats Team Confidential!

This award caused a dust up in the judges room! The team we selected had a strong presence in their community, and early set them themselves apart by working hard to sprout a new generation of robotics. Every member of this team seemed so well attuned to their fully custom machine it was almost like they were…cyborgs. Congrats 4061!

This team had a great business plan and delicious mascots the judges loved. Like a mori awase, they diversified their funding streams by creating their own brand. They embodied the entrepreneurship spirit of being committed to the grind, while balancing hard work with self care and support for all their members. This team is as sweet as ginger and strong as wasabi! Congrats, Sushi Squad!

When it came to being graciously professional, this team is a model by collaborating with other schools and cheering for all. Tapping their schillings to help others with parts, they impressed the judges with their lineage. The judges were royally impressed with this team! Congrats, Royal Robotics.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: When it comes to industrial design, this team was able to climb its way to the top. This team clearly had no horsing around when they were ironing out their design. We would like congratulate the Iron Mustangs!

Deep in the night, the robot was seen clearly in the dark. The talons were narrow and the holes were shallow. Lightning struck the metal to strengthen the structure. The Stormbots clearly won this award! Congrats team 2811, Stormbots!

These rookies may be young in name but their goal to inspire in STEM remains the same. Though COVID was not smooth sailing, partnerships and strong organization were key to their fame. Congrats, Team Classified!

Your team spirit has climbed to the highest bar. Displaying your exciting enthusiasm- we are nuts for your too-too cute tutus! Your collaborative efforts make us want to grab our Pom poms and cheer beside you. Keep up the enthusiasm! Congrats, Sonic Squirrels!

Execution in Autonomous Period is always a nail BITEr. This team demonstrated that they have consistent execution during this period on the field. They used further autonomy to find metal to take them to the next level every TIME

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: This team spun its away to the top of the crowd. Their creative focus on bar traversal was quite a ride. With a spinning Ferris wheel of clamps, the rotating hexagon design allowed them to achieve their goal of being a steady climber.

They are a multi-school team that created and defined their own name that incorporated their values. 40 is their lucky number in 2022, as they have a 40% increase in sponsorship by engaging family and friends as well as current membership that is 40% female. They have OWNed and overcome various challenges.

This team has delivered a one-two punch to the competition. Their extensive design process led to an elegantly engineered craft that weathers the seas of this challenge. This team deserves to ride the WAVE to success.

This team knows what it takes to spread FIRST values within their community. They inspired the formation of another team and ensured that the team had everything that they needed, for the entire season, from funding to parts. Their black and blue shirt should be a welcome sight for any team in need, showing that a you don’t need to be a veteran team to show kindness to others.

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: Mystery and Intrigue surround the sleek yet shadowy design of this team’s aura. You may be memorized by their elegant simplicity, effective shooting and climbing or their dark, secretive pit area. However, they prefer to remain incognito.

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: This team worked to a develop a machine that ensured all details were planned out. They showed how spending the time to design can make your robot royalty. Industrial design is about how the entire design work together and how the design process drives this integration. Laying out where and how every wire is run gives this bot a professional look.

This team showed COMPREHENSIVE Control of their robot with a delux driver control panel. By combining a ball tracking screen and shot tracking with a collection of “Easy” buttons, they could not fail.

This team has been a standout in multiple categories. Their attention to detail and Continuous Improvement activities would impress even the most Lean companies. They have even applied these concepts to standardizing and sustaining their STEM activities.
This team’s Quality is clear. Their welds could not be melted by the fiery forge of competition nor could forceful impacts shake their wires loose. It is in their DNA.

This team’s flight departs just before night. Pandemic-suspended season?...Not for this team. Instead, this team hosted dozens of virtual seminars and a chat to help new teams prepare for the big show. This team WIRES the world by crossing international borders.

This team makes other teams GREEN with envy. Although, their amazing outreach PAINTS, a pretty picture, they’ve canvassed their entire community with STEM. Sometimes it can get messy, but they make it art.

Despite being new, this team leaves the impression of being a veteran. Their meticulous documentation of team growth and CAD development along with their planning for further outreach will allow them to LEAD THE CHARGE in the years to come. If you haven’t met them, just look for the knights in shining armor.

This team is very energized for the future and outreach is the name of their game. With FLL programs in place and local community events lined up, there is no stopping this powerhouse of a team. This team is WIRED for success and is doing everything they can to keep the FIRST current flowing in their community.

Energy fluttered around every member of this team, both on and off the field. Their energy overflows into community outreach, enticing younger recruits from a variety of sources including a Brat Fry. From their freshly hatched FLL team on up, these birds kept their fledglings SAFE and INVOLVED!

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors

records.script: 这是一支强调综合能力全面发展的队伍， 为了团队的多样化， 他（她）们专设了女生工作坊活动，为了培养新人，他们搭建了入门训练备机。团队的新老交替可持续良性发展建设， 使得他们屡获殊荣！ 今年他们的团队和他们的机器人有着多方面优异的表现，但是更加脱颖而出和稳定可靠的是他们的自动程序表现， 恭喜6941， 上海平和机器人社获得自动程序奖 ！

records.awardName: Creativity Award sponsored by Rockwell Automation
records.script: 这是一支来自广东，充满活力的队伍，他们在传承中锐意进取，创新地应用坐标系矩阵算法解决了转向纠正系统难题，展现出了独特的创新能力，本次最佳创意奖授予5516深圳中加国际学校参赛队。
他们是一只充满活力的队伍，每位队员都清晰地知道比赛的目标和学习的价值， 用队伍发展展示墙、一对一老带新等方法，保持队伍的传承和发展，他们极具科学管理的精神，把每一分经费都花的井井有条，在展示过程中如同企业分工一样完美，恭喜来自上海的6353队，获得企业家精神奖。
这是一支快速成长中的队伍，拥有完善的组织架构和明确的分工合作。 在机器人的设计制作过程中，他们善于总结经验， 归纳和整理制作过程中碰到的问题，不断改进，并将他们设计的吸球和爬升装置申请了两项专利。 他们的机器精良， 稳定可靠， 源于从设计到制作以结果为导向的不懈努力。 他们是来自广州的8011！ 他们获得了卓越工程奖！

他们来自华东地区，满怀着学习新科技的热情和对未来理想的追求，投身到机器人研制的事业中。这群年轻人的技术精湛，精益求精，无论CAD设计和机床操作样样都行，他们帮助四十多个小学建立起机器人社团，还倾力辅助周边地区学校建立起多支FRC队伍。他们是一群了不起的年轻人，他们在校园里建设起“体验中心”，接待过一万多人参观机器人演示并接受STEM培训，他们实力非凡，赢得了FRC南太平洋赛区比赛的冠军，曾经两次荣获FRC主席奖，他们像雏鹰一样时刻准备展翅飞翔。本次最佳风尚奖授予江苏省镇江高级职业学校的6304团队！

records.awardName: Imagery Award in honor of Jack Kamen
records.script: 他们队伍人数不多，单个队员承担的任务较其他队伍要更多；他们没有专业指导老师，在机器工程方面，遇到问题，都是通过上网独自查找资料解决，有较强的自我学习、团队协同解决问题的能力；在团队文化方面，队徽设计结合江西文化元素，设计形象且极具特色；在学校社区活动方面，他们支持 FIRST 核心价值观的原则，在学校成立了社团，并组织纳新，积极宣传FIRST的理念。他们是来自江西的一支新队伍，也是江西省第一支FRC队伍，他们的队号是8809。

records.awardName: Industrial Design Award sponsored by General Motors
records.script: 这是一支来自上海，战绩骄人的队伍，他们采用工业设计原则，设计了实用高效的的机器人，展现出了优秀的设计能力，本次工业设计奖授予7522上海造个机器人俱乐部参赛队。
作为一支新的队伍，他们不仅展示了自身优秀的技术特质，而且在FIRST技术领域展现了非凡的品质，特别在控制概念和执行方面有新颖独特的创新。他们在机器控制系统中，增加了超声波检测和四轮独特转向的方法，使得在人机配合协调策略中能发挥较好控制水平，恭喜8172获得控制创新奖。

这只队伍综合实力非常优秀，在各个奖项中他们多次被提名；在机器设计方面，他们采用模块化设计思路，设计完成度很高，轻量化的创意射球结构、一套完整高效的软件控制算法，给评委留下了深刻得印象；在学校社区活动方面，他们在学校创办社团MAKERs’开发者根据地，向同学们传授在参加 FRC时学习的 3D 建模、3D 打印、电焊、材料加工、编程等知识，传播 FRC 竞技精神；他们是来自深圳的一支联队，他们的队号是8214。
他们的机器从设计上具备工程思维，考虑设计材料的选型，加工工艺、安全冗余性、装配维护的便捷性，保障了机器的坚固稳定；设计的爬升机构，采用双臂多段升降机构，确保爬升的高效与稳定性；在其他结构设计上考虑防呆和限位设计，极大保证了机器运行的安全性；在学校社区活动方面，团队在校内组织FRC的的各种宣讲活动，宣传和推广FIRST的理念。他们是来自深圳的队伍，他们的队号是7146。

这是一支来自华东地区的队伍，他们的团队超过了300人，他们积极进取、勇于创新，善于拓展。这个团队技术水平优秀，参加过FRC 2018、2019、2021赛季的比赛，并且获得了优异的成绩，荣获多个大奖。他们不断地通过各种方式和渠道宣传、弘扬First精神，他们不仅主动关心帮助其他地区的队伍，编制并分享专门的教程，还设立运营管理部在校内外开展形式多样的宣教工作。他们广泛地与国内外著名厂商进行合作，用丰富多彩的活动传播科创精神，他们赢得得了同学、社区、企业的高度评价，被当地政府评选为三星级学生科技社团。本次工程启发奖授予上海复旦附中的6907团队！

这个团队来自上海，刚刚成立一年，虽然平均年龄很小，但是他们是一群令人惊叹的年轻人，怀着对未知世界的探索精神，勇于开拓，努力地去创造无限的可能性。在过去的一年里，他们克服疫情肆虐的影响，不仅建设起了专用的训练场地，还通过向兄弟团队请教学习，自主搭建完成比赛机器人。更令人惊叹的是，他们通过各种方式走向社会，在波音（中国）、上海华为、新石器等多个著名公司开展路演，近乎完美的机器人表演赢得企业高度的赞誉，获得大量经济及技术方面的支持，他们是如此出众，中央电视台CCTV14专门录制并播出了关于他们的节目。这群年轻人是FRC舞台上正在冉冉升起的新星。本次新秀全明星奖授予上海中学生联队 8814团队！
他们是一支年轻有张力，敢打敢拼的团队，他们紧跟科技时代的脚步，直播招新；他们通过公众号、期刊杂志等将工程技术和工程师的理念广而告之。在疫情时代下，为了满足大家线下赛的渴望，他们说服了学校承办了比赛。他们是来自东莞清澜山学校的8857队伍。恭喜他们获得2022年FRC新秀启发奖！
他们是一支老牌劲旅，他们充满激情与活力，传帮带的作用在这支队伍中体现得淋漓尽致，他们沉淀下来的精神力量已经根深蒂固，分享、交流、创新、拼搏影响着每一位新加入的成员，我们为这样的团队而骄傲自豪，获得“团队精神奖”的队伍是：7047河南省实验中学。

scope: official team judged award results, with citations when FIRST publishes them
